children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> (Entering the Path of Awakening) composed by <s>Śāntideva</s>.
Om, homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.
Chapter One, entitled 'The Benefits of <s>Bodhicitta</s> (the Awakening Mind).'
Having reverently bowed to the <s>Sugatas</s> (the Well-Gone Ones), together with their sons and the body of the <s>Dharma</s>, and to all who are worthy of veneration,
I shall briefly describe, in accordance with scripture, the entrance into the discipline of the sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>. [1.1]

children.text: na hi kiṃcidapūrvamatra vācyaṃ na ca saṃgrathanakauśalaṃ mamāsti /
children.translated_text: Nothing new is to be said here, nor do I possess any skill in composition.

children.text: ata eva na me parārthacintā svamano vāsayituṃ kṛtaṃ mayedam // SBca_1.2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, I have no thought for the benefit of others; I have composed this to cultivate my own mind. [1.2]

children.text: mama tāvadanena yāti vṛddhiṃ kuśalaṃ bhāvayituṃ prasādavegaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, the surge of faith in me, at least, grows for the cultivation of virtue.

children.text: atha matsamadhātureva paśyed aparo 'pyenamato 'pi sārthako 'yam // SBca_1.3 //
children.translated_text: And if another of the same disposition as mine should see this, then it too would be meaningful. [1.3]
This fortunate moment, so difficult to obtain, which is the means of accomplishing the goal of human life, has been attained.

children.text: yadi nātra vicintyate hitaṃ punarapyeṣa samāgamaḥ kutaḥ // SBca_1.4 //
children.translated_text: If one does not contemplate what is beneficial here, how will this conjunction come again? [1.4]

children.text: rātrau yathā meghaghanāndhakāre vidyut kṣaṇaṃ darśayati prakāśam /
children.translated_text: Just as on a dark night, thick with clouds, lightning for an instant reveals the light,

children.text: buddhānubhāvena tathā kadācil lokasya puṇyeṣu matiḥ kṣaṇaṃ syāt // SBca_1.5 //
children.translated_text: so too, by the power of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the mind of the world may for an instant turn toward merit. [1.5]

children.text: tasmācchubhaṃ durbalameva nityaṃ balaṃ tu pāpasya mahatsughoram /
children.translated_text: Therefore, virtue is always feeble, while the power of evil is great and exceedingly terrible.

children.text: tajjīyate 'nyena śubhena kena saṃbodhicittaṃ yadi nāma na syāt // SBca_1.6 //
children.translated_text: By what other virtue could it be overcome, if <s>Bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind) were not to arise? [1.6]
The lords of sages, contemplating for countless <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), have seen this very thing to be beneficial,

children.text: yataḥ sukhenaiva sukhaṃ pravṛddham utplāvayatyapramitāñjanaughān // SBca_1.7 //
children.translated_text: for by it, happiness swelling easily from happiness carries away immeasurable multitudes of beings. [1.7]
By those who wish to cross over the hundreds of sufferings of existence, by those who wish to remove the afflictions of beings,

children.text: bahusaukhyaśatāni bhoktukāmair na vimocyaṃ hi sadaiva bodhicittam // SBca_1.8 //
children.translated_text: by those who wish to enjoy hundreds of joys — <s>Bodhicitta</s> should never be abandoned. [1.8]

children.text: bhavacārakabandhano varākaḥ sugatānāṃ suta ucyate kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: The wretched one, bound in the prison of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), is in an instant called a son of the <s>Sugatas</s>,

children.text: sanarāmaralokavandanīyo bhavati smodita eva bodhicitte // SBca_1.9 //
children.translated_text: and becomes worthy of veneration by the worlds of gods and humans, when <s>Bodhicitta</s> has arisen. [1.9]
Taking this impure image, it makes it into the priceless image of a <s>Jina</s> (Victor) jewel.

children.text: rasajātamatīva vedhanīyaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ gṛhṇata bodhicittasaṃjñam // SBca_1.10 //
children.translated_text: Hold firmly to that which is called <s>Bodhicitta</s>, which is like the supremely transformative elixir of the alchemists. [1.10]
Well-examined by those of immeasurable wisdom, the sole caravan-leaders of the world, it is of great value.
You who are accustomed to wandering in the stations of the lower realms, hold firmly to the jewel of <s>Bodhicitta</s>! [1.11]

children.text: kadalīva phalaṃ vihāya yāti kṣayamanyat kuśalaṃ hi sarvameva /
children.translated_text: Like the plantain tree, which perishes after bearing fruit, all other virtue goes to exhaustion.

children.text: satataṃ phalati kṣayaṃ na yāti prasavatyeva tu bodhicittavṛkṣaḥ // SBca_1.12 //
children.translated_text: But the tree of <s>Bodhicitta</s> bears fruit perpetually, does not go to exhaustion, and only continues to grow. [1.12]
Even having committed terrible sins, one crosses over in an instant by taking refuge in it,
as one crosses great dangers by taking refuge in a hero. Why is it not taken up by ignorant beings? [1.13]
Like the fire at the end of an age, it burns up great sins in an instant.
Its immeasurable benefits were proclaimed by the wise Lord <s>Maitreya</s> to <s>Sudhana</s>. [1.14]
That <s>Bodhicitta</s> should be known, in brief, as twofold:
<s>Bodhipraṇidhicitta</s> (the mind of aspiration for awakening) and <s>Bodhiprasthāna</s> (the actual setting forth toward awakening). [1.15]
Just as the distinction between one who wishes to go and one who is actually going is understood,
so the distinction between these two should be known by the wise, in that very order. [1.16]
The <s>Bodhipraṇidhicitta</s> (aspiration mind) bears great fruit even in <s>saṃsāra</s>,
but it does not have the uninterrupted flow of merit that belongs to the mind that has actually set forth. [1.17]
From the moment when one takes up that mind with an irreversible resolve
for the liberation of the boundless realm of beings, [1.18]
from that moment, even for one who is asleep or heedless,
uninterrupted streams of merit flow forth, equal to the sky. [1.19]
This was stated with reasoning by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself
in the <s>Subāhupṛcchā</s>, for the sake of beings of lesser aspiration. [1.20]
One who thinks 'I shall destroy the headaches of beings'

children.text: aprameyeṇa puṇyena gṛhyate sma hitāśayaḥ // SBca_1.21 //
children.translated_text: is endowed with a beneficent intention and is seized by immeasurable merit. [1.21]
How much more so one who wishes to remove the incomparable suffering of each and every being,
and who wishes to bestow immeasurable virtue upon each and every being! [1.22]
What mother or father has such a desire for the welfare of others?

children.text: devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ vā brahmaṇāṃ vā bhaviṣyati // SBca_1.23 //
children.translated_text: Will it be found among the gods, the sages, or <s>Brahmā</s>? [1.23]
Even for those very beings themselves, such a wish for their own welfare

children.text: notpannapūrvaḥ svapne 'pi parārthe saṃbhavaḥ kutaḥ // SBca_1.24 //
children.translated_text: has never arisen before, not even in a dream — how then could it arise for the sake of others? [1.24]
How does this extraordinary jewel among beings arise,
this desire for the welfare of others that does not arise in others even for their own sake? [1.25]
Of this jewel of the mind, the seed of the world's joy and the medicine for the world's suffering,

children.text: cittaratnasya yatpuṇyaṃ tatkathaṃ hi pramīyatām // SBca_1.26 //
children.translated_text: how can its merit be measured? [1.26]
The worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> is surpassed by the mere wish for the welfare of others.
How much more so by striving for the complete happiness of all beings! [1.27]
Those who desire to escape from suffering rush toward suffering itself.

children.text: sukhecchayaiva saṃmohāt svasukhaṃ ghnanti śatruvat // SBca_1.28 //
children.translated_text: Out of the very desire for happiness, through delusion, they destroy their own happiness as if it were an enemy. [1.28]
One who would satisfy with all happinesses those who are starved of happiness and afflicted in many ways,

children.text: tṛptiṃ sarvasukhaiḥ kuryātsarvāḥ pīḍāśchinatti ca // SBca_1.29 //
children.translated_text: and who would cut off all their afflictions — [1.29]
and who would destroy their delusion — where is a saint equal to such a one?

children.text: kuto vā tādṛśaṃ mitraṃ puṇyaṃ vā tādṛśaṃ kutaḥ // SBca_1.30 //
children.translated_text: Where is such a friend, and where is such merit? [1.30]
Even one who repays a kindness done to him is praised to that extent.
What then shall be said of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who does good unsolicited? [1.31]
One who gives a meal to a few beings is honored by people as a doer of good —
for a contemptible gift of mere morsels of food, enough for only half a day's sustenance. [1.32]
How much more so one who gives to an unlimited number of beings, for an unlimited time,
the inexhaustible fulfillment of all desires, lasting until the end of beings as numerous as the sky! [1.33]

children.text: iti sattrapatau jinasya putre kaluṣaṃ sve hṛdaye karoti yaśca /
children.translated_text: One who harbors ill-will in his heart toward such a lord of generosity, a son of the <s>Jina</s> —

children.text: kaluṣodayasaṃkhyayā sa kalpān narakeṣvāvasatīti nātha āha // SBca_1.34 //
children.translated_text: the Protector has said that such a one dwells in the hells for as many <s>kalpas</s> as the number of his moments of ill-will. [1.34]

children.text: atha yasya manaḥ prasādameti prasavettasya tato 'dhikaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: But one whose mind attains faith toward them — the fruit of that is even greater.

children.text: mahatā hi balena pāpakaṃ jinaputreṣu śubhaṃ tvayatnataḥ // SBca_1.35 //
children.translated_text: For in the case of the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, evil requires great force, while good arises effortlessly. [1.35]
I bow to the bodies of those in whom that precious jewel of the supreme mind has arisen.

children.text: yatrāpakāro 'pi sukhānubandhī sukhākarāṃstān śaraṇaṃ prayāmi // SBca_1.36 //
children.translated_text: Even offense toward them leads to happiness — I go for refuge to those sources of bliss. [1.36]

children.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ bodhicittānuśaṃsāvivaraṇaṃ nāma prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, the exposition of the benefits of <s>Bodhicitta</s>, in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.
Chapter Two, entitled '<s>Pāpadeśanā</s> (The Confession of Sins).'
In order to properly seize that jewel of the mind, I offer worship to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

children.text: saddharmaratnasya ca nirmalasya buddhātmajānāṃ ca guṇodadhīnām // SBca_2.1 //
children.translated_text: to the stainless jewel of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and to the sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, who are oceans of virtue. [2.1]

children.text: yāvanti puṣpāṇi phalāni caiva bhaiṣajyajātāni ca yāni santi /
children.translated_text: Whatever flowers and fruits there are, and whatever kinds of medicines exist,

children.text: ratnāni yāvanti ca santi loke jalāni ca svacchamanoramāṇi // SBca_2.2 //
children.translated_text: whatever jewels there are in the world, and whatever clear and delightful waters — [2.2]
mountains made of jewels, and forest regions delightful in their solitude,

children.text: latāḥ sapuṣpābharaṇojjvalāśca drumāśca ye satphalanamraśākhāḥ // SBca_2.3 //
children.translated_text: creepers radiant with their ornaments of flowers, and trees with branches bending under good fruit — [2.3]

children.text: devādilokeṣu ca gandhadhūpāḥ kalpadrumā ratnamayāśca vṛkṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: fragrant incenses from the worlds of gods and others, wish-fulfilling trees and jewel-trees,
lakes adorned with lotuses, enchanting with the calls of geese — [2.4]

children.text: akṛṣṭajātāni ca śasyajātāny anyāni vā pūjyavibhūṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: crops growing without cultivation, and other ornaments worthy of offering,
all of these, extending to the limits of the expanse of space, and without an owner — [2.5]
taking these in thought, I offer them to the bulls among sages, together with their sons.

children.text: gṛhṇantu tanme varadakṣiṇīyā mahākṛpā māmanukampamānāḥ // SBca_2.6 //
children.translated_text: May those supreme recipients of gifts, out of great compassion, accept these from me, showing me favor! [2.6]
I am without merit, utterly destitute; I have nothing else for the purpose of worship.

children.text: ato mamārthāya parārthacittā gṛhṇantu nāthā idamātmaśaktyā // SBca_2.7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, for my sake, may the protectors, whose minds are set on the welfare of others, accept this by their own power! [2.7]

children.text: dadāmi cātmānamahaṃ jinebhyaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ ca tadātmajebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: I give myself entirely to the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), and all that I have to their sons.

children.text: parigrahaṃ me kurutāgrasattvā yuṣmāsu dāsatvamupaimi bhaktyā // SBca_2.8 //
children.translated_text: Accept me, O supreme beings! With devotion I enter into servitude to you. [2.8]
Having been accepted by you, I become fearless in existence and work for the welfare of beings.

children.text: pūrvaṃ ca pāpaṃ samatikramāmi nānyacca pāpaṃ prakaromi bhūyaḥ // SBca_2.9 //
children.translated_text: I transcend my former sins, and I shall commit no other sins henceforth. [2.9]
In those bathing chambers, fragrant, with pillars radiant with jewels,
with canopies gleaming with pearls, on floors of shining, bright crystal — [2.10]
with many great pitchers made of precious gems, filled with fragrant water and flowers,

children.text: snānaṃ karomyeṣa tathāgatānāṃ tadātmajānāṃ ca sagītivādyam // SBca_2.11 //
children.translated_text: I bathe the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and their sons, with song and music. [2.11]
With incomparable, fragrant, well-scented cloths, I dry their bodies,

children.text: tataḥ suraktāni sudhūpitāni dadāmi tebhyo varacīvarāṇi // SBca_2.12 //
children.translated_text: and then I offer them excellent robes, well-dyed and well-perfumed. [2.12]
With divine garments, soft, fine, of wondrous beauty,
and with the finest ornaments, I adorn <s>Samantabhadra</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, <s>Lokeśvara</s>, and others. [2.13]
With the finest fragrances, spreading throughout the entire three-thousand-fold universe,
I anoint the bodies of all the lords of sages, blazing with the splendor of well-smelted, polished, purified gold. [2.14]
With <s>māndāra</s> flowers, blue lotuses, jasmine, and all other fragrant and delightful blossoms,
I worship the most worship-worthy lords of sages, and with garlands beautifully arranged. [2.15]
With clouds of incense, richly fragrant and delightful, I perfume them,

children.text: bhojyaiśca khādyairvividhaiśca peyais tebhyo nivedyaṃ ca nivedayāmi // SBca_2.16 //
children.translated_text: and I present offerings to them of various foods, drinks, and sweets. [2.16]
I offer jewel-lamps, arranged in rows upon golden lotuses,

children.text: gandhopalipteṣu ca kuṭṭimeṣu kirāmi puṣpaprakarān manojñān // SBca_2.17 //
children.translated_text: and upon the fragrance-anointed floors, I scatter delightful heaps of flowers. [2.17]
Those palaces in the sky, beautiful with hanging strings of pearls and gems, luminous, adorning the quarters of space,
delightful with hymns and songs of praise — I offer them also to those who are the embodiment of loving-kindness. [2.18]
With golden handles of beautiful form, upraised, studded with pearls,
I hold aloft for the great sages jeweled parasols of surpassing beauty. [2.19]
Henceforth, may delightful clouds of offerings arise,
and clouds of musical instruments and songs, bringing joy to all beings! [2.20]
Upon all the jewels of the true <s>Dharma</s>, upon the <s>caityas</s> (shrines) and images,
may rains of flowers, jewels, and the like fall without ceasing! [2.21]
Just as <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> and others worship the <s>Jinas</s>,
so do I worship the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the protectors, together with their sons. [2.22]
With hymns that are oceans of melodious voices, I praise these oceans of virtue.
May clouds of hymns and songs of praise arise for them, without fail! [2.23]
With prostrations as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields,
I bow to all the <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times, together with the <s>Dharma</s> and the supreme <s>Saṃgha</s>. [2.24]
I venerate all <s>caityas</s> and the abodes of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;
I pay homage to the teachers and to the venerable ascetics as well. [2.25]
I go to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge, until the seat of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening);

children.text: dharmaṃ gacchāmi śaraṇaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ tathā // SBca_2.26 //
children.translated_text: I go to the <s>Dharma</s> for refuge, and likewise to the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. [2.26]
With joined palms, I inform the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> established in all directions,
and the greatly compassionate <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as well. // SBca_2.27 //
In <s>saṃsāra</s> without beginning, whether in this birth or in another,

children.text: yanmayā paśunā pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ kāritameva vā // SBca_2.28 //
children.translated_text: whatever evil has been done or caused to be done by me, a brute, // SBca_2.28 //
and whatever I have foolishly rejoiced in, to my own destruction —
that transgression I confess, tormented by remorse. // SBca_2.29 //
Whatever offense against the Three Jewels, or against my mother and father,

children.text: guruṣvanyeṣu vā kṣepāt kāyavāgbuddhibhiḥ kṛtaḥ // SBca_2.30 //
children.translated_text: or against my teachers and others, committed through contempt by body, speech, and mind — // SBca_2.30 //
whatever terrible evil has been done by me, a sinner, defiled by numerous faults —

children.text: yatkṛtaṃ dāruṇaṃ pāpaṃ tatsarvaṃ deśayāmyaham // SBca_2.31 //
children.translated_text: all that I confess, O Leaders! // SBca_2.31 //
And how shall I escape from this? I am constantly anxious, O Leaders!
May death not come to me soon, while my heap of evil is not exhausted! // SBca_2.32 //
And how shall I escape from this? Rescue me quickly!
May death not come swiftly to me whose evil is not exhausted! // SBca_2.33 //
This death, which does not examine what is done and undone, is a treacherous slayer,
not to be trusted by the healthy or the sick — a sudden great thunderbolt. // SBca_2.34 //
For the sake of the dear and the unpleasant, evil has been done in many ways;
that all must be abandoned when one departs — this was not understood. // SBca_2.35 //

children.text: apriyā na bhaviṣyanti priyo me na bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: The unpleasant will no longer exist; my beloved will no longer exist;

children.text: ahaṃ ca na bhaviṣyāmi sarvaṃ ca na bhaviṣyati // SBca_2.36 //
children.translated_text: I myself will no longer exist; and nothing at all will exist. // SBca_2.36 //
Whatever thing is experienced becomes merely a memory;
like something experienced in a dream, all has gone and is never seen again. // SBca_2.37 //
Even while standing right here, many dear and unpleasant [persons] have departed;

children.text: tannimittaṃ tu yatpāpaṃ tatsthitaṃ ghoramagrataḥ // SBca_2.38 //
children.translated_text: but the terrible evil done on their account remains before me. // SBca_2.38 //
Thus 'I am a transient visitor' — this was not reflected upon by me;
through delusion, attachment, and hatred, evil has been done in many ways. // SBca_2.39 //
Night and day, without pause, the spending of life increases;

children.text: āyasya cāgamo nāsti na mariṣyāmi kiṃ nvaham // SBca_2.40 //
children.translated_text: and there is no replenishment of what is spent — shall I not surely die? // SBca_2.40 //
Even while lying in bed, even while standing among relatives,
the pain of having one's vital parts cut must be endured by me alone. // SBca_2.41 //
When seized by the messengers of <s>Yama</s>, where is a relative? Where is a friend?

children.text: puṇyamekaṃ tadā trāṇaṃ mayā tacca na sevitam // SBca_2.42 //
children.translated_text: Merit alone is the refuge at that time, and that I have not cultivated. // SBca_2.42 //
Clinging to this impermanent life, not knowing this danger,

children.text: pramattena mayā nāthā bahu pāpamupārjitam // SBca_2.43 //
children.translated_text: much evil has been accumulated by me, heedless, O Protectors! // SBca_2.43 //
Even one being led away today for the amputation of a limb withers;
parched with thirst, with piteous eyes, he sees the world as something entirely other. // SBca_2.44 //
How much more when one is overcome by the terrifying forms of <s>Yama's</s> messengers,
seized by the great fever of terror, smeared with one's own excrement! // SBca_2.45 //
With fearful glances, seeking refuge in the four directions,
'Who will be my good refuge from this great fear?' // SBca_2.46 //
Seeing the directions devoid of refuge, falling again into bewilderment —

children.text: tadāhaṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmi tasmin sthāne mahābhaye // SBca_2.47 //
children.translated_text: then what shall I do, in that place of great fear? // SBca_2.47 //
Today itself I take refuge in the Lords of the World, the greatly powerful,
the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), who are devoted to protecting the world and who remove all terrors, // SBca_2.48 //
and in the <s>Dharma</s> realized by them, which destroys the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: śaraṇaṃ yāmi bhāvena bodhisattvagaṇaṃ tathā // SBca_2.49 //
children.translated_text: I take refuge with devotion likewise in the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // SBca_2.49 //
Trembling with fear, I give myself to <s>Samantabhadra</s>,
and again to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> I give myself of my own accord. // SBca_2.50 //
And to that lord <s>Avalokita</s>, who moves about with compassionate distress —

children.text: viraumyārtaravaṃ bhītaḥ sa māṃ rakṣatu pāpinam // SBca_2.51 //
children.translated_text: terrified, I cry out a desperate cry: may he protect me, a sinner! // SBca_2.51 //
To the noble <s>Ākāśagarbha</s> and to <s>Kṣitigarbha</s>, with devotion,
and to all the greatly compassionate ones — seeking refuge, I cry out! // SBca_2.52 //

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva ca saṃtrastāḥ palāyante caturdiśam /
children.translated_text: And to the Thunderbolt-bearer (<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>), upon seeing whom alone
the wicked <s>Yama</s>-messengers and others flee in terror to the four directions — to him I pay homage. // SBca_2.53 //
Having transgressed your word before, now at the sight of danger,

children.text: śaraṇaṃ yāmi vo bhīto bhayaṃ nāśayata drutam // SBca_2.54 //
children.translated_text: I come to you for refuge, terrified — destroy my fear swiftly! // SBca_2.54 //
Even one frightened by a passing illness would not disregard a physician's word;
how much less one afflicted by the four hundred and four diseases! // SBca_2.55 //
Since by even one [disease], all the people dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>

children.text: naśyanti yeṣāṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ sarvadikṣu na labhyate // SBca_2.56 //
children.translated_text: can be destroyed, and no medicine for them is found in any direction — // SBca_2.56 //
the word of the all-knowing Physician, who removes all thorns [of suffering],
I would disregard? — shame on me, utterly deluded! // SBca_2.57 //
Even at lesser precipices I stand most attentively;
how much more at the precipice a thousand leagues deep, lasting for ages! // SBca_2.58 //

children.text: adyaiva maraṇaṃ naiti na yuktā me sukhāsikā /
children.translated_text: Death will not come today alone — it is not fitting for me to sit at ease;

children.text: avaśyameti sā velā na bhaviṣyāmyahaṃ yadā // SBca_2.59 //
children.translated_text: that time will surely come when I shall no longer exist. // SBca_2.59 //

children.text: abhayaṃ kena me dattaṃ niḥsariṣyāmi vā katham /
children.translated_text: By whom has fearlessness been given to me? And how shall I escape?

children.text: avaśyaṃ na bhaviṣyāmi kasmānme susthitaṃ manaḥ // SBca_2.60 //
children.translated_text: I will surely cease to exist — why then is my mind at ease? // SBca_2.60 //
From things previously experienced and now lost, what essence remains for me,

children.text: yeṣu me 'bhiniviṣṭena gurūṇāṃ laṅghitaṃ vacaḥ // SBca_2.61 //
children.translated_text: through attachment to which I have transgressed the words of my teachers? // SBca_2.61 //
Having left this world of the living and all familiar relatives,

children.text: ekākī kvāpi yāsyāmi kiṃ me sarvaiḥ priyāpriyaiḥ // SBca_2.62 //
children.translated_text: alone I shall go somewhere — what use to me are all things dear and unpleasant? // SBca_2.62 //

children.text: iyameva tu me cintā yuktā rātriṃdivaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: This alone should be my constant thought, day and night:

children.text: aśubhānniyataṃ duḥkhaṃ niḥsareyaṃ tataḥ katham // SBca_2.63 //
children.translated_text: from the unwholesome comes certain suffering — how shall I escape from it? // SBca_2.63 //
Whatever evil has been accumulated by me, a foolish and confused person,

children.text: prakṛtyā yacca sāvadyaṃ prajñaptyāvadyameva ca // SBca_2.64 //
children.translated_text: whether naturally blameworthy or blameworthy by designation — // SBca_2.64 //
all that I confess, standing here before the Protectors,
with joined palms, afraid of suffering, bowing again and again. // SBca_2.65 //
May the Leaders accept my transgression as transgression!

children.text: na bhadrakamidaṃ nāthā na kartavyaṃ punarmayā // SBca_2.66 //
children.translated_text: This is not good, O Protectors — it shall not be done again by me. // SBca_2.66 //

children.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ pāpadeśanā nāma dvitīyaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>, [this is] the second chapter, named 'The Confession of Evil.'
Chapter 3: The third chapter, named 'Embracing <s>Bodhicitta</s>' (the Mind of Awakening).
I rejoice with delight in the good done by all beings

children.text: anumode pramodena sukhaṃ tiṣṭhantu duḥkhitāḥ // SBca_3.1 //
children.translated_text: that brings respite from the sufferings of the evil destinies — may those who suffer dwell in happiness! // SBca_3.1 //
I rejoice in the liberation of embodied beings from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
I rejoice in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-hood and <s>buddhahood</s> of the Protectors. // SBca_3.2 //
I rejoice in the oceans of the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> by the Teachers,
which bring happiness to all beings and which establish the welfare of all beings. // SBca_3.3 //
With joined palms I beseech the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> in all directions:
may they kindle the lamp of <s>Dharma</s> for those who fall into suffering through delusion! // SBca_3.4 //
With joined palms I implore the <s>Jinas</s> who wish to pass into <s>nirvāṇa</s>:
may they remain for infinite <s>kalpas</s> — let not this world be blind! // SBca_3.5 //
Having thus done all this, whatever merit I have gathered,
by that may I become the one who pacifies all the sufferings of all beings! // SBca_3.6 //

children.text: glānānāmasmi bhaiṣajyaṃ bhaveyaṃ vaidya eva ca /
children.translated_text: May I be the medicine for the sick, may I be the physician as well,
and their attendant too, until the non-recurrence of disease! // SBca_3.7 //
May I destroy the affliction of hunger and thirst by showers of food and drink;
in the intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of famine, may I become drink and food! // SBca_3.8 //
For impoverished beings, may I be an inexhaustible treasure;
may I stand before them in the form of various requisites! // SBca_3.9 //
My bodies, my enjoyments, and all my merit of the three times —
I relinquish without attachment, for the accomplishment of the welfare of all beings. // SBca_3.10 //

children.text: sarvatyāgaśca nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇārthi ca me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The relinquishment of all is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and my mind aspires to <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: tyaktavyaṃ cenmayā sarvaṃ varaṃ sattveṣu dīyatām // SBca_3.11 //
children.translated_text: if all must be relinquished by me, better it be given to beings! // SBca_3.11 //
This self of mine I have given for the happiness of all embodied beings;

children.text: ghnantu nindantu vā nityamākirantu ca pāṃsubhiḥ // SBca_3.12 //
children.translated_text: let them strike me, revile me always, and shower me with dust! // SBca_3.12 //

children.text: krīḍantu mama kāyena hasantu vilasantu ca /
children.translated_text: Let them play with my body, let them laugh and make sport;

children.text: dattastebhyo mayā kāyaścintayā kiṃ mamānayā // SBca_3.13 //
children.translated_text: I have given my body to them — why should this [concern] be mine? // SBca_3.13 //

children.text: kārayantu ca karmāṇi yāni teṣāṃ sukhāvaham /
children.translated_text: Let them make me do whatever deeds bring them happiness;
may no harm ever come to anyone on my account! // SBca_3.14 //
For those whose mind toward me is angry or pleased,

children.text: teṣāṃ sa eva hetuḥ syānnityaṃ sarvārthasiddhaye // SBca_3.15 //
children.translated_text: may that itself always be the cause of the accomplishment of all their aims! // SBca_3.15 //

children.text: abhyākhyāsyanti māṃ ye ca ye cānye 'pyapakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who slander me, and those who do me harm,
and likewise those who mock me — may they all become sharers in awakening! // SBca_3.16 //
I am the protector of the unprotected, the caravan-leader of travelers,

children.text: pārepsūnāṃ ca naubhūtaḥ setuḥ saṃkrama eva ca // SBca_3.17 //
children.translated_text: the boat, the bridge, and the causeway for those who wish to cross! // SBca_3.17 //
I am the lamp for those who desire a lamp, the bed for those who desire a bed;
may I be the servant for those who desire a servant — for all embodied beings! // SBca_3.18 //
May I be the wish-fulfilling gem, the auspicious vessel, the perfected <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-spell), the great herb;
may I be the wish-fulfilling tree and the wish-granting cow for embodied beings! // SBca_3.19 //
Just as the great elements — earth and the rest — serve in various ways
the immeasurable beings dwelling throughout all of space, // SBca_3.20 //
so may I in various ways be the sustenance
of the realm of beings extending to the limits of space, until all are liberated! // SBca_3.21 //
Just as <s>bodhicitta</s> was generated by the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) of old,
and just as they were established step by step in the <s>bodhisattva</s> trainings, // SBca_3.22 //
so do I generate <s>bodhicitta</s> for the welfare of the world,

children.text: tadvadeva ca tāḥ śikṣāḥ śikṣiṣyāmi yathākramam // SBca_3.23 //
children.translated_text: and so shall I train in those very trainings in due order. // SBca_3.23 //
Having thus wisely grasped <s>bodhicitta</s> with clear faith,

children.text: punaḥ pṛṣṭasya puṣṭyarthaṃ cittamevaṃ praharṣayet // SBca_3.24 //
children.translated_text: one should, for the sake of nourishing it further, gladden the mind thus: // SBca_3.24 //

children.text: adya me saphalaṃ janma sulabdho mānuṣo bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Today my birth has become fruitful; the human existence has been well obtained.

children.text: adya buddhakule jāto buddhaputro 'smi sāṃpratam // SBca_3.25 //
children.translated_text: Today I am born in the family of the <s>Buddhas</s>; I am now a son of the <s>Buddha</s>! // SBca_3.25 //
Henceforth I must act as befits those who act in accordance with their family,

children.text: nirmalasya kulasyāsya kalaṅko na bhavedyathā // SBca_3.26 //
children.translated_text: so that no stain may come upon this pure family. // SBca_3.26 //
Just as a blind person might find a jewel in a heap of refuse,
so somehow this <s>bodhicitta</s> has arisen in me. // SBca_3.27 //
This elixir has been born for the destruction of the world's death;
this is the inexhaustible treasure that dispels the world's poverty. // SBca_3.28 //
This is the supreme medicine that allays the world's diseases;
it is the tree of rest for the world weary from wandering on the road of existence. // SBca_3.29 //
It is the universal bridge for all travelers crossing out of the evil destinies;
it is the risen mind-moon that cools the world's afflictions. // SBca_3.30 //
It is the great sun that dispels the darkness of the world's ignorance;
it is the fresh butter arisen from churning the milk of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // SBca_3.31 //
For the caravan of beings traveling the road of existence, hungering for the enjoyment of happiness,
this feast of joy has been prepared, sating all the beings who arrive! // SBca_3.32 //

children.text: jagadadya nimantritaṃ mayā sugatatvena sukhena cāntarā /
children.translated_text: Today I invite the world to <s>Sugata</s>-hood and to happiness in the interim;
before all the Protectors, may gods, <s>asuras</s>, and others rejoice! // SBca_3.33 //

children.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ bodhicittaparigraho nāma tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>, [this is] the third chapter, named 'Embracing <s>Bodhicitta</s>.'
Chapter 4: The fourth chapter, named 'Heedfulness regarding <s>Bodhicitta</s>.'
Having thus firmly grasped <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), a son of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones)
should always strive diligently, without laziness, not to transgress the trainings. [4.1]
That which is rashly undertaken, that which is not properly considered —

children.text: tatra kuryānna vetyevaṃ pratijñāyāpi yujyate // SBca_4.2 //
children.translated_text: even after making a vow, it is fitting [to reconsider] whether to do it or not. [4.2]
But that which has been examined by the <s>Buddhas</s> and their greatly wise sons,

children.text: mayāpi ca yathāśakti tatra kiṃ parilambyate // SBca_4.3 //
children.translated_text: and by me too according to my ability — why should there be any delay in that? [4.3]

children.text: yadi caivaṃ pratijñāya sādhayeyaṃ na karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: If, having vowed thus, I were not to accomplish it in deed,

children.text: etāṃ sarvāṃ visaṃvādya kā gatirme bhaviṣyati // SBca_4.4 //
children.translated_text: having deceived all these beings, what destiny would be mine? [4.4]
A person who, having merely thought of giving something in his mind, does not give it —
becomes a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), so it is said, even concerning the most trifling thing. [4.5]
How much more so, having loudly proclaimed the unsurpassed happiness with sincere intent,

children.text: jagatsarvaṃ visaṃvādya kā gatirme bhaviṣyati // SBca_4.6 //
children.translated_text: and then having deceived the entire world — what destiny would be mine? [4.6]
Only the Omniscient One knows this inconceivable course of <s>karma</s> (action),
by which he liberates even those people who abandon <s>bodhicitta</s>. [4.7]
Therefore, for a <s>bodhisattva</s>, every transgression is most grave,
since by falling he destroys the welfare of all sentient beings. [4.8]
And whoever creates an obstacle, even for a moment, to his merit —
for that destroyer of beings' welfare, there is no end to evil destinies. [4.9]

children.text: ekasyāpi hi sattvasya hitaṃ hatvā hato bhavet /
children.translated_text: For even by destroying the welfare of a single being, one would be destroyed;
how much more so of embodied beings dwelling throughout the entirety of boundless space? [4.10]
Thus, tossed back and forth by the force of transgressions and the force of <s>bodhicitta</s>,
one is long delayed in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) before attaining the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>). [4.11]
Therefore, what I have vowed should be accomplished by me with care;

children.text: nādya cetkriyate yatnastalenāsmi talaṃ gataḥ // SBca_4.12 //
children.translated_text: if I make no effort today, I have sunk from depth to depth. [4.12]
Immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> have passed, who sought the welfare of all beings,
yet through my own fault, I have not come within the range of their healing. [4.13]

children.text: adyāpi cettathaiva syāṃ yathaivāhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if even now I continue just as before, again and again
I would obtain evil destinies, sickness, death, cutting, splitting, and the like. [4.14]
When shall I obtain — so extremely rare — the arising of a <s>Tathāgata</s>,
faith, human birth, and fitness for the practice of virtue? [4.15]
This day of health, with food, free from calamity —
life is but a moment, deceptive, the body like something merely borrowed. [4.16]
Indeed, by such conduct of mine, human birth is not obtained again;

children.text: alabhyamāne mānuṣye pāpameva kutaḥ śubham // SBca_4.17 //
children.translated_text: and if human birth is not obtained, there is only sin — whence any good? [4.17]
When, though capable of virtue, I do not perform virtue,

children.text: apāyaduḥkhaiḥ saṃmūḍhaḥ kiṃ kariṣyāmyahaṃ tadā // SBca_4.18 //
children.translated_text: what then shall I do, bewildered by the sufferings of the lower realms? [4.18]
For one who does not perform virtue and who accumulates sin,
even the very word 'happy destiny' is destroyed for hundreds of billions of <s>kalpas</s> (eons). [4.19]
For this very reason the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) declared: 'Human birth is exceedingly rare —
like a turtle inserting its neck through a hole in a yoke floating in the great ocean.' [4.20]
From sin committed in a single instant, one dwells in <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell) for an eon;

children.text: anādikālopacitāt pāpāt kā sugatau kathā // SBca_4.21 //
children.translated_text: from sin accumulated since beginningless time, what hope is there for a happy destiny? [4.21]
Nor is one freed after experiencing merely that much [suffering];
for even while experiencing that, further sin is born. [4.22]

children.text: nātaḥ parā vañcanāsti na ca moho 'styataḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no greater self-deception than this, no greater delusion:

children.text: yadīdṛśaṃ kṣaṇaṃ prāpya nābhyastaṃ kuśalaṃ mayā // SBca_4.23 //
children.translated_text: that having obtained such a [precious] moment, I have not practiced virtue. [4.23]

children.text: yadi caivaṃ vimṛṣyāmi punaḥ sīdāmi mohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if, even after reflecting thus, I again sink into delusion,

children.text: śociṣyāmi ciraṃ bhūyo yamadūtaiḥ pracoditaḥ // SBca_4.24 //
children.translated_text: I shall grieve for a long time, impelled by the messengers of <s>Yama</s> (the lord of death). [4.24]

children.text: ciraṃ dhakṣyati me kāyaṃ nārakāgniḥ suduḥsahaḥ /
children.translated_text: The unbearable fire of the hells will burn my body for a long time,
and the fire of remorse will burn my untrained mind for a long time. [4.25]
Having somehow reached this beneficial ground, so extremely rare to find,

children.text: jānannapi ca nīye 'haṃ tāneva narakān punaḥ // SBca_4.26 //
children.translated_text: yet knowing full well, I am being led again to those very hells. [4.26]

children.text: atra me cetanā nāsti mantrairiva vimohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this matter I have no will, as if bewildered by spells;

children.text: na jāne kena muhyāmi ko 'trāntarmama tiṣṭhati // SBca_4.27 //
children.translated_text: I do not know what deludes me, or who dwells within me. [4.27]
The enemies — craving, hatred, and the like — have no hands, no feet;

children.text: na śūrā na ca te prājñāḥ kathaṃ dāsīkṛto 'smi taiḥ // SBca_4.28 //
children.translated_text: they are neither brave nor wise — how then have I been enslaved by them? [4.28]
Abiding in my own mind, they strike me down at their ease;
and yet I do not become angry at them — shame on such misplaced forbearance! [4.29]

children.text: sarve devā manuṣyāśca yadi syurmama śatravaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all the gods and humans were my enemies,

children.text: te 'pi nāvīcikaṃ vahniṃ samudānayituṃ kṣamāḥ // SBca_4.30 //
children.translated_text: even they could not drag me into the fire of <s>Avīci</s>. [4.30]
That which, upon contact, leaves not even ashes of <s>Meru</s> (the cosmic mountain),

children.text: kṣaṇāt kṣipanti māṃ tatra balinaḥ kleśaśatravaḥ // SBca_4.31 //
children.translated_text: into that [fire] these powerful <s>kleśa</s>-enemies (affliction-enemies) hurl me in an instant. [4.31]
Indeed, no other enemy has a lifespan so long —
so immensely long, beginningless and endless — as my <s>kleśa</s>-enemies (affliction-enemies). [4.32]
All others, when served with kindness, become helpers for one's welfare;
but these <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), when served, only cause even greater suffering. [4.33]
Thus, while these perpetual, long-standing enemies, the sole cause of floods of misfortune,

children.text: hṛdaye nivasatsu nirbhayaṃ mama saṃsāraratiḥ kathaṃ bhavet // SBca_4.34 //
children.translated_text: dwell in my heart, how can I fearlessly delight in <s>saṃsāra</s>? [4.34]
These wardens of the prison of existence, these executioners in the hells and elsewhere —

children.text: mativeśmani lobhapañjare yadi tiṣṭhanti kutaḥ sukhaṃ mama // SBca_4.35 //
children.translated_text: if they remain in the cage of greed within the house of my mind, how can there be happiness for me? [4.35]

children.text: tasmānna tāvadahamatra dhuraṃ kṣipāmi yāvanna śatrava ime nihatāḥ samakṣam /
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall not lay down this burden until these enemies are slain before my eyes;

children.text: svalpe 'pi tāvadapakāriṇi baddharoṣā mānonnatāstamanihatya na yānti nidrām // SBca_4.36 //
children.translated_text: even those who are seized with anger toward a petty offender, puffed up with pride, do not sleep until they have destroyed that foe. [4.36]
heedless of the pain from countless arrows and spears, do not turn back without accomplishing their goal. [4.37]
Those who are fierce enough to slay in the front lines of battle the wretched beings blinded by the suffering of natural death,
How much more so for me, who am resolved to destroy the natural enemies that are the perpetual cause of all suffering —

children.text: bhavati mama viṣādadainyamadya vyasanaśatairapi kena hetunā vai // SBca_4.38 //
children.translated_text: by what reason should there be dejection and wretchedness in me today, even from hundreds of adversities? [4.38]
They bear on their bodies the scars of enemies' wounds as if they were ornaments, even without purpose;

children.text: mahārthasiddhyai tu samudyatasya duḥkhāni kasmānmama bādhakāni // SBca_4.39 //
children.translated_text: why then, for one striving toward the great goal, should sufferings be a hindrance to me? [4.39]
Fishermen, outcasts, farmers, and the like, their minds fixed merely on their own livelihood,

children.text: śītātapādivyasanaṃ sahante jagaddhitārthaṃ na kathaṃ sahe 'ham // SBca_4.40 //
children.translated_text: endure the hardships of cold, heat, and the rest — how then should I not endure for the welfare of the world? [4.40]
Having vowed to liberate the world from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) throughout the ten directions and the reaches of space,

children.text: pratijñāya madātmāpi na kleśebhyo vimocitaḥ // SBca_4.41 //
children.translated_text: I myself have not yet been freed from <s>kleśas</s>. [4.41]
Not knowing my own measure, I spoke like a madman then;
therefore I shall be unwavering forever in destroying the <s>kleśas</s>. [4.42]
In this I shall be tenacious, sworn to enmity, and combative,
except against that type of <s>kleśa</s> that is connected with the destruction of [other] <s>kleśas</s>. [4.43]

children.text: galantvantrāṇi me kāmaṃ śiraḥ patatu nāma me /
children.translated_text: Let my entrails spill out if they will, let my head fall —

children.text: na tvevāvanatiṃ yāmi sarvathā kleśavairiṇām // SBca_4.44 //
children.translated_text: but never shall I bow down before the <s>kleśa</s>-enemies. [4.44]

children.text: nirvāsitasyāpi tu nāma śatrordeśāntare sthānaparigrahaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: An exiled foe may establish himself in another land,

children.text: yataḥ punaḥ saṃbhṛtaśaktireti na kleśaśatrorgatirīdṛśī tu // SBca_4.45 //
children.translated_text: from which, having regathered his strength, he returns — but the <s>kleśa</s>-enemy's course is not like that. [4.45]

children.text: kvāsau yāyānmanmanaḥstho nirastaḥ sthitvā yasmin madvadhārthaṃ yateta /
children.translated_text: Where would it go, this enemy dwelling in my mind, once expelled? Where would it stand to strive for my destruction?

children.text: nodyogo me kevalaṃ mandabuddheḥ kleśāḥ prajñādṛṣṭisādhyā varākāḥ // SBca_4.46 //
children.translated_text: It is merely that I, dull-witted, make no effort — the <s>kleśas</s> are wretched things, conquered by the eye of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). [4.46]

children.text: na kleśā viṣayeṣu nendriyagaṇe nāpyantarāle sthitā
children.translated_text: The <s>kleśas</s> do not dwell in sense-objects, nor in the group of sense-faculties, nor in the space between,

children.text: nāto 'nyatra kuha sthitāḥ punaramī mathnanti kṛtsnaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: nor anywhere else — yet where then do they dwell, these that torment the entire world?
They are mere illusion! Therefore, release the fear in your heart and embrace effort
for the sake of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Why do you torment yourself needlessly in the hells? [4.47]
Having thus resolved, I shall make effort for the sake of practicing the trainings as taught;
how can there be healing for one whose illness is curable by medicine, if he strays from the physician's instructions? [4.48]
Thus ends the fourth chapter, on Heedfulness regarding <s>Bodhicitta</s>, in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.
Chapter Five, entitled 'The Guarding of Introspective Awareness' (<s>Saṃprajanyarakṣaṇa</s>).
One who wishes to guard the trainings must guard the mind with effort;

children.text: na śikṣā rakṣituṃ śakyā calaṃ cittamarakṣatā // SBca_5.1 //
children.translated_text: one who does not guard the fickle mind cannot guard the trainings. [5.1]

children.text: adāntā mattamātaṅgā na kurvantīha tāṃ vyathām /
children.translated_text: Untamed, maddened elephants do not cause such harm in this world
as the unleashed elephant of the mind causes in <s>Avīci</s> and the other [hells]. [5.2]
But if the elephant of the mind is bound on all sides by the rope of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness),
all fear vanishes and all good arrives. [5.3]

children.text: vyāghrāḥ siṃhā gajā ṛkṣāḥ sarpāḥ sarve ca śatravaḥ /
children.translated_text: Tigers, lions, elephants, bears, serpents, all enemies,
all the wardens of the hells, <s>ḍākinīs</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) — [5.4]
all these become bound by the binding of the one mind alone;

children.text: cittasyaikasya damanāt sarve dāntā bhavanti ca // SBca_5.5 //
children.translated_text: by the taming of the one mind alone, all these become tamed. [5.5]
For all fears and immeasurable sufferings
arise from the mind alone — so declared the Speaker of Truth. [5.6]
By whom were the weapons in the hells fashioned with such effort?

children.text: taptāyaḥkuṭṭimaṃ kena kuto jātāśca tāḥ striyaḥ // SBca_5.7 //
children.translated_text: By whom was the floor of burning iron made? And whence arose those women? [5.7]
All such things arise from the sinful mind, declared the Sage;

children.text: tasmānna kaścit trailokye cittādanyo bhayānakaḥ // SBca_5.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore there is nothing more fearsome in the three worlds than the mind. [5.8]
If <s>dānapāramitā</s> (the perfection of giving) consisted in making the world free of poverty,
since the world is still poor today, how did the former <s>Buddhas</s> perfect it? [5.9]
The <s>dānapāramitā</s> is said to be the mind of relinquishing all to all people, together with its fruit;

children.text: dānapāramitā proktā tasmātsā cittameva tu // SBca_5.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore it is the mind itself. [5.10]

children.text: matsyādayaḥ kva nīyantāṃ mārayeyaṃ yato na tān /
children.translated_text: Where could fish and the like be taken so that I would not kill them?

children.text: labdhe viraticitte tu śīlapāramitā matā // SBca_5.11 //
children.translated_text: When the mind of abstention is obtained, that is considered <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (the perfection of morality). [5.11]
How many wicked beings, as vast as the sky, could I kill?

children.text: mārite krodhacitte tu māritāḥ sarvaśatravaḥ // SBca_5.12 //
children.translated_text: When the mind of anger is killed, all enemies are killed. [5.12]
Where would there be enough leather to cover the entire earth?
With merely the leather of a sandal, the earth is covered. [5.13]

children.text: bāhyā bhāvā mayā tadvacchakyā vārayituṃ na hi /
children.translated_text: Likewise, I cannot ward off external things;
I shall ward off my own mind — what need have I for other things to be warded off? [5.14]
Even accompanied by speech and body, a dull practice does not bear that fruit
which the keen practice of the mind alone [bears] — such as [attaining] <s>Brahmaloka</s> and the like. [5.15]
All recitations and austerities, even those performed for a long time,
are entirely useless when done with a distracted, dull mind — so declared the All-Knowing One. [5.16]

children.text: duḥkhaṃ hantuṃ sukhaṃ prāptuṃ te bhramanti mudhāmbare /
children.translated_text: Those who have not cultivated this mind, the secret essence of all <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: yairetaddharmasarvasvaṃ cittaṃ guhyaṃ na bhāvitam // SBca_5.17 //
children.translated_text: wander uselessly in space, seeking to destroy suffering and attain happiness. [5.17]
Therefore I must keep my mind well-established and well-guarded;

children.text: cittarakṣāvrataṃ mukttvā bahubhiḥ kiṃ mama vrataiḥ // SBca_5.18 //
children.translated_text: apart from the vow of guarding the mind, what use are many vows to me? [5.18]
Just as one in the midst of a restless crowd carefully guards a wound,
so, when among wicked people, one should always guard the wound of the mind. [5.19]
If, fearing the slight pain of a wound, I carefully protect the wound,
should I not [protect] the wound of the mind, fearing the crushing blow of the mountain-presses [of hell]? [5.20]
For one who lives in this manner, even among wicked people
and even amid crowds of women, the steadfast ascetic is not broken. [5.21]

children.text: lābhā naśyantu me kāmaṃ satkāraḥ kāyajīvitam /
children.translated_text: Let my gains perish, as well as honor, body, and livelihood;

children.text: naśyatvanyacca kuśalaṃ mā tu cittaṃ kadācana // SBca_5.22 //
children.translated_text: let other virtues perish — but never the mind. [5.22]
To those who wish to guard the mind, I make this entreaty with palms joined:

children.text: smṛtiṃ ca saṃprajanyaṃ ca sarvayatnena rakṣata // SBca_5.23 //
children.translated_text: Guard <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>saṃprajanya</s> (introspective awareness) with every effort! (5.23)
Just as a person afflicted by illness is incapable of all activities,

children.text: tathābhyāṃ vikalaṃ cittaṃ na kṣamaṃ sarvakarmasu // SBca_5.24 //
children.translated_text: so too a mind lacking these two is incapable of all activities. (5.24)
What has been heard, contemplated, and meditated upon by one whose mind lacks <s>saṃprajanya</s> (introspective awareness)
does not remain in memory, like water in a leaking pot. (5.25)
Many who are learned, who have faith, and who are devoted to effort,
become stained by downfalls through the fault of lacking <s>saṃprajanya</s> (introspective awareness). (5.26)
Robbed by the thief of lack of <s>saṃprajanya</s>, who follows upon the theft of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness),

children.text: upacityāpi puṇyāni muṣitā yānti durgatim // SBca_5.27 //
children.translated_text: even those who have accumulated merit are plundered and go to unfortunate rebirths. (5.27)
This band of <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) thieves seeks an opening;
having found an opening, they plunder and destroy the life of fortunate rebirth. (5.28)
Therefore, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) should never be removed from the door of the mind;
even if it has departed, it should be restored by recalling the suffering of the lower realms. (5.29)
Through the instruction of preceptors, through the reverence of those who act respectfully even out of fear,
and through the company of a <s>guru</s> — for the fortunate, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) arises easily. (5.30)
The <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> possess unobstructed vision everywhere;
everything is before them — I stand in their very presence. (5.31)
Reflecting thus, one should remain filled with modesty, respect, and fear;
and in this way, <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>) will arise for such a person again and again. (5.32)

children.text: saṃprajanyaṃ tadāyāti na ca yātyāgataṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃprajanya</s> (introspective awareness) then arrives and, once come, does not depart again,
when <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) stands at the door of the mind for the purpose of guarding. (5.33)
First, then, the mind should always be kept in this manner:
I should remain always as if without sense faculties, like a block of wood. (5.34)
Fruitless glancing of the eyes should never be done;
rather, the gaze should always be cast downward, as if in deep contemplation. (5.35)
But for the sake of resting the eyes, one may occasionally look to the [four] directions;

children.text: ābhāsamātraṃ dṛṣṭvā ca svāgatārthaṃ vilokayet // SBca_5.36 //
children.translated_text: and having seen only an appearance, one may look up to greet [someone]. (5.36)
On the road and so forth, to detect danger, one should look repeatedly in the four directions;

children.text: diśo viśramya vīkṣeta parāvṛtyaiva pṛṣṭhataḥ // SBca_5.37 //
children.translated_text: having paused, one should look in the [four] directions, and look behind only by turning around. (5.37)
Whether going forward or back, having examined what is ahead and behind,

children.text: evaṃ sarvāsvavasthāsu kāryaṃ buddhvā samācaret // SBca_5.38 //
children.translated_text: one should act in all situations after having understood what needs to be done. (5.38)
Having set [oneself to a task] thinking 'the body should be positioned thus,' and then returning to the activity,

children.text: kathaṃ kāyaḥ sthita iti draṣṭavyaṃ punarantarā // SBca_5.39 //
children.translated_text: one should check again in between: 'How is the body positioned?' (5.39)
The mind, like a maddened elephant, should be watched with every effort,

children.text: dharmacintāmahāstambhe yathā baddho na mucyate // SBca_5.40 //
children.translated_text: so that, bound to the great pillar of <s>dharma</s>-reflection, it is not released. (5.40)

children.text: kutra me vartata iti pratyavekṣyaṃ tathā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where is my mind dwelling?' — the mind should be examined thus,
so that one does not for even a moment release the yoke of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). (5.41)
If one is unable [to maintain this] in connection with danger, festivities, and the like, one may act as is comfortable;
for at the time of giving, it is said that [the strictness of] moral conduct may be relaxed. (5.42)
Whatever one has understood and begun to do, one should not think of anything else;
that very task should be brought to completion first, with the inner self absorbed in it. (5.43)

children.text: evaṃ hi sukṛtaṃ sarvamanyathā nobhayaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: In this way, everything is done well; otherwise, neither [task] is accomplished.
And the <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) of lack of <s>saṃprajanya</s> will also increase in this way. (5.44)
Amid the many kinds of idle talk going on in various ways,
and amid all [objects of] curiosity, one should destroy the eagerness that has arisen. (5.45)
Kneading clay, cutting grass, drawing lines, and other fruitless [activities] —
remembering the <s>Tathāgata's</s> training, one should fearfully abandon them at once. (5.46)
Whenever one wishes to move or wishes to speak,
one should first examine one's own mind, and then act properly with steadiness. (5.47)
Whenever one sees that one's own mind is attracted or repelled,

children.text: na kartavyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ sthātavyaṃ kāṣṭhavattadā // SBca_5.48 //
children.translated_text: one should neither act nor speak, but remain like a block of wood. (5.48)
Whenever [the mind] is agitated, derisive, filled with pride and arrogance,

children.text: sotprāsātiśayaṃ vakraṃ vañcakaṃ ca mano bhavet // SBca_5.49 //
children.translated_text: contemptuous, excessive, crooked, or deceitful — (5.49)
whenever it tends toward self-aggrandizement or disparagement of others,
or toward reproach and contentiousness — then one should remain like a block of wood. (5.50)
'My mind seeks gain, honor, and fame, or seeks a following,

children.text: upasthānārthe me cittaṃ tasmāttiṣṭhāmi kāṣṭhavat // SBca_5.51 //
children.translated_text: or seeks personal service' — therefore I shall remain like a block of wood. (5.51)
'My mind is harsh toward others' interests, seeks its own interest, or desires an audience,

children.text: vaktumicchati me cittaṃ tasmāttiṣṭhāmi kāṣṭhavat // SBca_5.52 //
children.translated_text: and wishes to speak' — therefore I shall remain like a block of wood. (5.52)
[When the mind is] impatient, lazy, timid, impudent, or garrulous,
or biased toward one's own faction — therefore I shall remain like a block of wood. (5.53)
Seeing the mind thus afflicted or pursuing fruitless endeavors,

children.text: nigṛhṇīyād dṛḍhaṃ śūraḥ pratipakṣeṇa tatsadā // SBca_5.54 //
children.translated_text: the courageous one should always firmly restrain it by means of the antidote. (5.54)
[The mind should be] firmly resolved, serene, steadfast, respectful and reverent,
modest, fearful, peaceful, and devoted to pleasing others. (5.55)
Unwearied by the mutually contradictory childish desires [of beings],
[knowing that] 'these [desires] arise from the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),' one should be filled with compassion. (5.56)
Always under the control of myself and [other] beings in blameless matters,
I shall maintain this mind free from pride, like a magical creation. (5.57)
Recalling again and again the supreme opportune moment, obtained after so long,
I shall maintain such a mind, unshakeable like <s>Sumeru</s>. (5.58)
Dragged here and there by vultures greedy for flesh,

children.text: na karotyanyathā kāyaḥ kasmādatra pratikriyām // SBca_5.59 //
children.translated_text: the body does not react — why then do you counteract [their pulling]? (5.59)
Why do you guard this mind, appropriating [the body] and elevating it?

children.text: tvattaścetpṛthagevāyaṃ tenātra tava ko vyayaḥ // SBca_5.60 //
children.translated_text: If it is something separate from you, what loss is there to you in this? (5.60)

children.text: na svīkaroṣi he mūḍha kāṣṭhaputtalakaṃ śucim /
children.translated_text: You do not take as your own, O fool, a clean wooden doll;
why then do you guard this putrid machine assembled from filth? (5.61)
First, with your own intelligence, separate this envelope of skin;
with the sword of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), release the flesh from the cage of bones. (5.62)
Having separated the bones too, look at the marrow within;
'Is there any essence here?' — examine this for yourself. (5.63)

children.text: evamanviṣya yatnena na dṛṣṭaṃ sāramatra te /
children.translated_text: Having searched thus diligently and finding no essence here,

children.text: adhunā vada kasmāttvaṃ kāyamadyāpi rakṣasi // SBca_5.64 //
children.translated_text: now say — why do you still guard this body? (5.64)

children.text: na khāditavyamaśuci tvayā peyaṃ na śoṇitam /
children.translated_text: The impure [flesh] is not to be eaten by you, the blood is not to be drunk,

children.text: nāntrāṇi cūṣitavyāni kiṃ kāyena kariṣyasi // SBca_5.65 //
children.translated_text: the entrails are not to be sucked — what will you do with this body? (5.65)
It would be fitting to keep it as food for vultures and jackals;
but this body of human beings is merely an instrument for action. (5.66)
And even as you guard it thus, merciless death will seize it

children.text: kāyaṃ dāsyati gṛdhrebhyastadā tvaṃ kiṃ kariṣyasi // SBca_5.67 //
children.translated_text: and give this body to the vultures — what will you do then? (5.67)

children.text: na sthāsyatīti bhṛtyāya na vastrādi pradīyate /
children.translated_text: One does not give clothing and such to a servant who will not stay;

children.text: kāyo yāsyati khāditvā kasmāttvaṃ kuruṣe vyayam // SBca_5.68 //
children.translated_text: the body will depart after consuming — why do you incur this expense? (5.68)
Having given it its wages, therefore, O mind, now pursue your own purpose;

children.text: na hi vaitanikopāttaṃ sarvaṃ tasmai pradīyate // SBca_5.69 //
children.translated_text: for not everything earned by a hired worker is given to him. (5.69)
Establish the notion of a ship regarding the body — [it is merely] a basis for coming and going;
make the body go as you wish, for the accomplishment of the welfare of beings. (5.70)
One who has thus brought the self under control should always be of smiling countenance;
one should abandon frowning, be the first to greet others, and be a friend to the world. (5.71)
One should not throw down seats and such noisily and suddenly;
one should not bang doors, and should always delight in quietness. (5.72)
The crane, the cat, and the thief — moving silently and stealthily —
accomplish their desired goal; the practitioner should always conduct himself thus. (5.73)
One should accept with bowed head the words of those skilled in exhorting others,

children.text: pratīcchecchirasā vākyaṃ sarvaśiṣyaḥ sadā bhavet // SBca_5.74 //
children.translated_text: of those who offer help unsolicited — one should always be a student of all. (5.74)
To all who speak well, one should utter 'Well said!';
seeing one who performs meritorious deeds, one should gladden them with praises. (5.75)
One should speak of [others'] virtues in their absence, and repeat them with satisfaction;
when one's own praises are spoken, one should reflect on the other's appreciation of good qualities. (5.76)

children.text: sarvārambhā hi tuṣṭyarthāḥ sā vittairapi durlabhā /
children.translated_text: For all endeavors are for the sake of satisfaction, which is hard to obtain even with wealth;
therefore I shall enjoy the satisfaction [that comes] from the good qualities produced by others' efforts. (5.77)

children.text: na cātra me vyayaḥ kaścitparatra ca mahatsukham /
children.translated_text: There is no loss to me in this, and great happiness in the hereafter;

children.text: aprītiduḥkhaṃ dveṣaistu mahadduḥkhaṃ paratra ca // SBca_5.78 //
children.translated_text: but from hatred there is the suffering of displeasure, and great suffering in the hereafter. (5.78)
One should speak words that are trustworthy, with clear meaning, delightful,
pleasant to the ear, rooted in compassion, soft, and in a gentle, low voice. (5.79)
One should always look directly at beings, as if drinking them in with the eyes;

children.text: etāneva samāśritya buddhatvaṃ me bhaviṣyati // SBca_5.80 //
children.translated_text: 'Depending on these very [beings], my <s>Buddhahood</s> will come about.' (5.80)
Great merit arises from continuous, dedicated [practice], from the application of antidotes,

children.text: guṇopakārikṣetre ca duḥkhite ca mahacchubham // SBca_5.81 //
children.translated_text: in the field of those with good qualities and those who have helped one, and [in the field of] the suffering. (5.81)
One should be skilled, diligent, and always act by oneself;
one should not yield the opportunity to anyone in any task. (5.82)
The <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), beginning with <s>dāna</s> (generosity), are progressively superior;
one should not abandon a superior one for the sake of an inferior, except where it serves as a bridge of conduct. (5.83)
Understanding this, one should always be active in the welfare of others;
even what is prohibited is permitted for the compassionate one who sees the [greater] purpose. (5.84)
Sharing with those who have fallen into misfortune, the protectorless, and those observing vows,
one should eat a moderate amount, and give away everything beyond the three robes. (5.85)
One should not torment this body, which serves the true <s>Dharma</s>, for trivial purposes;
for only in this way will one quickly fulfill the aspirations of beings. (5.86)
Therefore, one should not sacrifice one's life when the compassionate intent is impure;

children.text: tulyāśaye tu tattyājyamitthaṃ na parihīyate // SBca_5.87 //
children.translated_text: but when the intent is equal [i.e., pure], one should sacrifice it — thus one does not lose. (5.87)

children.text: dharmaṃ nirgaurave svasthe na śiroveṣṭite vadet /
children.translated_text: One should not teach the <s>Dharma</s> to one who lacks respect, to one who is healthy [but wraps their head], to one wearing a head-covering,
or to one with an umbrella, staff, or weapon, or to one with the head veiled. (5.88)
The profound and lofty [<s>Dharma</s>] should not [be taught] to the lowly, nor to women without a man present;
one should practice equal reverence toward both the lower and higher <s>Dharma</s> teachings. (5.89)
One should not direct a vessel of the lofty <s>Dharma</s> to the lower <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: na cācāraṃ parityajya sūtramantraiḥ pralobhayet // SBca_5.90 //
children.translated_text: nor should one entice [people] away from good conduct with <s>sūtras</s> and <s>mantras</s>. (5.90)
The discarding of tooth-sticks and phlegm openly

children.text: neṣṭaṃ jale sthale bhogye mūtrādeścāpi garhitam // SBca_5.91 //
children.translated_text: is not approved; [urinating] in water, on ground [used by others], or in enjoyable [places], and such [discharge] of urine and the like is also censured. (5.91)
One should not eat with the mouth overfull, noisily, or with the mouth gaping open;

children.text: pralambapādaṃ nāsīta na bāhū mardayetsamam // SBca_5.92 //
children.translated_text: one should not sit with legs stretched out, and should not rub both arms simultaneously. (5.92)
One should not travel, lie down, or sit alone with another's wife;

children.text: lokāprasādakaṃ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭvā ca varjayet // SBca_5.93 //
children.translated_text: having observed and inquired, one should avoid everything that displeases people. (5.93)
One should not point or gesture with a finger, but respectfully with the right hand;
one should indicate the way with the entire hand, in the same manner. (5.94)
One should not wave one's arms and shout at anyone in a slight emergency;
rather, one should snap the fingers and the like — otherwise one would be undisciplined. (5.95)
One should lie down in the preferred direction, in the manner of the Lord's <s>parinirvāṇa</s> posture;
with full awareness and [the resolve for] quick rising, one should rise before [the appointed time], as a matter of duty. (5.96)
The conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is said to be immeasurable;
one should certainly practice that conduct which purifies the mind. (5.97)

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ ca triskandhaṃ triṣkālaṃ ca pravartayet /
children.translated_text: Day and night, one should practice the <s>triskandha</s> (three-part [confession]) three times;
by that, and by reliance on <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind) and the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), the remaining downfalls are pacified. (5.98)

children.text: yā avasthāḥ prapadyeta svayaṃ paravaśo 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever situations one encounters, whether by oneself or under another's power —

children.text: tāsvavasthāsu yāḥ śikṣāḥ śikṣettā eva yatnataḥ // SBca_5.99 //
children.translated_text: In those states, whatever trainings there are, one should train in them diligently. (5.99)

children.text: na hi tadvidyate kiṃcidyanna śikṣyaṃ jinātmajaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For there is nothing whatsoever that should not be trained in by the sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One);

children.text: na tadasti na yatpuṇyamevaṃ viharataḥ sataḥ // SBca_5.100 //
children.translated_text: there is no merit that does not accrue to one who conducts himself thus. (5.100)
Whether indirectly or directly, one should do nothing except for the benefit of beings;

children.text: sattvānāmeva cārthāya sarvaṃ bodhāya nāmayet // SBca_5.101 //
children.translated_text: and for the sake of beings alone, one should dedicate everything toward <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening). (5.101)

children.text: sadā kalyāṇamitraṃ ca jīvitārthe 'pi na tyajet /
children.translated_text: One should never abandon the virtuous spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), even at the cost of one's life —
one who upholds the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vow and is skilled in the meaning of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. (5.102)
From the Śrīsaṃbhavavimokṣa, one should learn the proper conduct toward the teacher;
this and other teachings spoken by the <s>Buddha</s> should be known from reading the <s>sūtras</s>. (5.103)
The trainings are found in the <s>sūtras</s>; therefore one should recite the <s>sūtras</s>;
and in the <s>Ākāśagarbha Sūtra</s>, one should examine the root downfalls. (5.104)
The <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> (Compendium of Training) must be consulted again and again,
since the proper conduct is shown therein in detail. (5.105)
Or, in brief, one should examine the <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s> (Compendium of Sūtras);
and with effort, the second one composed by the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>. (5.106)

children.text: yato nivāryate yatra yadeva ca niyujyate /
children.translated_text: Whatever is prohibited, and whatever is enjoined —
having examined the training, one should practice it for the sake of guarding the minds of worldly beings. (5.107)
This alone, in brief, is the characteristic of <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear awareness):
the repeated examination of the state of one's body and mind. (5.108)

children.text: kāyenaiva paṭhiṣyāmi vākpāṭhena tu kiṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: I shall recite this with my body alone — what use is mere verbal recitation?
What benefit will come to the sick person from merely reciting the prescription? (5.109)

children.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ saṃprajanyarakṣaṇaṃ nāma pañcamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, named "Guarding Clear Awareness," in the commentary (<s>Pañjikā</s>) on the <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.
Chapter 6: The Perfection of Patience (<s>Kṣānti-pāramitā</s>), the Sixth Chapter.
All this good conduct — giving, worship of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) —
performed over thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (eons), is destroyed by anger (<s>pratigha</s>). (6.1)

children.text: na ca dveṣasamaṃ pāpaṃ na ca kṣāntisamaṃ tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no evil equal to hatred, and no austerity equal to patience;
therefore one should cultivate patience by various means, with great effort. (6.2)

children.text: manaḥ śamaṃ na gṛhṇāti na prītisukhamaśnute /
children.translated_text: The mind finds no peace, enjoys no delight or happiness,

children.text: na nidrāṃ na dhṛtiṃ yāti dveṣaśalye hṛdi sthite // SBca_6.3 //
children.translated_text: finds neither sleep nor steadiness, when the thorn of hatred is lodged in the heart. (6.3)
Even those whom one honors with wealth and respect, and those who depend upon him —
even they wish to kill this master made wretched by hatred. (6.4)
Even friends are repelled by him; he gives, yet is not served.

children.text: saṃkṣepānnāsti tatkiṃcit krodhano yena susthitaḥ // SBca_6.5 //
children.translated_text: In short, there is nothing by which an angry person can be well-situated. (6.5)
Recognizing that hatred produces such sufferings as these,

children.text: yaḥ krodhaṃ hanti nirbandhāt sa sukhīha paratra ca // SBca_6.6 //
children.translated_text: one who resolutely destroys anger is happy here and hereafter. (6.6)
Arising from the occurrence of the undesired and from the obstruction of the desired,

children.text: daurmanasyāśanaṃ prāpya dveṣo dṛpto nihanti mām // SBca_6.7 //
children.translated_text: hatred, having obtained the nourishment of mental distress, grows arrogant and destroys me. (6.7)
Therefore I shall destroy the nourishment of that enemy,
for this foe has no other purpose than my destruction. (6.8)
Even upon the arrival of the most undesirable, my cheerfulness should not be disturbed;
for even in mental distress there is nothing desirable, and wholesome conduct is impaired. (6.9)
If there is a remedy, then what is the use of distress?

children.text: atha nāsti pratīkāro daurmanasyena tatra kim // SBca_6.10 //
children.translated_text: And if there is no remedy, then what is the use of distress? (6.10)
Suffering, contempt, harsh words, and disrepute — these are undesired
for oneself and one's dear ones, and the reverse of these for one's enemy. (6.11)
Happiness is obtained with difficulty, while suffering persists effortlessly;

children.text: duḥkhenaiva ca niḥsāraḥ cetastasmād dṛḍhībhava // SBca_6.12 //
children.translated_text: yet liberation is only through suffering — therefore, O mind, be firm! (6.12)
The devotees of <s>Durgā</s> and the <s>Karṇāṭas</s> endure the pain of burning and cutting

children.text: vṛthā sahante muktyarthamahaṃ kasmāttu kātaraḥ // SBca_6.13 //
children.translated_text: pointlessly, for the sake of liberation — why then am I a coward? (6.13)
There is nothing that is difficult through practice;
therefore, by practicing with mild pain, even great pain should be endured. (6.14)
The pain of gadflies, gnats, mosquitoes, hunger, thirst, and the like,

children.text: mahatkaṇḍvādiduḥkhaṃ ca kimanarthaṃ na paśyasi // SBca_6.15 //
children.translated_text: and great suffering such as itching — do you not see these as meaningless? (6.15)
Through cold, heat, rain, wind, travel, illness, bondage, and beatings,

children.text: saukumāryaṃ na kartavyamanyathā vardhate vyathā // SBca_6.16 //
children.translated_text: one should not cultivate delicacy, lest the suffering increase. (6.16)
Some, upon seeing their own blood, become all the more valiant;

children.text: paraśoṇitamapyeke dṛṣṭvā mūrcchāṃ vrajanti yat // SBca_6.17 //
children.translated_text: while others, even upon seeing another's blood, fall into a faint. (6.17)
That comes from the firmness or cowardice of the mind;
therefore one should be a conqueror of suffering and should overcome pain. (6.18)

children.text: duḥkhe 'pi naiva cittasya prasādaṃ kṣobhayed budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in suffering, the wise one should not disturb the serenity of the mind,

children.text: saṃgrāmo hi saha kleśairyuddhe ca sulabhā vyathā // SBca_6.19 //
children.translated_text: for the battle is with the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and in battle, wounds are natural. (6.19)
Those who, receiving the blows of enemies upon their chests, conquer their foes —

children.text: te te vijayinaḥ śūrāḥ śeṣāstu mṛtamārakāḥ // SBca_6.20 //
children.translated_text: they are the true victorious heroes; the rest are merely slayers of the dead. (6.20)
Another virtue of suffering: through disillusionment, pride is shed,

children.text: saṃsāriṣu ca kāruṇyaṃ pāpādbhītirjine spṛhā // SBca_6.21 //
children.translated_text: compassion arises for those in <s>saṃsāra</s>, fear of sin, and longing for the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). (6.21)
I feel no anger toward bile and the like, though they cause great suffering;

children.text: sacetaneṣu kiṃ kopaḥ te 'pi pratyayakopitāḥ // SBca_6.22 //
children.translated_text: why then anger toward sentient beings? They too are provoked by conditions. (6.22)
Just as a boil arises unwished for,
so too does anger arise forcefully, though unwished for. (6.23)

children.text: kupyāmīti na saṃcintya kupyati svecchayā janaḥ /
children.translated_text: A person does not become angry by deliberately thinking "I shall be angry";

children.text: utpatsya ityabhipretya krodha utpadyate na ca // SBca_6.24 //
children.translated_text: nor does anger arise by intending "I shall arise." (6.24)
Whatever offenses there are and whatever various sins —

children.text: sarvaṃ tatpratyayabalāt svatantraṃ tu na vidyate // SBca_6.25 //
children.translated_text: all arise through the force of conditions; nothing arises independently. (6.25)
The assemblage of conditions does not have the thought "I shall produce";

children.text: na cāpi janitasyāsti janito 'smīti cetanā // SBca_6.26 //
children.translated_text: nor does what is produced have the thought "I have been produced." (6.26)
That which is called the <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Matter), what is postulated as the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) —

children.text: tadeva hi bhavābhīti na saṃcintyopajāyate // SBca_6.27 //
children.translated_text: even that does not come into being by deliberation, thinking "I shall become." (6.27)

children.text: anutpannaṃ hi tannāsti ka icchedbhavituṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: For what has not arisen does not exist — who then would wish to come into being?
And since it is occupied with its objects, it does not even strive to cease. (6.28)
The <s>Ātman</s>, being eternal and unconscious, is clearly inactive, like space;
even in contact with other conditions, what action is possible for the changeless? (6.29)

children.text: yaḥ pūrvavat kriyākāle kriyāyāstena kiṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: If at the time of action it remains as before, what has been done by it through action?
If the connection is called "its action," which of the two is the basis of that? (6.30)

children.text: evaṃ paravaśaṃ sarvaṃ yadvaśaṃ so 'pi cāvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus everything is dependent on another, and that upon which it depends is itself dependent;
when things are inert like magical creations, toward what should anger arise? (6.31)

children.text: vāraṇāpi na yuktaivaṃ kaḥ kiṃ vārayatīti cet /
children.translated_text: If one objects: "Then even prevention is not justified — who prevents what?" —
it is justified, because through dependent arising, the cessation of suffering is accepted. (6.32)
Therefore, seeing an enemy or even a friend acting unjustly,

children.text: īdṛśāḥ pratyayā asyetyevaṃ matvā sukhī bhavet // SBca_6.33 //
children.translated_text: one should think "such are the conditions that led to this" and remain happy. (6.33)

children.text: yadi tu svecchayā siddhiḥ sarveṣāmeva dehinām /
children.translated_text: If indeed all embodied beings could achieve their wishes by their own will,

children.text: na bhavetkasyacidduḥkhaṃ na duḥkhaṃ kaścidicchati // SBca_6.34 //
children.translated_text: then no one would have suffering, for no one desires suffering. (6.34)
Through carelessness, people hurt themselves with thorns and the like;
through anger, they deprive themselves of food; and through desire for what is hard to obtain, such as women. (6.35)
Some destroy themselves through hanging, leaping from cliffs,
eating poison and unwholesome food, and through sinful conduct. (6.36)
When, under the power of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), they destroy even their own dear selves,

children.text: tadaiṣāṃ parakāyeṣu parihāraḥ kathaṃ bhavet // SBca_6.37 //
children.translated_text: how then could they show restraint toward the bodies of others? (6.37)
Toward those driven mad by the <s>kleśas</s>, who are engaged in self-destruction,

children.text: na kevalaṃ dayā nāsti krodha utpadyate katham // SBca_6.38 //
children.translated_text: not only should one feel compassion — how can anger arise? (6.38)
If it is the nature of the foolish to harm others,

children.text: teṣu kopo na yukto me yathāgnau dahanātmake // SBca_6.39 //
children.translated_text: then anger toward them is unjust, as toward fire whose nature is to burn. (6.39)
