But if this fault is adventitious and beings are by nature gentle,
then anger toward them is equally unjust, as toward the sky for acrid smoke. (6.40)

children.text: mukhyaṃ daṇḍādikaṃ hitvā prerake yadi kupyate /
children.translated_text: If, ignoring the primary cause such as the stick, one is angry at the instigator,

children.text: dveṣeṇa preritaḥ so 'pi dveṣe dveṣo 'stu me varam // SBca_6.41 //
children.translated_text: he too is impelled by hatred — better that my hatred be directed at hatred itself. (6.41)
I too have previously caused such suffering to beings;
therefore it is fitting that this comes to me, who have caused harm to beings. (6.42)

children.text: tacchastraṃ mama kāyaśca dvayaṃ duḥkhasya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Both his weapon and my body are the causes of suffering;

children.text: tena śastraṃ mayā kāyo gṛhītaḥ kutra kupyate // SBca_6.43 //
children.translated_text: he has taken up the weapon, I have taken up the body — at whom should one be angry? (6.43)
This body, shaped like a boil, unable to bear touch, I have grasped;

children.text: tṛṣṇāndhena mayā tatra vyathāyāṃ kutra kupyate // SBca_6.44 //
children.translated_text: blinded by craving — toward whom should one be angry when pain arises? (6.44)
I do not desire suffering, yet I foolishly desire its causes;
when suffering comes through my own fault, why be angry at another? (6.45)
Just as the forest of sword-leaves, just as the birds of hell —

children.text: matkarmajanitā eva tathedaṃ kutra kupyate // SBca_6.46 //
children.translated_text: these too are produced by my own <s>karma</s>; toward what then should anger arise? (6.46)
Impelled by my own <s>karma</s>, those who harm me have arisen;

children.text: yena yāsyanti narakānmayaivāmī hatā nanu // SBca_6.47 //
children.translated_text: if because of this they go to the hells, is it not I who have destroyed them? (6.47)

children.text: etānāśritya me pāpaṃ kṣīyate kṣamato bahu /
children.translated_text: Relying on these, my sin is greatly diminished through patient endurance;

children.text: māmāśritya tu yāntyete narakān dīrghavedanān // SBca_6.48 //
children.translated_text: but relying on me, they go to the hells of long-lasting torment. (6.48)
It is I who harm them, and they who benefit me;
why then, O wicked mind, do you grow angry in perverse fashion? (6.49)
If I do not go to the hells through the merit of my intention,

children.text: eṣāmatra kimāyātaṃ yadyātmā rakṣito mayā // SBca_6.50 //
children.translated_text: what benefit accrues to them if I protect only myself? (6.50)

children.text: atha pratyapakārī syāṃ tathāpyete na rakṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if I were to retaliate, they would still not be protected,

children.text: hīyate cāpi me caryā tasmānnaṣṭāstapasvinaḥ // SBca_6.51 //
children.translated_text: and my practice would be impaired — therefore the ascetics are lost. (6.51)
The mind, being immaterial, cannot be struck by anyone anywhere;
but because of its attachment to the body, the mind is afflicted by suffering. (6.52)
Contempt, harsh words, and disrepute — this group

children.text: kāyaṃ na bādhate tena cetaḥ kasmātprakupyasi // SBca_6.53 //
children.translated_text: does not harm the body; why then, O mind, do you become angry? (6.53)

children.text: mayyaprasādo yo 'nyeṣāṃ sa māṃ kiṃ bhakṣayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: The displeasure of others toward me — will it devour me

children.text: iha janmāntare vāpi yenāsau me 'nabhīpsitaḥ // SBca_6.54 //
children.translated_text: in this life or in another? Why then is it undesired by me? (6.54)
If it is undesired because it obstructs my gains,

children.text: naṅkṣyatīhaiva me lābhaḥ pāpaṃ tu sthāsyati dhruvam // SBca_6.55 //
children.translated_text: my gains will perish in this very life, while sin will remain firmly. (6.55)
Better that I die today than live long through wrong livelihood,

children.text: yasmācciramapi sthitvā mṛtyuduḥkhaṃ tadeva me // SBca_6.56 //
children.translated_text: for even after living long, the suffering of death remains the same for me. (6.56)

children.text: svapne varṣaśataṃ saukhyaṃ bhuktvā yaśca vibudhyate /
children.translated_text: One who enjoys happiness for a hundred years in a dream and then awakens,

children.text: muhūrtamaparo yaśca sukhī bhūtvā vibudhyate // SBca_6.57 //
children.translated_text: and another who enjoys happiness for a moment and then awakens — (6.57)
does not the happiness cease for both upon awakening?
This same analogy applies at the time of death to one who lives long and one who lives briefly. (6.58)

children.text: labdhvāpi ca bahūṃllābhān ciraṃ bhuktvā sukhānyapi /
children.translated_text: Even having obtained many gains and having enjoyed pleasures for a long time,

children.text: riktahastaśca nagnaśca yāsyāmi muṣito yathā // SBca_6.59 //
children.translated_text: I shall depart empty-handed and naked, as if robbed. (6.59)

children.text: pāpakṣayaṃ ca puṇyaṃ ca lābhājjīvan karomi cet /
children.translated_text: If, through gains, I live and accomplish the exhaustion of sin and the accumulation of merit,

children.text: puṇyakṣayaśca pāpaṃ ca lābhārthaṃ krudhyato nanu // SBca_6.60 //
children.translated_text: does not anger for the sake of gains bring exhaustion of merit and accumulation of sin? (6.60)
If the very purpose for which I live is destroyed,
what use is that life which produces nothing but evil? (6.61)
If one says hatred toward the defamer is justified because he destroys beings' faith,

children.text: parāyaśaskare 'pyevaṃ kopaste kiṃ na jāyate // SBca_6.62 //
children.translated_text: then why does your anger not arise equally toward one who defames another? (6.62)
If your tolerance toward the unfavorable is because their displeasure depends on others,
then why is there no tolerance toward the defamer, since it too depends on the arising of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)? (6.63)
And toward those who destroy images, <s>stūpas</s>, and the holy <s>Dharma</s>, and toward revilers —

children.text: na yujyate mama dveṣo buddhādīnāṃ na hi vyathā // SBca_6.64 //
children.translated_text: My hatred is not justified, for the <s>Buddhas</s> and others feel no distress. (6.64)
When harm is done to one's teachers, relatives, and loved ones,
seeing, as before, that it arises from conditions, one should ward off anger. (6.65)
The suffering of embodied beings, caused by both the conscious and the unconscious, is inevitable;

children.text: sā vyathā cetane dṛṣṭā kṣamasvaināṃ vyathāmataḥ // SBca_6.66 //
children.translated_text: that suffering is perceived in conscious beings — therefore, be patient with this suffering. (6.66)
Some offend out of delusion; others, equally deluded, become angry.

children.text: brūmaḥ kameṣu nirdoṣaṃ kaṃ vā brūmo 'parādhinam // SBca_6.67 //
children.translated_text: Whom among these shall we call blameless, and whom shall we call the offender? (6.67)

children.text: kasmādevaṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ yenaivaṃ bādhyase paraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Why did you act as you did before, such that you are now harmed by others?
All are subject to the power of <s>karma</s> (past actions) — who am I to alter this? (6.68)

children.text: evaṃ buddhvā tu puṇyeṣu tathā yatnaṃ karomyaham /
children.translated_text: Having understood this, I shall strive in meritorious deeds,

children.text: yena sarve bhaviṣyanti maitracittāḥ parasparam // SBca_6.69 //
children.translated_text: so that all beings may become friendly-minded toward one another. (6.69)
Just as when a house is on fire, one goes to the neighboring house and
removes the straw and such things to which the fire might spread, (6.70)
so too, when the mind is being consumed by the fire of hatred through attachment,
one should instantly abandon that, out of fear of burning the merit within. (6.71)
If a condemned man is freed by having his hand cut off, is that not fortunate?
If one is freed from the hells by enduring human sufferings, is that not fortunate? (6.72)
If even this much present suffering cannot be endured,
then why is anger — the cause of hellish torment — not restrained? (6.73)
For the sake of anger, I have been tormented thousands of times in the hells,

children.text: kārito 'smi na cātmārthaḥ parārtho vā kṛto mayā // SBca_6.74 //
children.translated_text: yet I have accomplished nothing for myself or for others thereby. (6.74)

children.text: na cedaṃ tādṛśaṃ duḥkhaṃ mahārthaṃ ca kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: This suffering is not so great, and it will accomplish a great purpose;
when facing suffering that removes the suffering of the world, only joy is appropriate here. (6.75)
If others have obtained the pleasure of joy by praising one who is rich in virtues,

children.text: manastvamapi taṃ stutvā kasmādevaṃ na hṛṣyasi // SBca_6.76 //
children.translated_text: why then, O mind, do you not also praise him and rejoice in the same way? (6.76)

children.text: idaṃ ca te hṛṣṭisukhaṃ niravadyaṃ sukhodayam /
children.translated_text: This joy and pleasure of yours would be blameless, a source of happiness,

children.text: na vāritaṃ ca guṇibhiḥ parāvarjanamuttamam // SBca_6.77 //
children.translated_text: not forbidden by the virtuous, and the best means of winning others over. (6.77)

children.text: tasyaiva sukhamityevaṃ tavedaṃ yadi na priyam /
children.translated_text: If you say 'The happiness is his alone' and therefore find no delight in it,
then by ceasing to give wages and the like, both the seen and the unseen rewards would be lost. (6.78)
When your own virtues are being praised, you wish others to be pleased as well,
but when the virtues of another are being praised, you do not wish for your own pleasure. (6.79)
Having generated <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) out of a wish for the happiness of all beings,
why do you now become angry at beings who have found happiness on their own? (6.80)
You profess to wish <s>Buddhahood</s> — worshipped by the three worlds — for all beings,

children.text: satkāramitvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ kiṃ paridahyase // SBca_6.81 //
children.translated_text: so why do you burn with envy when you see them receiving mere temporary honor? (6.81)

children.text: puṣṇāti yastvayā poṣyaṃ tubhyameva dadāti saḥ /
children.translated_text: One who nourishes those whom you ought to nourish is actually giving to you;

children.text: kuṭumbajīvinaṃ labdhvā na hṛṣyasi prakupyasi // SBca_6.82 //
children.translated_text: having found one who supports your family, you do not rejoice but instead grow angry? (6.82)

children.text: sa kiṃ necchasi sattvānāṃ yasteṣāṃ bodhimicchati /
children.translated_text: What does he not wish for beings, he who wishes them <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)?
How can one who is angered at another's good fortune possess <s>bodhicitta</s>? (6.86)

children.text: yadi tena na tallabdhaṃ sthitaṃ dānapatergṛhe /
children.translated_text: If that gift was not obtained by the other person, it remains in the patron's house;

children.text: sarvathāpi na tatte 'sti dattādattena tena kim // SBca_6.84 //
children.translated_text: in any case it is not yours — so what difference does it make whether it is given or not? (6.84)
Should he suppress his merits, his faith, or his own virtues?

children.text: labhamāno na gṛhṇātu vada kena na kupyasi // SBca_6.85 //
children.translated_text: Should one who is receiving not accept? Tell me, with whom are you not angry? (6.85)

children.text: na kevalaṃ tvamātmānaṃ kṛtapāpaṃ na śocasi /
children.translated_text: Not only do you not grieve over yourself, a doer of evil,
but you wish to compete with others who have done meritorious deeds! (6.86)
Even if something unpleasant befalls your enemy, what satisfaction would come to you from that?
Your mere wish alone will not become a cause [of his misfortune]. (6.87)

children.text: atha tvadicchayā siddhaṃ tadduḥkhe kiṃ sukhaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: And even if his suffering were fulfilled through your wish, what happiness would that bring you?

children.text: athāpyartho bhavedevamanarthaḥ ko nvataḥ paraḥ // SBca_6.88 //
children.translated_text: Even if there were some purpose in it, what greater harm could there be than this? (6.88)
For this is the terrible hook cast by the fisherman of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),

children.text: yato narakapālāstvāṃ krītvā pakṣyanti kumbhiṣu // SBca_6.89 //
children.translated_text: by which the guardians of hell will purchase you and cook you in their cauldrons. (6.89)

children.text: stutiryaśo 'tha satkāro na puṇyāya na cāyuṣe /
children.translated_text: Praise, fame, and honor bring neither merit nor longevity to me,

children.text: na balārthaṃ na cārogye na ca kāyasukhāya me // SBca_6.90 //
children.translated_text: neither strength, nor health, nor bodily pleasure. (6.90)
This much would constitute self-interest for a wise person who knows his true benefit;
but one who desires mental pleasure might as well resort to liquor and gambling. (6.91)
For the sake of fame, people squander their wealth and even destroy themselves;

children.text: kimakṣarāṇi bhakṣyāṇi mṛte kasya ca tatsukham // SBca_6.92 //
children.translated_text: are syllables edible? And when one is dead, whose is that pleasure? (6.92)
Just as a child wails in distress when its sand-castle is destroyed,

children.text: tathā stutiyaśohānau svacittaṃ pratibhāti me // SBca_6.93 //
children.translated_text: so too does my mind appear to react when praise and fame are lost. (6.93)
Since sound itself is without consciousness, it is impossible that 'it praises me';

children.text: paraḥ kila mayi prīta ityetatprītikāraṇam // SBca_6.94 //
children.translated_text: rather, the cause of my delight is the thought that 'another is pleased with me.' (6.94)

children.text: anyatra mayi vā prītyā kiṃ hi me parakīyayā /
children.translated_text: But what use is another's affection to me, whether directed at me or at someone else?

children.text: tasyaiva tatprītisukhaṃ bhāgo nālpo 'pi me tataḥ // SBca_6.95 //
children.translated_text: The joy and pleasure of that love belong to that person alone — not even a small share falls to me. (6.95)
If I am happy through the happiness arising from another's love, then let me feel that everywhere;

children.text: kasmādanyaprasādena sukhiteṣu na me sukham // SBca_6.96 //
children.translated_text: why then do I not feel happy when others are made happy by someone else's favor? (6.96)
Thus the pleasure that arises in oneself from thinking 'I am praised'
is, upon reflection, equally baseless — it is merely childish behavior. (6.97)
Praise and such things destroy my spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>),

children.text: guṇavatsu ca mātsaryaṃ saṃpatkopaṃ ca kurvate // SBca_6.98 //
children.translated_text: generate envy toward those with virtues, and produce anger at others' success. (6.98)
Therefore, those who have appeared before me to destroy praise and the like

children.text: apāyapātarakṣārthaṃ pravṛttā nanu te mama // SBca_6.99 //
children.translated_text: are surely engaged in protecting me from falling into the lower realms. (6.99)
For one who seeks liberation, the bondage of gain and honor is unfitting;

children.text: ye mocayanti māṃ bandhāddveṣasteṣu kathaṃ mama // SBca_6.100 //
children.translated_text: those who free me from this bondage — how can I hate them? (6.100)
Those who have become like a door bolted shut for one who wishes to enter suffering —

children.text: buddhādhiṣṭhānata iva dveṣasteṣu kathaṃ mama // SBca_6.101 //
children.translated_text: how can I hate them, as if they were established by the <s>Buddhas</s> themselves? (6.101)
'He has created an obstacle to my merit' — anger here is not justified,

children.text: kṣāntyā samaṃ tapo nāsti nanvetattadupasthitam // SBca_6.102 //
children.translated_text: for there is no <s>tapas</s> (austerity) equal to patience, and is this not precisely the occasion for it? (6.102)
If through my own fault I do not practice patience here,
then it is I who have created the obstacle, when the cause of merit was at hand. (6.103)

children.text: yo hi yena vinā nāsti yasmiṃśca sati vidyate /
children.translated_text: For that which does not exist without a certain thing, and which comes into being when that thing is present —

children.text: sa eva kāraṇaṃ tasya sa kathaṃ vighna ucyate // SBca_6.104 //
children.translated_text: that very thing is its cause; how then can it be called an obstacle? (6.104)
A beggar who appears at the right time does not obstruct generosity,

children.text: na ca pravrājake prāpte pravrajyāvighna ucyate // SBca_6.105 //
children.translated_text: and one who meets a renunciant is not called an obstacle to renunciation. (6.105)
Beggars are easy to find in the world, but those who do harm are rare,
because no one wrongs me when I have committed no wrong. (6.106)
Therefore, like a treasure appearing in one's house without effort,
my enemy is to be cherished, for he is a companion in the practice of <s>bodhicaryā</s> (the conduct of awakening). (6.107)
Since this fruit of patience has been attained by me and by him together,

children.text: etasmai prathamaṃ deyametatpūrvā kṣamā yataḥ // SBca_6.108 //
children.translated_text: to him it should first be given, for he was the prior cause of patience. (6.108)

children.text: kṣamāsiddhyāśayo nāsya tena pūjyo na cedariḥ /
children.translated_text: If the enemy is not to be honored because he lacks the intention to produce patience,
then how is the true <s>Dharma</s>, which is also without intention, honored as a cause of attainment? (6.109)
If the enemy is not to be honored because his intention is to cause harm,

children.text: anyathā me kathaṃ kṣāntirbhiṣajīva hitodyate // SBca_6.110 //
children.translated_text: then how otherwise could my patience arise? — just as medicine that is beneficial [may taste bitter]. (6.110)
Therefore, patience arises in dependence on his hostile intention;

children.text: sa evātaḥ kṣamāhetuḥ pūjyaḥ saddharmavanmayā // SBca_6.111 //
children.translated_text: he alone is thus the cause of patience and should be honored by me, like the true <s>Dharma</s>. (6.111)
For this reason the Sage (<s>Muni</s>) declared that the field of beings is like the field of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones),

children.text: etānārādhya bahavaḥ saṃpatpāraṃ yato gatāḥ // SBca_6.112 //
children.translated_text: for many have gone to the far shore of prosperity by worshipping them. (6.112)
Since the attainment of the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> depends equally on beings and on the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: jineṣu gauravaṃ yadvanna sattveṣviti kaḥ kramaḥ // SBca_6.113 //
children.translated_text: what kind of reasoning is it that pays reverence to the <s>Jinas</s> but not to beings? (6.113)

children.text: āśayasya ca māhātmyaṃ na svataḥ kiṃ tu kāryataḥ /
children.translated_text: The greatness of an intention lies not in itself but in its effects;

children.text: samaṃ ca tena māhātmyaṃ sattvānāṃ tena te samāḥ // SBca_6.114 //
children.translated_text: since the greatness [arising from beings] is equal, beings are therefore equal [to the <s>Jinas</s>]. (6.114)
That which makes the intention of loving-kindness worthy of honor — that is itself the greatness of beings;
that which makes merit arise from devotion to the <s>Buddhas</s> — that is itself the greatness of the <s>Buddhas</s>. (6.115)
Therefore, insofar as beings share in the attainment of the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, they are equal to the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: na tu buddhaiḥ samāḥ kecidanantāṃśairguṇārṇavaiḥ // SBca_6.116 //
children.translated_text: yet none are truly equal to the <s>Buddhas</s>, who are oceans of infinite qualities. (6.116)
If even a tiny fraction of the virtue of those who are the sole repositories of the essence of all virtues

children.text: dṛśyate tasya pūjārthaṃ trailokyamapi na kṣamam // SBca_6.117 //
children.translated_text: were to be seen somewhere, the three worlds would not suffice to honor it. (6.117)
Yet in beings there exists the supreme share that gives rise to the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>;
in proportion to that share, the worship of beings should be performed. (6.118)
Moreover, for those who are genuine friends, benefactors beyond measure,

children.text: sattvārādhanamutsṛjya niṣkṛtiḥ kā parā bhavet // SBca_6.119 //
children.translated_text: what greater recompense could there be than pleasing the beings [they have adopted]? (6.119)

children.text: bhindanti dehaṃ praviśantyavīciṃ yeṣāṃ kṛte tatra kṛte kṛtaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: For those for whose sake they rend their bodies and enter <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell) — by doing good to those very beings, the debt would be repaid;
therefore, even toward great wrongdoers, one should practice only what is wholesome. (6.120)

children.text: svayaṃ mama svāmina eva tāvad yadarthamātmanyapi nirvyapekṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: When my very Lords themselves are, for the sake of beings, indifferent even to their own bodies,

children.text: ahaṃ kathaṃ svāmiṣu teṣu teṣu karomi mānaṃ na tu dāsabhāvam // SBca_6.121 //
children.translated_text: how can I behave with pride toward those same beings who are their masters, rather than adopting the attitude of a servant? (6.121)

children.text: yeṣāṃ sukhe yānti mudaṃ munīndrāḥ yeṣāṃ vyathāyāṃ praviśanti manyum /
children.translated_text: The great sages rejoice in the happiness of beings and are distressed at their suffering;
by pleasing beings, all the great sages are pleased; by harming them, the sages are harmed. (6.122)

children.text: ādīptakāyasya yathā samantān na sarvakāmairapi saumanasyam /
children.translated_text: Just as one whose body is entirely ablaze finds no pleasure in any desirable object,

children.text: sattvavyathāyāmapi tadvadeva na prītyupāyo 'sti dayāmayānām // SBca_6.123 //
children.translated_text: so too, when beings suffer, there is no means of bringing joy to those who are filled with compassion. (6.123)
Therefore, whatever suffering I have inflicted upon the great compassionate ones by causing pain to beings,

children.text: tadadya pāpaṃ pratideśayāmi yatkheditāstanmunayaḥ kṣamantām // SBca_6.124 //
children.translated_text: that sin I now confess; may the sages whom I have grieved forgive me. (6.124)
For the sake of pleasing the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, today with my whole being I enter into servitude to the world;

children.text: kurvantu me mūrghni padaṃ janaughā vighnantu vā tuṣyatu lokanāthaḥ // SBca_6.125 //
children.translated_text: let the masses of people trample upon my head or even slay me — may the Protector of the World be pleased. (6.125)

children.text: ātmīkṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ jagattaiḥ / kṛpātmabhirnaiva hi saṃśayo 'sti /
dṛśyanta ete nanu sattvarūpās ta eva nāthāḥ kimanādaro 'tra // SBca_6.126 //
children.translated_text: are not these beings seen as the very form of those Protectors? Why then this disrespect? (6.126)
Those compassionate ones have made all this world their own — of this there is no doubt;
This alone is the worship of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; this alone is the accomplishment of one's own purpose;
this alone removes the suffering of the world — therefore let this be my vow. (6.127)
Just as a single king's officer may oppress a great multitude,

children.text: vikartuṃ naiva śaknoti dīrghadarśī mahājanaḥ // SBca_6.128 //
children.translated_text: the far-sighted multitude cannot retaliate against him, (6.128)

children.text: yasmānnaiva sa ekākī tasya rājabalaṃ balam /
children.translated_text: because he is not alone — the king's power is his power;

children.text: tathā na durbalaṃ kaṃcidaparāddhaṃ vimānayet // SBca_6.129 //
children.translated_text: so too, one should not despise any weak person who has given offense, (6.129)
for the guardians of hell and the compassionate ones are his allies;
therefore one should propitiate beings as a servant propitiates a wrathful king. (6.130)
What could an angry king do that would equal the suffering of hell
which is experienced as a result of causing displeasure to beings? (6.131)
What could a pleased king bestow that would equal <s>Buddhahood</s>
which is experienced as a result of bringing joy to beings? (6.132)
Setting aside the future <s>Buddhahood</s> that arises from pleasing beings,

children.text: ihaiva saubhāgyayaśaḥsausthityaṃ kiṃ na paśyasi // SBca_6.133 //
children.translated_text: do you not see even in this very life the fruits of good fortune, fame, and well-being? (6.133)
Beauty, health, joy, long life,

children.text: cakravartisukhaṃ sphītaṃ kṣamī prāpnoti saṃsaran // SBca_6.134 //
children.translated_text: and the abundant happiness of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) — the patient one attains all these while still in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth). (6.134)

children.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitā nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, entitled <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Patience), in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.
Chapter Seven: <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Vigor).

children.text: evaṃ kṣamo bhajedvīryaṃ vīrye bodhiryataḥ sthitā /
children.translated_text: Having thus cultivated patience, one should exert vigor, for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is established in vigor.

children.text: na hi vīryaṃ vinā puṇyaṃ yathā vāyuṃ vināgatiḥ // SBca_7.1 //
children.translated_text: For without <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), there is no merit, just as without wind there is no movement. [7.1]
What is <s>vīrya</s>? Zeal for the wholesome. What is said to be its opposite?
<s>Ālasya</s> (laziness) — attachment to the contemptible, despondency, and self-denigration. [7.2]
Through relishing the pleasure of inactivity, craving for sleep, and longing for shelter,
through having no weariness of the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, laziness arises. [7.3]
Sniffed out by the hunters' net of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), having entered the trap of births —
do you still not know that you have entered the jaws of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death)? [7.4]
Do you not see that those of your own kind are being slain one by one?

children.text: tathāpi nidrāṃ yāsyeva caṇḍālamahiṣo yathā // SBca_7.5 //
children.translated_text: Yet still you go on sleeping, like a buffalo before the butcher! [7.5]
When <s>Yama</s> (Death) is watching you, when your path is blocked on all sides,

children.text: kathaṃ te rocate bhoktuṃ kathaṃ nidrā kathaṃ ratiḥ // SBca_7.6 //
children.translated_text: how can you delight in eating? How in sleep? How in pleasure? [7.6]
Death will come swiftly, having gathered its provisions;
even if you cast off laziness then, at that untimely hour, what will you do? [7.7]
"This is not yet attained, this is just begun, this stands half-done" —
suddenly death has arrived — "Alas, I am destroyed!" — so thinking, [7.8]
seeing the faces of your kinsmen, with eyes tearful and red, swollen with the rush of grief,
despairing — and seeing also the faces of <s>Yama</s>'s messengers, [7.9]
tormented by the recollection of your own sins, hearing the screams of the hells,
your body smeared with the excrement of terror, helpless — what will you do? [7.10]
"I am like a live fish" — such fear is fitting for you even here;
how much more so, having committed sins, from the intense sufferings of the hells! [7.11]
O tender one, you are scorched even when touched by hot water;

children.text: kṛtvā ca nārakaṃ karma kimevaṃ svasthamāsyate // SBca_7.12 //
children.translated_text: having done deeds leading to hell, how can you remain at ease thus? [7.12]
Without effort yet expecting results, O tender one of much suffering,
seized by death yet behaving as if immortal — alas, wretched one, you are being destroyed! [7.13]
Having found the boat of human birth, cross the great river of suffering!

children.text: mūḍha kālo na nidrāyā iyaṃ naurdurlabhā punaḥ // SBca_7.14 //
children.translated_text: O fool, this is not the time for sleep — this boat is hard to find again! [7.14]
Having abandoned the supreme delight in the <s>Dharma</s>, the unending stream of joy,
how can you find pleasure in excitement, laughter, and the like — causes of suffering? [7.15]
Non-despondency, the marshalling of forces, earnestness, self-mastery,
the equality of self and others, and the exchange of self and others — [7.16]
One should not despair, thinking "How shall I attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)?"
For the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), the speaker of truth, has truly spoken thus: [7.17]
Even gadflies, gnats, mosquitoes, and worms
have, by the power of their effort, attained the supreme and hard-to-reach <s>bodhi</s>. [7.18]

children.text: kimutāhaṃ naro jātyā śakto jñātuṃ hitāhitam /
children.translated_text: How much more I, born as a human being, capable of knowing what is beneficial and harmful —
not abandoning the way of the Omniscient One, why should I not attain <s>bodhi</s>? [7.19]
But if I have fear, thinking "hands, feet, and the like must be given up" —
that would be my confusion about what is weighty and what is light, born from lack of discernment. [7.20]
I shall be cut, split, burned, and torn apart, many times over,
for countless millions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) — and yet <s>bodhi</s> will not come to be. [7.21]

children.text: idaṃ tu me parimitaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃbodhisādhanam /
children.translated_text: But this limited suffering of mine leads to <s>saṃbodhi</s> (full awakening),
like the pain of the procedure that removes the suffering of a lodged splinter. [7.22]
All physicians bring about freedom from disease through painful treatments;
therefore, to destroy many sufferings, a small one must be endured. [7.23]
The supreme physician has not even given this customary treatment,
but cures the gravely ill with the gentlest of remedies. [7.24]
The Guide first directs one to the giving of vegetables and the like;
then gradually, one comes to relinquish even one's own flesh. [7.25]
When understanding arises regarding one's own flesh as if it were vegetables,

children.text: māṃsāsthi tyajatastasya tadā kiṃ nāma duṣkaram // SBca_7.26 //
children.translated_text: then for one who gives up flesh and bone, what indeed is difficult? [7.26]
Not suffering, because sins have been abandoned; not dejected, because of wisdom —

children.text: mithyākalpanayā citte pāpātkāye yato vyathā // SBca_7.27 //
children.translated_text: for it is from false conceptualization that there is suffering of the mind, and from sin that there is suffering of the body. [7.27]

children.text: puṇyena kāyaḥ sukhitaḥ pāṇḍityena manaḥ sukhi /
children.translated_text: By merit the body is made happy; by wisdom the mind is happy;

children.text: tiṣṭhan parārthaṃ saṃsāre kṛpāluḥ kena khidyate // SBca_7.28 //
children.translated_text: remaining in <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of others, how is the compassionate one wearied? [7.28]
Exhausting former sins and receiving oceans of merit,
by the power of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) alone, one advances faster even than the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers). [7.29]
Thus going from happiness to happiness, who that is conscious would despair,
having mounted the chariot of <s>bodhicitta</s>, which removes all weariness and fatigue? [7.30]
The forces of aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), steadfastness (<s>sthāman</s>), joy (<s>rati</s>), and letting go (<s>mukti</s>) are for the accomplishment of the welfare of beings.
One should cultivate aspiration out of fear of suffering and by contemplating its benefits. [7.31]
Thus, having uprooted the opposing forces, one should strive to increase vigor
through the forces of aspiration, pride, joy, letting go, earnestness, and self-mastery. [7.32]
Immeasurable are the faults to be destroyed, of myself and of others;

children.text: ekaikasyāpi doṣasya yatra kalpārṇavaiḥ kṣayaḥ // SBca_7.33 //
children.translated_text: where the exhaustion of even a single fault requires oceans of <s>kalpas</s>. [7.33]
And yet, not even a trace of effort for the exhaustion of faults is seen in me;

children.text: aprameyavyathābhājye noraḥ sphuṭati me katham // SBca_7.34 //
children.translated_text: how does my heart not burst, being the vessel of immeasurable suffering? [7.34]
Many virtues are to be cultivated by me, for myself and for others;
and the practice of even a single virtue may or may not take oceans of <s>kalpas</s>. [7.35]
Not even the slightest practice of virtue has ever arisen in me;

children.text: vṛthā nītaṃ mayā janma kathaṃcillabdhamadbhutam // SBca_7.36 //
children.translated_text: I have wasted this life of mine, somehow wondrously obtained! [7.36]
I have not experienced the joy of the great festival of worshipping the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One);

children.text: na kṛtā śāsane kārā daridrāśā na pūritā // SBca_7.37 //
children.translated_text: I have not served the teaching; I have not fulfilled the hopes of the poor. [7.37]

children.text: bhītebhyo nābhayaṃ dattamārtā na sukhinaḥ kṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: I have not given fearlessness to the frightened; I have not made the afflicted happy;
I have served only as a lance of pain in my mother's womb, for suffering alone. [7.38]
From my former separation from aspiration toward the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: vipattirīdṛśī jātā ko dharme chandamutsṛjet // SBca_7.39 //
children.translated_text: such misfortune has now arisen — who would abandon aspiration toward the <s>Dharma</s>? [7.39]

children.text: kuśalānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ chandaṃ mūlaṃ munirjagau /
children.translated_text: The Sage has declared aspiration to be the root of all wholesome states;
and its root, in turn, is the constant contemplation of the fruits of ripening. [7.40]
Sufferings, mental anguish, and various fears,
and the frustration of desires — these arise for doers of evil. [7.41]
Wherever the heart's desire of the doer of good goes,
there, by the merit of that [good deed], one is honored with the reward of its fruit. [7.42]
But wherever the desire for happiness of the evil-doer goes,
there, by those very sins, one is struck down with the weapons of suffering. [7.43]
Having entered the womb of a vast, fragrant, cool lotus,
their radiance increased by nourishment from the sweet voice of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor),
their beautiful bodies emerging from lotuses opened by the hand of the Sage —

children.text: sugatasutā bhavanti sugatasya puraḥ kuśalaiḥ // SBca_7.44 //
children.translated_text: the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) come into being before the <s>Sugata</s>, through their wholesome deeds. [7.44]
Stripped of all skin by the servants of <s>Yama</s>, crying out in agony,
the body drenched with molten copper fleeing from the heat of fire,
the slabs of flesh sliced apart by hundreds of blows from blazing swords and spears —
one falls repeatedly upon the burning iron ground, through unwholesome deeds. [7.45]
Therefore, aspiration for the wholesome should be cultivated, contemplating thus with care;
then, by the method set forth in the <s>Vajradhvaja</s> [Sūtra], one should cultivate pride. [7.46]
First, having examined one's resources, one should begin or not begin;

children.text: anārambho varaṃ nāma na tvārabhya nivartanam // SBca_7.47 //
children.translated_text: it is better not to begin at all than to begin and then turn back. [7.47]
In another life too, that habit [of abandoning] grows, and suffering from sin [grows];

children.text: anyacca kāryakālaṃ ca hīnaṃ tacca na sādhitam // SBca_7.48 //
children.translated_text: and another [opportunity for] action and its time is lost, and that [task] is not accomplished. [7.48]
Pride should be applied in three [areas]: action, the afflictions, and one's own power.
"This is to be done by me alone" — this is pride regarding action. [7.49]
This world, subject to the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), is incapable of accomplishing its own welfare;

children.text: tasmānmayaiṣāṃ kartavyaṃ nāśakto 'haṃ yathā janaḥ // SBca_7.50 //
children.translated_text: therefore I must act for them, for I am not powerless like [ordinary] people. [7.50]

children.text: nīcaṃ karma karotyanyaḥ kathaṃ mayyapi tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: When another does a lowly task, how can I just stand by?

children.text: mānāccenna karomyetanmāno naśyatu me varam // SBca_7.51 //
children.translated_text: If I do not do it out of pride, better that my pride perish! [7.51]
Even a crow acts like <s>Garuḍa</s> when it comes upon a dead snake;

children.text: āpadābādhate 'lpāpi mano me yadi durbalam // SBca_7.52 //
children.translated_text: if my mind is weak, even a slight misfortune will overwhelm me. [7.52]
When one is rendered inactive by despondency, misfortunes are surely easy [to befall];
but one who rises up and strives is unconquerable even by the great. [7.53]
Therefore, with firm mind, I shall overcome misfortune by [attacking] misfortune itself;
for if I am defeated, my aspiration to conquer the three worlds would be laughable! [7.54]

children.text: mayā hi sarvaṃ jetavyamahaṃ jeyo na kenacit /
children.translated_text: For all is to be conquered by me — I am not to be conquered by anything!

children.text: mayaiṣa māno voḍhavyo jinasiṃhasuto hyaham // SBca_7.55 //
children.translated_text: This pride must I bear, for I am a son of the Lion of the <s>Jinas</s>! [7.55]

children.text: ye sattvā mānavijitā varakāste na māninaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those beings who are conquered by [false] pride are wretched — they are not [truly] proud;

children.text: mānī śatruvaśaṃ naiti mānaśatruvaśāśca te // SBca_7.56 //
children.translated_text: the [truly] proud one does not fall under the power of the enemy, while those are under the power of the enemy, pride [i.e., conceit]. [7.56]
Led by [false] pride to the lower realms, deprived of joy even in human birth,

children.text: parapiṇḍāśino dāsā mūrkhā durdarśanāḥ kṛśā // SBca_7.57 //
children.translated_text: eating the food of others, slaves, fools, ugly, and emaciated — [7.57]
despised by all, yet stiff with pride, the wretched ones —

children.text: te 'pi cenmānināṃ madhye dīnāstu vada kīdṛśāḥ // SBca_7.58 //
children.translated_text: if they too are counted among the proud, tell me, what are the pitiable like? [7.58]

children.text: te mānino vijayinaśca ta eva śūrā ye mānaśatruvijayāya vahanti mānam /
children.translated_text: Those are [truly] proud, those are victorious, those are heroes, who bear pride for the conquest of the enemy that is [false] pride;

children.text: ye taṃ sphurantamapi mānaripuṃ nihatya kāmaṃ jane jayaphalaṃ pratipādayanti // SBca_7.59 //
children.translated_text: who, having slain the swelling enemy of [false] pride, freely bestow the fruits of victory upon beings. [7.59]
Standing amidst the host of afflictions, one should be a thousandfold defiant,
unconquerable by the hosts of <s>kleśas</s>, like a lion among herds of deer. [7.60]

children.text: mahatsvapi hi kṛcchreṣu na rasaṃ cakṣurīkṣate /
children.translated_text: For even in great difficulties, the eye does not perceive a taste;

children.text: evaṃ kṛcchramapi prāpya na kleśavaśago bhavet // SBca_7.61 //
children.translated_text: likewise, even when encountering hardship, one should not fall under the power of the <s>kleśas</s>. [7.61]
Whatever task one undertakes, one should become absorbed in that very task,
intoxicated with that work, insatiable in spirit — like one desiring the pleasure of a game's reward. [7.62]

children.text: sukhārthaṃ kriyate karma tathāpi syānna vā sukham /
children.translated_text: Actions are done for the sake of happiness, yet happiness may or may not result;

children.text: karmaiva tu sukhaṃ yasya niṣkarmā sa sukhī katham // SBca_7.63 //
children.translated_text: but for one whose happiness is in the action itself, how can one be happy without action? [7.63]
In <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is no satisfaction from sense pleasures, which are like honey on a razor's edge;
how then can there be satisfaction from the nectar of merits, sweet in their ripening, auspicious? [7.64]
Therefore, even at the completion of a task, one should plunge into the next task,

children.text: yathā madhyāhnasaṃtapta ādau prāptasarāḥ karī // SBca_7.65 //
children.translated_text: as an elephant, scorched by the midday sun, straightaway enters a lake it has reached. [7.65]
But when one's strength is failing, one should set [the task] aside to do again later;
and when well completed, one should let it go, with longing for what follows next. [7.66]
One should guard against the blows of the <s>kleśas</s>, and strike back at the <s>kleśas</s> firmly,
as if engaged in a sword fight with a skilled adversary. [7.67]
Just as one would seize a fallen sword in haste, with fear,

children.text: smṛtikhaḍgaṃ tathā bhraṣṭaṃ gṛhṇīyānnarakān smaran // SBca_7.68 //
children.translated_text: so too, when the sword of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) has fallen, one should seize it back, remembering the hells. [7.68]
Just as poison, reaching the blood, spreads through the body,
so too, a fault, finding an opening, spreads through the mind. [7.69]
Like one carrying a vessel full of oil, watched over by sword-bearing men,
who, from fear of death should he stumble, is utterly attentive — so too should the vow-keeper be. [7.70]
Therefore, just as one rises quickly when a snake falls into one's lap,
so too, when drowsiness and laziness approach, one should swiftly counteract them. [7.71]
At each and every lapse, having thoroughly reproached oneself, one should reflect:

children.text: kathaṃ karomi yenedaṃ punarme na bhavediti // SBca_7.72 //
children.translated_text: "What shall I do so that this may never happen to me again?" [7.72]
For this reason, one should seek out companions or tasks [to encounter],
[thinking:] "How may the practice of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) come about in such situations?" [7.73]
One should make oneself light [i.e., alert], remembering the discourse on heedfulness,

children.text: karmāgamādyathā pūrvaṃ sajjaḥ sarvatra vartate // SBca_7.74 //
children.translated_text: so that, before the arrival of a task, one is always prepared beforehand. [7.74]
Just as a tuft of cotton is subject to the coming and going of the wind,
Thus one should come under the power of vigor, and in this way <s>ṛddhi</s> (spiritual accomplishment) too flourishes. // 7.75 //

children.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ vīryapāramitā nāma saptamaḥ paricchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter, called the Perfection of Vigor (<s>Vīryapāramitā</s>), in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.
Chapter 8: The Perfection of Meditation (<s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>).
Having thus strengthened vigor, one should establish the mind in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption),
for a person whose mind is distracted dwells between the fangs of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). // 8.1 //
Through the seclusion of body and mind, distraction does not arise;
therefore, abandoning the world, one should relinquish discursive thoughts. // 8.2 //

children.text: snehānna tyajyate loko lābhādiṣu ca tṛṣṇayā /
children.translated_text: The world is not abandoned because of attachment, and because of craving for gain and the like;
therefore, in order to abandon these, the wise person should reflect as follows. // 8.3 //
Knowing that <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), well-endowed with <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), destroys the <s>kleśas</s>,

children.text: śamathaḥ prathamaṃ gaveṣaṇīyaḥ sa ca loke nirapekṣayābhiratyā // SBca_8.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>śamatha</s> should be sought first; and that is [attained] through delight in detachment from the world. // 8.4 //
How can attachment arise in one who is impermanent, toward those who are impermanent?

children.text: yena janmasahasrāṇi draṣṭavyo na punaḥ priyaḥ // SBca_8.5 //
children.translated_text: One by whom the beloved will not be seen again for thousands of births. // 8.5 //

children.text: apaśyannaratiṃ yāti samādhau na ca tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: Not seeing [the beloved], one fails to find delight, and the mind does not settle in <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: na ca tṛpyati dṛṣṭvāpi pūrvavadbādhyate tṛṣā // SBca_8.6 //
children.translated_text: and even upon seeing [the beloved], one is not satisfied — one is tormented by craving as before. // 8.6 //
One does not see reality as it truly is, and one falls away from spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>);
one is consumed by grief, by the longing for union with the beloved. // 8.7 //
By thinking of that [beloved] again and again, this brief life passes in vain;

children.text: aśāśvatena dharmeṇa dharmo bhraśyati śāśvataḥ // SBca_8.8 //
children.translated_text: the eternal <s>Dharma</s> is lost on account of what is impermanent. // 8.8 //
One who keeps the company of fools surely goes to a bad destination;

children.text: neṣyate viṣabhāgaśca kiṃ prāptaṃ bālasaṃgamāt // SBca_8.9 //
children.translated_text: and one is led to what is unwholesome — what is gained from the company of fools? // 8.9 //
In an instant they become friends, in an instant they become enemies;
they grow angry even at what should please them — ordinary people are hard to satisfy. // 8.10 //

children.text: hitamuktāḥ prakupyanti vārayanti ca māṃ hitāt /
children.translated_text: When told what is beneficial, they grow angry and prevent me from what is wholesome;

children.text: atha na śrūyate teṣāṃ kupitā yānti durgatim // SBca_8.11 //
children.translated_text: and if they are not heeded, they grow angry and go to a bad destination. // 8.11 //
Envy toward a superior, rivalry with an equal, arrogance toward an inferior, pride from praise,
hostility from blame — when would there ever be benefit from a fool? // 8.12 //
Self-aggrandizement, disparaging others, talk delighting in <s>saṃsāra</s> —
some such unwholesome thing inevitably [arises] between one fool and another. // 8.13 //
Thus, through association with the other, there arises a convergence of calamities for both;
I shall dwell alone, with a happy and untroubled mind. // 8.14 //
One should flee far from the fool; when encountered, one should please them with kindly gestures,
not through the bond of familiarity, but like a good person who remains indifferent. // 8.15 //
Taking only what serves the <s>Dharma</s>, like a bee [taking] honey from a flower,
I shall dwell everywhere as if unknown, without intimacy. // 8.16 //
'I have gains, and I am honored, and many desire me' —
such [thoughts] in one who is mortal, as death approaches, give rise to fear. // 8.17 //

children.text: yatra yatra ratiṃ yāti manaḥ sukhavimohitam /
children.translated_text: Whatever the mind, deluded by pleasure, takes delight in,
that very thing, multiplied a thousandfold, returns as suffering. // 8.18 //
Therefore the wise person should not desire that [pleasure]; for from desire arises fear;

children.text: svayameva ca yātyetaddhairyaṃ kṛtvā pratīkṣatām // SBca_8.19 //
children.translated_text: and this [pleasure] passes away of its own accord — let one wait with fortitude! // 8.19 //
Many have had gains, and many have had fame;

children.text: saha lābhayaśobhiste na jñātāḥ kva gatā iti // SBca_8.20 //
children.translated_text: but where they have gone, together with their gains and fame, no one knows. // 8.20 //
If others despise me, why should I be delighted when praised?

children.text: māmevānye praśaṃsanti kiṃ viṣīdāmi ninditaḥ // SBca_8.21 //
children.translated_text: If others praise me, why should I be dejected when blamed? // 8.21 //
Beings of various dispositions have not been satisfied even by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors);
how much less by the ignorant like me — so what use is concern about the world? // 8.22 //
They disparage one who lacks gains, and they speak ill of one who has gains;

children.text: prakṛtyā duḥkhasaṃvāsaiḥ kathaṃ tairjāyate ratiḥ // SBca_8.23 //
children.translated_text: how can delight arise from those whose very nature makes them painful to live with? // 8.23 //
The <s>Tathāgatas</s> have declared that a fool is no one's friend,

children.text: na svārthena vinā prītiryasmādbālasya jāyate // SBca_8.24 //
children.translated_text: because the fool's affection does not arise without self-interest. // 8.24 //
That affection which comes through the door of self-interest is merely affection for oneself;

children.text: dravyanāśe yathodvegaḥ sukhahānikṛto hi saḥ // SBca_8.25 //
children.translated_text: just as distress at the loss of property is [really] caused by the loss of [one's own] pleasure. // 8.25 //

children.text: kadā taiḥ sukhasaṃvāsaiḥ saha vāso bhavenmama // SBca_8.26 //
children.translated_text: when shall I dwell together with those who are pleasant to live with? // 8.26 //
Trees do not disparage, and they need not be won over with effort;
Dwelling in an empty temple, at the foot of a tree, or in caves,
when shall I go forth without attachment, not looking back? // 8.27 //
In places that belong to no one, naturally spacious,
wandering freely, with the sky as my dwelling — when shall I dwell thus? // 8.28 //
Possessing only an earthen bowl, wearing robes not coveted by thieves,
when shall I dwell fearlessly, not concealing my body? // 8.29 //
Going to my own body's charnel ground, with other skeletons,
when shall I compare my own body, subject to decay, [with them]? // 8.30 //

children.text: ayameva hi kāyo me evaṃ pūtirbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: For this very body of mine will become so putrid
that even jackals will not approach it because of its stench. // 8.31 //
Even the bone-fragments born together with this single body

children.text: pṛthak pṛthaggamiṣyanti kimutānyaḥ priyo janaḥ // SBca_8.32 //
children.translated_text: will each go their separate ways — how much more so other dear ones? // 8.32 //

children.text: eka utpadyate janturmriyate caika eva hi /
children.translated_text: A being is born alone and dies alone;
no other shares in that suffering — what use are dear ones who create obstacles? // 8.33 //
Just as one who has set out on a journey takes lodging [along the way],
so one traveling the road of existence takes lodging at each birth. // 8.34 //
Before one is borne away by four men [on a bier],

children.text: āśocyamāno lokena tāvadeva vanaṃ vrajet // SBca_8.35 //
children.translated_text: while the world still mourns, one should depart for the forest. // 8.35 //
Without intimacy and without enmity, alone in body,

children.text: purvameva mṛto loke mriyamāṇo na śocati // SBca_8.36 //
children.translated_text: already dead to the world [in a sense], one who is dying does not grieve. // 8.36 //
And no bystanders cause pain by their mourning,

children.text: buddhādyanusmṛtiṃ cāsya vikṣipanti na kecana // SBca_8.37 //
children.translated_text: and no one distracts one from the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> and so forth. // 8.37 //
Therefore, delightful solitude, free from toil, the source of well-being,
which stills all distractions, should always be cultivated by me. // 8.38 //
Freed from all other thoughts, with the mind focused single-pointedly on my own mind,

children.text: samādhānāya cittasya prayatiṣye damāya ca // SBca_8.39 //
children.translated_text: I shall strive for the settling and taming of the mind. // 8.39 //

children.text: kāmā hyanarthajanakā iha loke paratra ca /
children.translated_text: For desires produce calamities in this world and the next —
in this world, imprisonment, slaughter, and ruin; in the next, the hells and so forth. // 8.40 //
For the sake of which, with folded hands, again and again, [one begged] through messengers and go-betweens;

children.text: na ca pāpamakīrtirvā yadarthaṃ gaṇitā purā // SBca_8.41 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of which, neither sin nor infamy was previously taken into account — // 8.41 //
one cast oneself into danger, and one's wealth was squandered;
and those very ones, the embracing of whom brought supreme delight — // 8.42 //
those are nothing but bones, belonging to no one, ownerless;

children.text: prakāmaṃ saṃpariṣvajya kiṃ na gacchasi nirvṛtim // SBca_8.43 //
children.translated_text: why do you not go to bliss by embracing them fully? // 8.43 //
That face which, with effort, was raised upward, or lowered in modesty,

children.text: purā dṛṣṭamadṛṣṭaṃ vā mukhaṃ jālikayāvṛtam // SBca_8.44 //
children.translated_text: whether seen before or unseen, [now] covered by a veil — // 8.44 //
that face, as if unable to bear your torment, has now
been laid bare by vultures — look! Why do you flee now? // 8.45 //
That which was guarded even from the glances of others,

children.text: tadadya bhakṣitaṃ yāvat kimīrṣyālo na rakṣasi // SBca_8.46 //
children.translated_text: is now being consumed — O jealous one, why do you not guard it? // 8.46 //
Seeing this heap of flesh being devoured by vultures and others,
do you worship the food of others with garlands, sandalwood, and ornaments? // 8.47 //
You are frightened even by a motionless skeleton, seen in this way;

children.text: vetāleneva kenāpi cālyamānādbhayaṃ na kim // SBca_8.48 //
children.translated_text: why are you not afraid of one that moves about, as if animated by a <s>vetāla</s> (zombie-spirit)? // 8.48 //
From a single source of food, both saliva and filth are produced;

children.text: tatrāmedhyamaniṣṭaṃ te lālāpānaṃ kathaṃ priyam // SBca_8.49 //
children.translated_text: if filth is undesired by you, how is drinking the saliva pleasing? // 8.49 //
Those deluded by impurity do not delight in cotton-stuffed pillows, soft to the touch,
[saying] 'They do not emit a bad smell' — the lustful, deluded by impurity! // 8.50 //
If you have desire even when [the body] is covered, why is the uncovered [body] not displeasing?

children.text: na cetprayojanaṃ tena kasmācchannaṃ vimṛdyate // SBca_8.51 //
children.translated_text: If you have no use for it [uncovered], why do you caress what is covered? // 8.51 //
If you have no desire for what is impure, why do you embrace another —
a cage of bones bound by sinews, smeared with a mud of flesh? // 8.52 //
You yourself have plenty of filth — satisfy yourself with that;
O devourer of excrement, forget the other bag of filth! // 8.53 //
'I am fond of the flesh' — you wish to see and touch it;

children.text: acetanaṃ svabhāvena māṃsaṃ tvaṃ kathamicchasi // SBca_8.54 //
children.translated_text: but that flesh is by nature devoid of consciousness — how can you desire it? // 8.54 //

children.text: yadicchasi na taccittaṃ draṣṭuṃ spraṣṭuṃ ca śakyate /
children.translated_text: That mind which you desire can be neither seen nor touched;

children.text: yacca śakyaṃ na tadvetti kiṃ tadāliṅgase mudhā // SBca_8.55 //
children.translated_text: and that which can [be seen and touched] is not conscious — why then do you embrace it in vain? // 8.55 //
That you do not recognize another's body as made of filth is not surprising;

children.text: svāmedhyamayameva tvaṃ taṃ nāvaiṣīti vismayaḥ // SBca_8.56 //
children.translated_text: but that you do not recognize your own as made of filth — that is astonishing! // 8.56 //
Leaving aside the young lotus, opened by the rays of the cloudless sun,
what delight is there in a cage of excrement for a mind addicted to filth? // 8.57 //
If you do not wish to touch earth and other things smeared with filth,
how do you wish to touch the body from which that [filth] has come? // 8.58 //

children.text: yadi te nāśucau rāgaḥ kasmādāliṅgase param /
children.translated_text: If you have no desire for what is impure, why do you embrace another,
born from a field of filth, its seed nourished by that [filth]? // 8.59 //
Because it is small, you do not desire an impure worm born from filth;
yet you desire a body, largely made of filth, also born from filth! // 8.60 //
Not only do you not feel disgust at your own impurity,
but, O devourer of excrement, you crave others who are vessels of impurity! // 8.61 //
Even delightful things such as camphor, or rice with curry —
once cast into the mouth and spat out, even the ground is considered impure. // 8.62 //
If, even though this impurity is obvious, you do not believe it,

children.text: śmaśāne patitān ghorān kāyān paśyāparānapi // SBca_8.63 //
children.translated_text: then look at the dreadful bodies of others, fallen in the charnel ground! // 8.63 //
Since great fear arises when the skin is torn off,

children.text: kathaṃ jñātvāpi tatraiva punarutpadyate ratiḥ // SBca_8.64 //
children.translated_text: how can desire arise again in that very [body], even knowing [its nature]? // 8.64 //
That fragrance applied to the body comes from sandalwood alone, not from anything else;
why are you attracted to something else by a fragrance that belongs to another? // 8.65 //
If natural foul-smelling [keeps] desire away, that is indeed beneficial;
why does the world, delighting in what is harmful, anoint it with fragrance? // 8.66 //
If the sandalwood is fragrant, what has it to do with the body?
Why is one attracted to something else by a fragrance belonging to another? // 8.67 //
If with long hair and nails, with teeth dirty and yellowish,
bearing a coat of grime, naked — the body is terrifying by nature — // 8.68 //
why is it adorned with such effort, like a weapon for self-destruction?
The earth is overrun by madmen, busy in the effort to delude themselves! // 8.69 //

children.text: kaṅkālān katiciddṛṣṭvā śmaśāne kila te ghṛṇā /
children.translated_text: Having seen a few skeletons in the charnel ground, you felt revulsion;
yet you delight in the village charnel ground, swarming with walking skeletons! // 8.70 //
Moreover, this impure thing is not obtained without a price;
for its sake, there is the toil of earning and the anguish of the hells and so forth. // 8.71 //
A child has no means to earn; with what [right] is he happy in youth?

children.text: yātyarjanena tāruṇyaṃ vṛddhaḥ kāmaiḥ karoti kim // SBca_8.72 //
children.translated_text: Youth passes in earning; and what can an old person do with desires? // 8.72 //
Some wretched sensualists, exhausted by the labors of the day,

children.text: gṛhamāgatya sāyāhne śerate sma mṛtā iva // SBca_8.73 //
children.translated_text: come home in the evening and lie there like the dead. // 8.73 //
Others, afflicted by the misery and hardships of military campaigns and foreign travel,
do not see their children and wives for years, though they long for them. // 8.74 //
That very thing for which the self was sold by those deluded by desire —

children.text: tanna prāptaṃ mudhaivāyurnītaṃ tu parakarmaṇā // SBca_8.75 //
children.translated_text: that was not obtained, and life was spent in vain, performing the work of others. [8.75]
Women of others give birth — those who have sold their own being,
who are forever running errands — in forest thickets and the like. [8.76]
They enter battle, risking their lives, just to survive,

children.text: mānārthaṃ dāsatāṃ yānti mūḍhāḥ kāmaviḍambitāḥ // SBca_8.77 //
children.translated_text: and for the sake of honor they go into servitude — fools mocked by desire! [8.77]
Some lovers are cut down, others are impaled upon stakes;
they are seen being burned and being killed with spears. [8.78]
Through the sorrows of gaining, guarding, and losing — know wealth to be an endless misfortune!
Those whose minds are attached to riches have no opportunity for liberation from the suffering of existence. [8.79]
Thus the miseries of the desirous are great, while their pleasures are small —
like the mouthful of grass snatched by the ox as it pulls the cart. [8.80]
For the sake of that mere morsel of pleasure, which even an animal can obtain without difficulty,
this precious opportunity of a human life, so rare to find, is destroyed by those stricken by fate! [8.81]
For the sake of this body, which must inevitably perish and is of little value, destined to fall into hells and the like,

children.text: kāyasyārthe kṛto yo 'yaṃ sarvakālaṃ pariśramaḥ // SBca_8.82 //
children.translated_text: all this toil has been undertaken for all time. [8.82]
With even a hundred-millionth fraction of that effort, <s>Buddhahood</s> could be attained.

children.text: caryāduḥkhānmahadduḥkhaṃ sā ca bodhirna kāminām // SBca_8.83 //
children.translated_text: The suffering of the path of desire is greater than the suffering of the bodhisattva's practice, and yet awakening is not for the desirous. [8.83]

children.text: na śastraṃ na viṣaṃ nāgnirna prapāto na vairiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither weapons, nor poison, nor fire, nor precipices, nor enemies
can compare with desires, when one recalls the sufferings of the hells and the like. [8.84]
Thus, becoming disenchanted with desires, one should generate delight in solitude —
in peaceful forest lands, free from quarrels and toils. [8.85]
The fortunate ones walk upon delightful, broad slabs of rock, cooled by moonbeams and sandalwood,

children.text: niḥśabdasaumyavanamārutavījyamānaiḥ caṃkramyate parahitāya vicintyate ca // SBca_8.86 //
children.translated_text: fanned by the silent, gentle forest breezes, contemplating the welfare of others. [8.86]

children.text: vihṛtya yatra kvacidiṣṭakālaṃ śūnyālaye vṛkṣatale guhāsu /
children.translated_text: Dwelling for as long as one wishes in empty abodes, at the foot of trees, in caves,
freed from the weariness of guarding possessions, one wanders as one pleases, without attachment. [8.87]
Living freely, dwelling without fixed abode, bound to no one —
the happiness of contentment that one enjoys is difficult even for <s>Indra</s> to obtain. [8.88]
By contemplating the virtues of solitude in such ways and the like,

children.text: upaśāntavitarkaḥ san bodhicittaṃ tu bhāvayet // SBca_8.89 //
children.translated_text: having stilled discursive thoughts, one should cultivate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). [8.89]
First, one should diligently cultivate the equality of self and others thus:
'All beings have equal suffering and happiness; I should protect them as I protect myself.' [8.90]
Just as the body, though manifold with its hands and other parts, is to be protected as one,
so too this entire world, though differentiated, is of the same nature in suffering and happiness. [8.91]
Although my suffering does not afflict other bodies,
nevertheless that suffering is mine and unbearable because of self-attachment. [8.92]
Likewise, although the suffering of another is not experienced by me,
nevertheless that suffering is unbearable to that being because of self-attachment. [8.93]
The suffering of others must be removed by me, because it is suffering, just like my own suffering.
Others must be helped by me, because they are sentient beings, just as I am a sentient being. [8.94]

children.text: yadā mama pareṣāṃ ca tulyameva sukhaṃ priyam /
children.translated_text: When happiness is equally dear to myself and others,

children.text: tadātmanaḥ ko viśeṣo yenātraiva sukhodyamaḥ // SBca_8.95 //
children.translated_text: what is special about the self that I should strive for happiness for it alone? [8.95]

children.text: yadā mama pareṣāṃ ca bhayaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca na priyam /
children.translated_text: When fear and suffering are equally unwelcome to myself and others,

children.text: tadātmanaḥ ko viśeṣo yattaṃ rakṣāmi netaram // SBca_8.96 //
children.translated_text: what is special about the self that I should protect it and not the other? [8.96]

children.text: tadduḥkhena na me bādhetyato yadi na rakṣyate /
children.translated_text: If I do not protect another because that suffering does not afflict me,
then the sufferings of my future body do not afflict me either — so why should I protect against them? [8.97]
'I shall be that one too' — this is a false construction,

children.text: anya eva mṛto yasmādanya eva prajāyate // SBca_8.98 //
children.translated_text: for it is one who dies and quite another who is born. [8.98]

children.text: yadi tasyaiva yadduḥkhaṃ rakṣyaṃ tasyaiva tanmatam /
children.translated_text: If one holds that only the suffering of that person is to be guarded against by that very person,

children.text: pādaduḥkhaṃ na hastasya kasmāttattena rakṣyate // SBca_8.99 //
children.translated_text: then the suffering of the foot is not the hand's — why should the hand protect it? [8.99]
If this proceeds even though unjustified, through the force of ego-grasping,
then what is unjustified, whether of self or other, should be rejected as far as possible. [8.100]
The continuum and the aggregate are false, like a row or an army.

children.text: yasya duḥkhaṃ sa nāstyasmātkasya tatsvaṃ bhaviṣyati // SBca_8.101 //
children.translated_text: The one whose suffering it is does not exist — so whose suffering will it be? [8.101]
All sufferings without exception are ownerless.
They are to be prevented simply because they are suffering. Why make any restriction here? [8.102]
If one asks why suffering should be prevented — that is undisputed by all.

children.text: vāryaṃ cetsarvamapyevaṃ na cedātmāpi sattvavat // SBca_8.103 //
children.translated_text: If it is to be prevented, then all of it should be; if not, then one's own case is the same as others'. [8.103]
If, through compassion, much suffering arises, why does one forcefully generate it?

children.text: jagadduḥkhaṃ nirūpyedaṃ kṛpāduḥkhaṃ kathaṃ bahu // SBca_8.104 //
children.translated_text: When one considers the suffering of the world, how can the suffering of compassion be great? [8.104]
If through the suffering of one, the suffering of many is removed,
then a compassionate person should produce that suffering for the sake of oneself and others. [8.105]
Therefore, <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, even knowing the king's oppression,

children.text: ātmaduḥkhaṃ na nihataṃ bahūnāṃ duḥkhināṃ vyayāt // SBca_8.106 //
children.translated_text: did not avert his own suffering, for the sake of releasing many who were suffering. [8.106]
Those whose mind-streams have been thus cultivated, who hold the suffering of others as dear as their own,
plunge into <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell) as swans plunge into a lotus grove. [8.107]
When beings are liberated, the oceans of joy that arise —

children.text: taireva nanu paryāptaṃ mokṣeṇārasikena kim // SBca_8.108 //
children.translated_text: are they not enough? What need is there for tasteless liberation? [8.108]

children.text: ataḥ parārthaṃ kṛtvāpi na mado na ca vismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even having acted for the sake of others, there is no pride and no amazement,
no expectation of the fruit of karmic ripening — out of sole thirst for the welfare of others. [8.109]
Therefore, just as I protect myself from even a small slight,
so should I cultivate a mind of protection and a mind of compassion toward others. [8.110]
Through habituation, even regarding drops of semen and blood belonging to another,
the notion 'I' arises, even though the thing is not really the self. [8.111]
In the same way, why should another's body not be grasped as one's self?

children.text: paratvaṃ tu svakāyasya sthitameva na duṣkaram // SBca_8.112 //
children.translated_text: And the otherness of one's own body is not difficult to establish. [8.112]
Having recognized the self as full of faults and others as oceans of virtues,
one should meditate on the abandonment of self-cherishing and the adoption of others. [8.113]
Just as the hands and other limbs are cherished as parts of the body,
why should embodied beings not be cherished as parts of the world? [8.114]
Just as the notion of self arises through habituation with respect to this selfless body,
why should not selfhood regarding others arise through habituation as well? [8.115]

children.text: evaṃ parārthaṃ kṛtvāpi na mado na ca vismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, even having acted for the sake of others, there is no pride and no amazement;

children.text: ātmānaṃ bhojayitvaiva phalāśā na ca jāyate // SBca_8.116 //
children.translated_text: just as when one has fed oneself, no expectation of reward arises. [8.116]
Therefore, just as you wish to protect yourself from suffering, grief, and the like,
so should a mind of protection and a mind of compassion toward the world be practiced. [8.117]
For this reason the Protector, the Lord <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, even consecrated his own name,
in order to remove the fear of timidity in people. [8.118]
One should not turn back from what is difficult, because through the power of habituation,

children.text: yasyaiva śravaṇātrāsastenaiva na vinā ratiḥ // SBca_8.119 //
children.translated_text: the very one whose name once caused fear, without that one there is no delight. [8.119]
One who wishes to quickly rescue both oneself and others
should practice the supreme secret: the exchange of self and others. [8.120]
Because of excessive attachment to the self, even from a small danger fear arises.
Who would not hate that self which is like an enemy and brings fear? [8.121]
One who, wishing to remedy illness, hunger, thirst, and the like,

children.text: pakṣimatsyamṛgān hanti paripanthaṃ ca tiṣṭhati // SBca_8.122 //
children.translated_text: kills birds, fish, and deer, and lies in ambush on the road — [8.122]
one who would even kill one's own parents for the sake of gain and honor,
and steal the property of the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels), thereby becoming fuel for <s>Avīci</s> — [8.123]
what wise person would desire, protect, or worship such a self?
Who would not view it as an enemy? And who would honor it? [8.124]

children.text: yadi dāsyāmi kiṃ bhokṣye ityātmārthe piśācatā /
children.translated_text: 'If I give, what shall I eat?' — such selfishness is the way of demons.

children.text: yadi bhokṣye kiṃ dadāmīti parārthe devarājatā // SBca_8.125 //
children.translated_text: 'If I eat, what shall I give?' — such concern for others is the way of the king of gods. [8.125]
By tormenting others for one's own sake, one is cooked in the hells and the like.

children.text: ātmānaṃ pīḍayitvā tu parārthaṃ sarvasaṃpadaḥ // SBca_8.126 //
children.translated_text: But by tormenting oneself for the sake of others, one attains all prosperity. [8.126]
Bad rebirth, lowliness, and stupidity arise from the very desire for self-advancement.
Transferring that desire to others, good rebirth, honor, and wisdom result. [8.127]
By commanding others for one's own sake, one experiences servitude and the like.
But by commanding oneself for the sake of others, one experiences lordship and the like. [8.128]

children.text: ye kecidduḥkhitā loke sarve te svasukhecchayā /
children.translated_text: All those who are miserable in the world are so because of their desire for their own happiness.

children.text: ye kecitsukhitā loke sarve te 'nyasukhecchayā // SBca_8.129 //
children.translated_text: All those who are happy in the world are so because of their desire for the happiness of others. [8.129]
But why say much? Just observe this difference:
between the fool who works for his own benefit and the sage who works for the benefit of others. [8.130]

children.text: na nāma sādhyaṃ buddhatvaṃ saṃsāre 'pi kutaḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: Without exchanging one's own happiness for the suffering of others, not only is <s>Buddhahood</s> not achieved,
but there is no happiness even in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). [8.131]

children.text: āstāṃ tāvatparo loke dṛṣṭo 'pyartho na sidhyati /
children.translated_text: Setting aside the next world, even worldly goals are not accomplished in this life,
when the servant does not do his work and the master does not pay his wages. [8.132]
Abandoning the generation of mutual happiness — a festival of seen and unseen joys —

children.text: anyonyaduḥkhanād ghoraṃ duḥkhaṃ gṛhṇanti mohitāḥ // SBca_8.133 //
children.translated_text: the deluded, through causing mutual suffering, grasp terrible suffering. [8.133]

children.text: upadravā ye ca bhavanti loke yāvanti duḥkhāni bhayāni caiva /
children.translated_text: Whatever calamities arise in the world, whatever sufferings and fears there are —

children.text: sarvāṇi tānyātmaparigraheṇa tatkiṃ mamānena parigraheṇa // SBca_8.134 //
children.translated_text: all arise from clinging to the self; what then is this clinging to me? [8.134]
Without abandoning the self, one cannot abandon suffering,

children.text: yathāgnimaparityajya dāhaṃ tyaktuṃ na śakyate // SBca_8.135 //
children.translated_text: just as without abandoning fire, one cannot abandon being burned. [8.135]
Therefore, for the sake of pacifying my own suffering and for the pacification of others' suffering,

children.text: dadāmyanyebhya ātmānaṃ parān gṛhṇāmi cātmavat // SBca_8.136 //
children.translated_text: I give myself to others and accept others as myself. [8.136]
'I am bound to others' — establish this conviction, O mind!
Having given up all for the sake of all beings, nothing else is to be thought of by you now. [8.137]
It is not right to use these eyes and the like, which belong to others, for one's own purposes.

children.text: na yuktaṃ syandituṃ svārthamanyadīyaiḥ karādibhiḥ // SBca_8.138 //
children.translated_text: It is not right to pursue one's own interests with hands and the like that belong to others. [8.138]
Therefore, having become devoted to other beings, whatever you observe in this body,
take that very thing away from it and use it for the benefit of others. [8.139]
Having established selfhood in the inferior and the like, and otherness in one's own self,

children.text: bhāvayerṣyāṃ ca mānaṃ ca nirvikalpena cetasā // SBca_8.140 //
children.translated_text: one should cultivate envy and pride with an undifferentiating mind. [8.140]

children.text: eṣa satkriyate nāhaṃ lābhī nāhamayaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: 'This one is honored, not I; this one gains, not I as he does;
he is praised, I am blamed; I am miserable, this one is happy. [8.141]

children.text: ahaṃ karomi karmāṇi tiṣṭhatyeṣa tu susthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: I perform tasks while this one simply sits at ease.

children.text: ayaṃ kila mahāṃlloke nīco 'haṃ kila nirguṇaḥ // SBca_8.142 //
children.translated_text: This one is apparently great in the world, while I am apparently lowly and without virtues. [8.142]
What can one without virtues accomplish? For everyone has a self endowed with virtues.

children.text: santi te yeṣvahaṃ nīcaḥ santi te yeṣvahaṃ varaḥ // SBca_8.143 //
children.translated_text: There are those to whom I am inferior, and there are those to whom I am superior. [8.143]
Decline in moral conduct, views, and the like is due to the power of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), not by my choice.
I should be healed as far as possible; I accept even the pain [of the cure]. [8.144]
But if I am incurable by him, why does he look down on me?

children.text: kiṃ mamaitadguṇaiḥ kṛtyamātmā tu guṇavānayam // SBca_8.145 //
children.translated_text: What use are his virtues to me? He alone is the one endowed with virtues. [8.145]
He has no compassion for people who stand in the jaws of the wild beasts of bad rebirths.
Moreover, out of pride in his qualities, he wishes to defeat the wise. [8.146]
Seeing himself as equal, for the sake of enhancing his own superiority,
even by quarrel he would secure gain and honor for himself. [8.147]

children.text: api sarvatra me loke bhaveyuḥ prakaṭā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: May my virtues become manifest to the entire world,

children.text: api nāma guṇā ye 'sya na śroṣyantyapi kecana // SBca_8.148 //
children.translated_text: and may whatever virtues he has not be heard of by anyone! [8.148]

children.text: chādyerannapi me doṣāḥ syānme pūjāsya no bhavet /
children.translated_text: Even if my faults were concealed, I might receive worship, but he would not;

children.text: sulabdhā adya me lābhāḥ pūjito 'hamayaṃ na tu // SBca_8.149 //
children.translated_text: today my gains are well-obtained — I am worshipped, but he is not! (8.149)
Let us watch with delight as he is humiliated for a long time,
made the laughingstock of all people, reviled here and there! (8.150)

children.text: asyāpi hi varākasya spardhā kila mayā saha /
children.translated_text: For this wretch, it seems, dares to compete with me!

children.text: kimasya śrutametāvat prajñā rūpaṃ kulaṃ dhanam // SBca_8.151 //
children.translated_text: Is his learning as great as mine? His wisdom, beauty, lineage, or wealth? (8.151)
Thus, hearing my own virtues being praised here and there,
with hair standing on end and thrilled with joy, I shall enjoy the festival of happiness! (8.152)
Even if he should obtain gains, they should be seized by us by force,
giving him only bare subsistence if he does our work. (8.153)
He should be cast down from happiness and always yoked to our suffering,

children.text: anena śataśaḥ sarve saṃsāravyathitā vayam // SBca_8.154 //
children.translated_text: for by this [self] we have all been made to suffer hundreds of times in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth). (8.154)
Immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) have passed while you sought your own interest;
by this great exertion, you have earned nothing but suffering. (8.155)
Therefore, at my urging, engage in this without hesitation;

children.text: drakṣyasyetadguṇān paścādbhūtaṃ hi vacanaṃ muneḥ // SBca_8.156 //
children.translated_text: you will see the benefits of this later, for the words of the Sage are true. (8.156)

children.text: abhaviṣyadidaṃ karma kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ yadi tvayā /
children.translated_text: If this practice had been performed by you before,

children.text: bauddhaṃ saṃpatsukhaṃ muktvā nābhaviṣyadiyaṃ daśā // SBca_8.157 //
children.translated_text: this condition would not have arisen, apart from the perfect bliss of <s>Buddhahood</s>. (8.157)
Therefore, just as you formed the notion of 'I' with respect to the drops of semen and blood belonging to others,
so too cultivate the same attitude toward others. (8.158)
Becoming a spy for others, whatever you see in this body,
seize it and use it for the benefit of others. (8.159)
'This one is well, the other is unwell; this one is lowly, the other is exalted;

children.text: paraḥ karotyayaṃ neti kuruṣverṣyāṃ tvamātmani // SBca_8.160 //
children.translated_text: the other acts, but this one does not' — thus cultivate jealousy toward yourself. (8.160)
Remove yourself from happiness and assign yourself to the suffering of others;

children.text: kadāyaṃ kiṃ karotīti chala(phala)masya nirūpaya // SBca_8.161 //
children.translated_text: 'When does this one do what?' — examine the deception of this [self]. (8.161)
Cast upon this one's head even the fault committed by another;

children.text: alpamapyasya doṣaṃ ca prakāśaya mahāmuneḥ // SBca_8.162 //
children.translated_text: and reveal even the slightest fault of this one before the great Sage. (8.162)
Tarnish the fame of this one by praising the superior fame of others;
and like the lowest servant, employ this one in the tasks for the welfare of beings. (8.163)
This one, full of faults, is not to be praised for some incidental virtue;

children.text: yathā kaścinna jānīyādguṇamasya tathā kuru // SBca_8.164 //
children.translated_text: act in such a way that no one may know of any virtue of this one. (8.164)
In brief, whatever harm you have done to others for your own sake,
let that harm fall upon yourself, for the sake of beings. (8.165)
No encouragement should be given to this one, by which he might become garrulous;

children.text: sthāpyo navavadhūvṛttau hrīto bhīto 'tha saṃvṛtaḥ // SBca_8.166 //
children.translated_text: he should be kept in the manner of a newly-wed bride — modest, fearful, and restrained. (8.166)

children.text: evaṃ kuruṣva tiṣṭhaivaṃ na kartavyamidaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: 'Do this! Stay just so! You must not do that!' —
thus he should be kept under control, and restrained when he transgresses. (8.167)
If, even when told thus, O mind, you will not do this,
then I shall restrain you yourself, for all faults depend upon you. (8.168)
