children.text: kva yāsyasi mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sarvadarpānnihanmi te /
children.translated_text: Where will you go? I have my eye on you! I shall crush all your arrogance.

children.text: anyo 'sau pūrvakaḥ kālastvayā yatrāsmi nāśitaḥ // SBca_8.169 //
children.translated_text: That former time is past, when you destroyed me. (8.169)

children.text: adyāpyasti mama svārtha ityāśāṃ tyaja sāṃpratam /
children.translated_text: Abandon now the hope that 'I still have my own interest';
I have sold you to others, without concern for your many sorrows. (8.170)

children.text: tvāṃ sattveṣu na dāsyāmi yadi nāma pramodataḥ /
children.translated_text: If I do not give you joyfully to beings,

children.text: tvaṃ māṃ narakapāleṣu pradāsyasi na saṃśayaḥ // SBca_8.171 //
children.translated_text: you will certainly deliver me to the guardians of the hells. (8.171)
Having been given over by you many times in this way, I have been tormented long;

children.text: nihanmi svārthaceṭaṃ tvāṃ tāni vairāṇyanusmaran // SBca_8.172 //
children.translated_text: remembering those enmities, I shall destroy you, the servant of self-interest. (8.172)
If you are fond of yourself, you should not cherish yourself;

children.text: yadyātmā rakṣitavyo 'yaṃ rakṣitavyo na yujyate // SBca_8.173 //
children.translated_text: if the self is to be protected, this [self] should not be protected. (8.173)
The more this body is cared for and pampered,

children.text: sukumārataro bhūtvā patatyeva tathā tathā // SBca_8.174 //
children.translated_text: the more delicate it becomes, and the more it declines. (8.174)
And when it has thus declined, not even this entire earth

children.text: nālaṃ pūrayituṃ vāñchāṃ tatko 'syecchāṃ kariṣyati // SBca_8.175 //
children.translated_text: can satisfy its desires — who then can fulfill its wishes? (8.175)
For one who desires the unattainable, frustration and disappointment of hope arise;

children.text: nirāśo yastu sarvatra tasya saṃpadajīrṇikā // SBca_8.176 //
children.translated_text: but for one who is free from expectations in all things, prosperity never decays. (8.176)
Therefore, no scope should be given to the body for the growth of its desires;

children.text: bhadrakaṃ nāma tadvastu yadiṣṭatvānna gṛhyate // SBca_8.177 //
children.translated_text: that thing is truly excellent which is not grasped at because it is desired. (8.177)
This [body], whose end is in ashes, motionless, moved by another,
a terrible, impure image — why do I cling to it? (8.178)

children.text: kiṃ mamānena yantreṇa jīvinā vā mṛtena vā /
children.translated_text: What use is this machine to me, whether alive or dead?

children.text: loṣṭādeḥ ko viśeṣo 'sya hāhaṃkāraṃ na naśyasi // SBca_8.179 //
children.translated_text: What difference is there between it and a clod of earth? Alas, you [ego] do not perish! (8.179)
Through partiality toward the body, suffering is uselessly acquired;
what use is hatred or affection for something equal to a piece of wood? (8.180)
Whether cared for by me in this way, or devoured by vultures and the like,

children.text: na ca sneho na ca dveṣastatra snehaṃ karomi kim // SBca_8.181 //
children.translated_text: it has neither attachment nor aversion — why then do I feel attachment to it? (8.181)

children.text: roṣo yasya khalīkārāttoṣo yasya ca pūjayā /
children.translated_text: If it itself does not know anger at being reviled or pleasure at being worshipped,

children.text: sa eva cenna jānāti śramaḥ kasya kṛtena me // SBca_8.182 //
children.translated_text: for whose sake then is my toil? (8.182)

children.text: imaṃ ye kāyamicchanti te 'pi me suhṛdaḥ kila /
children.translated_text: Those who desire this body are said to be my friends;

children.text: sarve svakāyamicchanti te 'pi kasmānna me priyāḥ // SBca_8.183 //
children.translated_text: but everyone desires their own body — why then are they not dear to me? (8.183)
Therefore, without attachment, I have given up this body for the welfare of the world;
hence, though it has many faults, it is maintained like a beast of burden for work. (8.184)
Enough, then, with worldly conduct! I shall follow the wise,
remembering the discourse on vigilance, and warding off torpor and sloth. (8.185)
Therefore, to destroy the obscurations, I shall practice <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration),
drawing the mind away from wrong paths, continuously fixing it on its proper object. (8.186)
End of the eighth chapter, called <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Meditation), in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s>.
Chapter 9, called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom).

children.text: imaṃ parikaraṃ sarvaṃ prajñārthaṃ hi munirjagau /
children.translated_text: All this preparation the Sage has taught for the sake of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom);
therefore, let one generate <s>prajñā</s>, with the desire to end suffering. (9.1)
<s>Saṃvṛti</s> (conventional truth) and <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth) — this pair of truths is accepted;
reality is beyond the reach of the intellect; the intellect is called <s>saṃvṛti</s> (the conventional). (9.2)

children.text: tatra loko dvidhā dṛṣṭo yogī prākṛtakastathā /
children.translated_text: In this regard, the world is seen to be twofold: the <s>yogin</s> (meditator) and the ordinary person;

children.text: tatra prākṛtako loko yogilokena bādhyate // SBca_9.3 //
children.translated_text: therein, the world of the ordinary person is refuted by the world of the <s>yogin</s>. (9.3)
And <s>yogins</s> too are refuted by successively higher ones,
by means of examples accepted by both parties, for the sake of the result, without further analysis. (9.4)

children.text: lokena bhāvā dṛśyante kalpyante cāpi tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: By the ordinary world, things are seen and are also conceptualized as real;

children.text: na tu māyāvadityatra vivādo yogilokayoḥ // SBca_9.5 //
children.translated_text: but that they are not like an illusion — this is the point of dispute between <s>yogins</s> and the world. (9.5)
Even direct perception of form and the like is by convention, not by valid cognition;
that convention is false, like the common acceptance of purity in what is impure and so on. (9.6)
For the purpose of leading the world, the Protector (<s>Buddha</s>) taught things;

children.text: tattvataḥ kṣaṇikā naite saṃvṛtyā cedvirudhyate // SBca_9.7 //
children.translated_text: in truth, these are not momentary — if this contradicts the conventional, [so be it]. (9.7)
There is no fault from the <s>yogin</s>'s conventional standpoint, relative to the world, for those who see reality;
otherwise there would be a contradiction with the world in the analysis of a woman as impure. (9.8)
Merit accrues from the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) who is like an illusion — just as it would if he were truly existent;

children.text: yadi māyopamaḥ sattvaḥ kiṃ punarjāyate mṛtaḥ // SBca_9.9 //
children.translated_text: if a being is like an illusion, how then is he reborn after death? (9.9)
As long as the collection of conditions exists, even illusion continues;
merely from continuity of a long series, how can a being truly exist? (9.10)
In the killing of an illusory person and the like, there is no sin, because there is no mind;
but from one endowed with the illusion of mind, both sin and merit arise. (9.11)
Because mantras and the like are incapable of producing a mind in an illusion,
illusion too is of various kinds, arising from various conditions;
no single condition has the power to produce everything. (9.12)
If one is liberated in the ultimate sense but transmigrates conventionally,

children.text: buddho 'pi saṃsaredevaṃ tataḥ kiṃ bodhicaryayā // SBca_9.13 //
children.translated_text: then even the <s>Buddha</s> would transmigrate — what then is the use of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice? (9.13)
When the conditions are not cut off, illusion too is not cut off;

children.text: pratyayānāṃ tu vicchedātsaṃvṛtyāpi na saṃbhavaḥ // SBca_9.14 //
children.translated_text: but when the conditions are severed, it does not arise even conventionally. (9.14)

children.text: pratyayānāṃ tu vicchedāt saṃvṛtyāpi na saṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when the conditions are severed, there is no arising even conventionally;

children.text: yadā na bhrāntirapyasti māyā kenopalabhyate // SBca_9.15 //
children.translated_text: when even delusion does not exist, by whom is illusion perceived? (9.15)

children.text: yadā māyaiva te nāsti tadā kimupalabhyate /
children.translated_text: When illusion itself does not exist for you, what then is perceived?

children.text: cittasyaiva sa ākāro yadyapyanyo 'sti tattvataḥ // SBca_9.16 //
children.translated_text: That is merely a form of the mind, even if it appears as something other in reality. (9.16)

children.text: cittameva yadā māyā tadā kiṃ kena dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: If the mind itself is illusion, then what is seen by what?

children.text: uktaṃ ca lokanāthena cittaṃ cittaṃ na paśyati // SBca_9.17 //
children.translated_text: And the Lord of the World has said: 'The mind does not perceive the mind.' (9.17)
Just as a sword-blade does not cut itself, so too is the mind;

children.text: ātmabhāvaṃ yathā dīpaḥ saṃprakāśayatīti cet // SBca_9.18 //
children.translated_text: if one objects, 'Just as a lamp illuminates itself' — (9.18)
the lamp is not something that is illuminated, since it is not covered by darkness;
blue, unlike a crystal, does not depend on something else for its blueness. (9.19)
Similarly, something is seen that depends on something else, and something that does not depend;
what is not blue does not make itself blue, just as the cause of blue is observed [to be external]. (9.20)
For who would make blue itself blue by itself?
What is not blue does not make itself blue by itself. (9.21)

children.text: dīpaḥ prakāśata iti jñātvā jñānena kathyate /
children.translated_text: 'The lamp illuminates' — this is said having been known through knowledge;

children.text: buddhiḥ prakāśata iti jñātvedaṃ kena kathyate // SBca_9.22 //
children.translated_text: 'The mind illuminates' — this being known, by what is it said? (9.22)

children.text: prakāśā vāprakāśā vā yadā dṛṣṭā na kenacit /
children.translated_text: Whether luminous or not luminous, when it is seen by no one,
like the grace of a barren woman's daughter, it is spoken of in vain. (9.23)
If there is no self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>), how is consciousness remembered?
Memory arises from the connection with another's experience, like the poison of a rat. (9.24)
It is because, when conjoined with other conditions, the self illuminates;
a pot seen by the application of magical ointment does not thereby become the ointment. (9.25)

children.text: yathā dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ jñātaṃ naiveha pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: What is seen, heard, and known is not denied here;
rather, what is to be rejected here is the conceptual construction that it is real, which is the cause of suffering. (9.26)
If illusion is not other than the mind, it is also not imagined as non-different;

children.text: vastu cetsā kathaṃ nānyānanyā cennāsti vastutaḥ // SBca_9.27 //
children.translated_text: if it is a real thing, how is it not other? And if it is non-different, it does not truly exist. (9.27)

children.text: asatyapi yathā māyā dṛśyā draṣṭṛ tathā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as illusion is perceived even though unreal, so too is the mind, the perceiver;
if <s>saṃsāra</s> rests upon a real basis, it would be like space. (9.28)
How can something non-existent have the capacity for action by resting on a real basis?
Your mind finds itself alone, accompanied by nothing real. (9.29)

children.text: grāhyamuktaṃ yadā cittaṃ tadā sarve tathāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the mind is freed from what is to be grasped, then all are <s>Tathāgatas</s>;

children.text: evaṃ ca ko guṇo labdhaścittamātre 'pi kalpite // SBca_9.30 //
children.translated_text: and what benefit is gained even if 'mind-only' is conceived? (9.30)
Even when one knows the illusion-like nature [of things], how are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) removed?
For even the creator of an illusory woman can develop desire for her. (9.31)
Indeed, the creator's habitual tendency toward affliction regarding the objects of knowledge is not abandoned;
therefore, at the time of perceiving that [illusion], his habitual tendency toward <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is weak. (9.32)
Through cultivating the habitual tendency toward <s>śūnyatā</s>, the habitual tendency toward real existence diminishes;
and through habituating to 'nothing whatsoever exists,' even that [tendency toward emptiness] is later abandoned. (9.33)

children.text: yadā na labhyate bhāvo yo nāstīti prakalpyate /
children.translated_text: When no entity is found that is conceptualized as 'non-existent,'

children.text: tadā nirāśrayo 'bhāvaḥ kathaṃ tiṣṭhenmateḥ puraḥ // SBca_9.34 //
children.translated_text: then how can non-existence, being without basis, remain before the mind? (9.34)

children.text: yadā na bhāvo nābhāvo mateḥ saṃtiṣṭhate puraḥ /
children.translated_text: When neither existence nor non-existence remains before the mind,
then, having no other course, being without support, the mind is pacified. (9.35)
Just as a wish-fulfilling gem and a wish-fulfilling tree fulfill desires,
so too is the image of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) seen, through the aspirations and vows of those to be guided. (9.36)
Just as a <s>gāruḍika</s> (snake-charm master), having consecrated a pillar, passes away,
that pillar, even long after his death, still neutralizes poisons and the like. // BCA 9.37 //
So too the pillar of the <s>Jina</s>, consecrated in accordance with the practice of awakening,
accomplishes all purposes even after the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // BCA 9.38 //

children.text: acittake kṛtā pūjā kathaṃ phalavatī bhavet /
children.translated_text: How could worship offered to one without mind bear fruit?

children.text: tulyaiva paṭhyate yasmāttiṣṭhato nirvṛtasya ca // SBca_9.39 //
children.translated_text: Because it is taught that [the merit] is equal whether [the Buddha] is present or has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // BCA 9.39 //

children.text: āgamācca phalaṃ tatra saṃvṛtyā tattvato 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: And according to scripture, there is fruit in that case, whether conventionally or in ultimate truth —

children.text: satyabuddhe kṛtā pūjā saphaleti kathaṃ yathā // SBca_9.40 //
children.translated_text: just as worship offered to a real <s>Buddha</s> is said to be fruitful — how [could it be otherwise]? // BCA 9.40 //
[Objection:] Liberation comes from seeing the [four noble] truths; what is the use of seeing <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)?

children.text: na vinānena mārgeṇa bodhirityāgamo yataḥ // SBca_9.41 //
children.translated_text: Because scripture states that there is no <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) without this path. // BCA 9.41 //
[Objection:] But the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is not established [as authentic] — how is your scripture established?
Because it is established for both [of us]; [and if you say] it was not established for you from the beginning, // BCA 9.42 //

children.text: yatpratyayā ca tatrāsthā mahāyāne 'pi tāṃ kuru /
children.translated_text: then whatever grounds give you confidence in your own [scripture], apply the same to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>;
if something is true merely because two parties accept it, then the <s>Vedas</s> and such would also be true. // BCA 9.43 //
[Objection:] The <s>Mahāyāna</s> is disputed! — [Reply:] Then abandon your own scripture [too],
since it is disputed by non-Buddhists, and other scriptures [are disputed] by your own [schools] and others. // BCA 9.44 //
The teaching has <s>bhikṣu</s> ordination as its root, and that very <s>bhikṣu</s> status is on uncertain ground;
for those whose minds have an object of grasping, even <s>nirvāṇa</s> is on uncertain ground. // BCA 9.45 //
[Objection:] If liberation comes from the abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), it should occur immediately after [their removal].

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ ca teṣu sāmarthyaṃ niṣkleśasyāpi karmaṇaḥ // SBca_9.46 //
children.translated_text: Yet one can see in those [arhats] the power of action even without afflictions. // BCA 9.46 //
[Response:] Granted, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) as <s>upādāna</s> (grasping) may not exist [in them] — so it may be maintained —

children.text: kimakliṣṭāpi tṛṣṇaiṣāṃ nāsti saṃmohavat satī // SBca_9.47 //
children.translated_text: but why should there not be unafflicted <s>tṛṣṇā</s> in them, existing as it does like <s>saṃmoha</s> (delusion)? // BCA 9.47 //
<s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), and <s>vedanā</s> exists in them;

children.text: sālambanena cittena sthātavyaṃ yatra tatra vā // SBca_9.48 //
children.translated_text: a mind that has an object of support must abide somewhere or other. // BCA 9.48 //
Without <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the mind is bound and arises again,
as in the <s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s> (attainment of non-perception) — therefore one should cultivate <s>śūnyatā</s>. // BCA 9.49 //
[Objection:] If whatever statement is found in a <s>sūtra</s> is accepted as spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: mahāyānaṃ bhavatsūtraiḥ prāyastulyaṃ na kiṃ matam // SBca_9.50 //
children.translated_text: then why is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, which is for the most part similar to your <s>sūtras</s>, not accepted? // BCA 9.50 //
If the whole [collection] is faulty because of one [text] that is not accepted,

children.text: ekena sūtratulyena kiṃ na sarvaṃ jinoditam // SBca_9.51 //
children.translated_text: then why is not everything spoken by the <s>Jina</s> [accepted] because of one [text] that agrees with the <s>sūtras</s>? // BCA 9.51 //
The teachings that could not be fathomed even by those headed by <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> —
who will declare them unacceptable merely because you have not understood them? // BCA 9.52 //
Remaining in <s>saṃsāra</s> is accomplished for the sake of liberation from suffering, through attachment and compassion;

children.text: mohena duḥkhināmarthe śūnyatāyā idaṃ phalam // SBca_9.53 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of those afflicted by delusion — this is the fruit of <s>śūnyatā</s>. // BCA 9.53 //
Thus, no objection against the position of <s>śūnyatā</s> is tenable;
therefore, without any doubt, one should meditate on <s>śūnyatā</s>. // BCA 9.54 //
<s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is the antidote to the darkness of the obscurations of <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions) and <s>jñeya</s> (cognitive [obscurations]);

children.text: śīghraṃ sarvajñatākāmo na bhāvayati tāṃ katham // SBca_9.55 //
children.translated_text: how can one who desires <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) swiftly not cultivate it? // BCA 9.55 //
Let fear arise toward that which produces suffering!

children.text: śūnyatā duḥkhaśamanī tataḥ kiṃ jāyate bhayam // SBca_9.56 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śūnyatā</s> pacifies suffering — so why should fear arise from it? // BCA 9.56 //

children.text: yatastato vāstu bhayaṃ yadyahaṃ nāma kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: If there were something called 'I,' fear could come from anywhere;

children.text: ahameva ca kiṃciccedbhayaṃ kasya bhaviṣyati // SBca_9.57 //
children.translated_text: but if I am nothing at all, whose fear could there be? // BCA 9.57 //
I am not teeth, hair, or nails; I am not bone, nor am I blood;

children.text: na siṃghāṇaṃ na ca śleṣmā na pūyaṃ lasikāpi vā // SBca_9.58 //
children.translated_text: I am not mucus, nor phlegm, nor pus, nor lymph; // BCA 9.58 //

children.text: nāhaṃ vasā na ca svedo na medo 'strāṇi nāpyaham /
children.translated_text: I am not fat, nor sweat, nor grease; the viscera are also not me;

children.text: na cāhamantranirguṇḍī gūthamūtramahaṃ na ca // SBca_9.59 //
children.translated_text: nor am I the intestinal cavity and entrails; I am not excrement or urine. // BCA 9.59 //

children.text: nāhaṃ māṃsaṃ na ca snāyu noṣmā vāyurahaṃ na ca /
children.translated_text: I am not flesh, nor sinew; I am not heat or breath;

children.text: na ca cchidrāṇyahaṃ nāpi ṣaḍ vijñānāni sarvathā // SBca_9.60 //
children.translated_text: nor am I the [bodily] apertures, nor in any way the six <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses). // BCA 9.60 //

children.text: śabdajñānaṃ yadi tadā śabdo gṛhyeta sarvadā /
children.translated_text: If the cognition of sound [were permanent], then sound would be apprehended at all times;

children.text: jñeyaṃ vinā tu kiṃ vetti yena jñānaṃ nirucyate // SBca_9.61 //
children.translated_text: but without a knowable object, what does it know, by virtue of which it is called 'cognition'? // BCA 9.61 //

children.text: ajānānaṃ yadi jñānaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ jñānaṃ prasajyate /
children.translated_text: If that which does not cognize is [called] cognition, then a piece of wood would absurdly be cognition;
therefore, it is certain that there is no cognition when a knowable object is not present. // BCA 9.62 //

children.text: tadeva rūpaṃ jānāti tadā kiṃ na śṛṇotyapi /
children.translated_text: If that very [cognition] cognizes form, then why does it not also hear [at the same time]?
[Reply:] Because sound is not present. — [Response:] Then the cognition of that [sound] is also nonexistent. // BCA 9.63 //
How could that which has the nature of apprehending sound be the apprehension of form?

children.text: ekaḥ pitā ca putraśca kalpyate na tu tattvataḥ // SBca_9.64 //
children.translated_text: One [person] may be designated as both father and son, but that is not ultimately real. // BCA 9.64 //

children.text: sattvaṃ rajastamo vāpi na putro na pitā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: For <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are neither son nor father;
and that [consciousness] is not seen to have a nature connected with the apprehension of sound. // BCA 9.65 //
If it is the same [entity] appearing in another form, like an actor, then it too is impermanent;
and if it is the very same thing yet with a different nature, then such a unity is unprecedented. // BCA 9.66 //
If the other form is unreal, then let its intrinsic nature be stated;
if it is [said to be] the nature of cognition, then it follows that all persons would be one. // BCA 9.67 //
And [there would be] unity of the conscious and the unconscious, since both equally have existence;

children.text: viśeṣaśca yadā mithyā kaḥ sādṛśyāśrayastadā // SBca_9.68 //
children.translated_text: when the differentiating feature is false, what then could serve as the basis for [their] similarity? // BCA 9.68 //
And I am not something unconscious, because [I would then be] devoid of consciousness like a cloth and such;
but if [the self] is a knower through conjunction with consciousness, it follows that the unknowing [self] has perished. // BCA 9.69 //
If, however, the <s>ātman</s> (self) is entirely unchanging, what has consciousness done to it?
Thus, empty space — unknowing and inert — would equally qualify as the <s>ātman</s>. // BCA 9.70 //
[Objection:] Without a self, the connection between action and its fruit would not be logical,

children.text: karma kṛtvā vinaṣṭe hi phalaṃ kasya bhaviṣyati // SBca_9.71 //
children.translated_text: for if an action perishes once it is done, to whom will the fruit belong? // BCA 9.71 //
Since it is established for both of us that action and fruit have different bases,

children.text: nirvyāpāraśca tatrātmetyatra vādo vṛthā nanu // SBca_9.72 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>ātman</s> is without any role in this — is not this dispute [about the self] pointless? // BCA 9.72 //
[Objection:] 'One endowed with a cause is connected with the fruit' — this is not [logically] possible [without a self].
[Reply:] It is taught that the agent and the experiencer [are designated] in dependence on the unity of the <s>saṃtāna</s> (continuum). // BCA 9.73 //

children.text: atītānāgataṃ cittaṃ nāhaṃ taddhi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: The past and future mind is not the 'I,' for that does not [presently] exist;
Furthermore, "I am the mind that has arisen" — but when this [mind] has perished, "I" no longer exist. (SBca 9.74)
Just as a plantain trunk, when taken apart piece by piece, is found to be nothing at all,
so too this "I," when sought through analysis, is found to be unreal. (SBca 9.75)

children.text: yadi sattvo na vidyeta kasyopari kṛpeti cet /
children.translated_text: If no <s>sattva</s> (being) exists, toward whom is compassion directed? — one may ask.
[It is directed toward] that which is imagined through the delusion accepted for the sake of accomplishing the goal. (SBca 9.76)

children.text: kāryaṃ kasya na cetsattvaḥ satyamīhā tu mohataḥ /
children.translated_text: Whose goal is it, if there is no being? True, the striving is due to delusion,

children.text: duḥkhavyupaśamārthaṃ tu kāryamoho na vāryate // SBca_9.77 //
children.translated_text: but for the purpose of the cessation of suffering, the delusion regarding the goal is not to be prevented. (SBca 9.77)
The sense of "I" (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) is the cause of suffering, and it increases through the delusion of a self;

children.text: tato 'pi na nivartyaścet varaṃ nairātmyabhāvanā // SBca_9.78 //
children.translated_text: if even that cannot be turned back, it is better to cultivate the meditation on selflessness (<s>nairātmya-bhāvanā</s>). (SBca 9.78)

children.text: kāyo na pādau na jaṅghā norū kāyaḥ kaṭirna ca /
children.translated_text: The body is not the feet, nor the shanks, nor the thighs, nor the hips,

children.text: nodaraṃ nāpyayaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ noro bāhū na cāpi saḥ // SBca_9.79 //
children.translated_text: nor the abdomen, nor the back, nor the chest, nor the arms; (SBca 9.79)

children.text: na hastau nāpyayaṃ pārśvau na kakṣau nāṃsalakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: it is not the hands, nor the sides, nor the armpits, nor characterized by the shoulders,

children.text: na grīvā na śiraḥ kāyaḥ kāyo 'tra kataraḥ punaḥ // SBca_9.80 //
children.translated_text: nor the neck, nor the head — then what is the body among these? (SBca 9.80)
If the body exists in all [its parts] partially,

children.text: aṃśā aṃśeṣu vartante sa ca kutra svayaṃ sthitaḥ // SBca_9.81 //
children.translated_text: the parts [themselves] exist in [their own] parts — so where does the body itself abide? (SBca 9.81)
And if the body were to exist in its entirety in all [parts] such as the hands and so forth,
then there would be as many bodies as there are hands and other [parts]. (SBca 9.82)

children.text: naivāntarna bahiḥ kāyaḥ kathaṃ kāyaḥ karādiṣu /
children.translated_text: The body is neither inside nor outside [the parts]; how then does it exist in the hands and so forth?

children.text: karādibhyaḥ pṛthaṅ nāsti kathaṃ nu khalu vidyate // SBca_9.83 //
children.translated_text: It is not separate from the hands and other [parts] — so how indeed can it be found? (SBca 9.83)
Therefore the body does not [truly] exist; but due to delusion, there is a notion of "body" with respect to the hands and so forth,
due to a particular configuration — like the notion of a person with respect to a post. (SBca 9.84)
As long as the assemblage of conditions persists, so long does the body appear as a person;

children.text: evaṃ karādau sā yāvattāvatkāyo 'tra dṛśyate // SBca_9.85 //
children.translated_text: likewise, as long as [the assemblage persists] in the hands and so forth, the body is seen therein. (SBca 9.85)
In the same way, since the foot is a collection of toes, which [among them] would be the foot?
And since each toe is a collection of joints, each joint too [can be divided] by the division of its own parts. (SBca 9.86)
The parts too [can be divided] by the division into atoms, and the atom itself [can be divided] by the division into directional quarters;
the directional quarter, being partless, is [like] space — therefore the atom does not [ultimately] exist. (SBca 9.87)

children.text: evaṃ svapnopame rūpe ko rajyeta vicārakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, what discerning person would be attached to form, which is like a dream?

children.text: kāyaścaivaṃ yadā nāsti tadā kā strī pumāṃśca kaḥ // SBca_9.88 //
children.translated_text: When the body is thus [found to be] nonexistent, then what is a woman, and what is a man? (SBca 9.88)

children.text: yadyasti duḥkhaṃ tattvena prahṛṣṭān kiṃ na bādhate /
children.translated_text: If suffering exists in reality, why does it not afflict those who are joyful?

children.text: śokādyārtāya mṛṣṭādi sukhaṃ cetkiṃ na rocate // SBca_9.89 //
children.translated_text: And if delicious food and the like are [truly] pleasant, why do they not delight one afflicted by grief and so forth? (SBca 9.89)
If it is not experienced because it is overpowered by something stronger,

children.text: vedanātvaṃ kathaṃ tasya yasya nānubhavātmatā // SBca_9.90 //
children.translated_text: how can that be a <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) whose very nature is not being experienced? (SBca 9.90)

children.text: asti sūkṣmatayā duḥkhaṃ sthaulyaṃ tasya hṛtaṃ nanu /
children.translated_text: "Suffering exists in a subtle form, [only] its gross [manifestation] has been removed" — is that not so?
If that [subtle suffering] is merely another form of contentment, then it too is [merely] a subtle [form of pleasure]. (SBca 9.91)
If suffering does not arise due to the arising of contrary conditions,
does it not follow that what is called "feeling" is [merely] an attachment to a mental construction? (SBca 9.92)
For this very reason, this analysis is cultivated as the antidote to that [attachment];
for <s>yogins</s> feed on <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption) born from the field of conceptual thought. (SBca 9.93)
If there is a gap between the sense faculty and its object, how can there be contact between the two?
And if there is no gap [between them], they would be one — so what would come into contact with what? (SBca 9.94)
One atom cannot penetrate another, for [an atom] is without [internal] space and is equal [in size to any other];

children.text: apraveśe na miśratvamamiśratve na saṃgatiḥ // SBca_9.95 //
children.translated_text: without penetration there is no mixing, and without mixing there is no contact. (SBca 9.95)
And how indeed can there be contact with something that is partless?

children.text: saṃsarge ca niraṃśatvaṃ yadi dṛṣṭaṃ nidarśaya // SBca_9.96 //
children.translated_text: If partlessness is observed [even] in contact, show an example of that! (SBca 9.96)
For consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), being immaterial, contact is simply not possible;
nor [is it possible] for a collection, since it too is not a [real] entity, as was previously analyzed. (SBca 9.97)
Thus, when contact does not exist, from what does <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) arise?

children.text: kimarthamayamāyāsaḥ bādhā kasya kuto bhavet // SBca_9.98 //
children.translated_text: For what purpose is this exertion? Whose affliction could arise, and from what? (SBca 9.98)

children.text: yadā na vedakaḥ kaścidvedanā ca na vidyate /
children.translated_text: When there is no experiencer and <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) does not [truly] exist,

children.text: tadāvasthāmimāṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛṣṇe kiṃ na vidīryase // SBca_9.99 //
children.translated_text: then, O <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), seeing this situation, why do you not fall apart? (SBca 9.99)
That which is seen and touched has a nature like a dream or an illusion;
<s>vedanā</s> (feeling), being co-arisen with the mind, is therefore not perceived [as separate from it]. (SBca 9.100)
What arises earlier or later is remembered but not [directly] experienced;
it does not experience itself, nor is it experienced by another. (SBca 9.101)

children.text: na cāsti vedakaḥ kaścidvedanāto na tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no experiencer whatsoever; therefore <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) does not exist in reality.

children.text: nirātmake kalāpe 'smin ka evaṃ bādhyate 'nayā // SBca_9.102 //
children.translated_text: In this selfless aggregate, who then is afflicted by it? (SBca 9.102)

children.text: nendriyeṣu na rūpādau nāntarāle manaḥ sthitam /
children.translated_text: The mind is not located in the sense faculties, nor in form and other [sense objects], nor in between;
the mind (<s>citta</s>) is found neither inside nor outside, nor anywhere else either. (SBca 9.103)

children.text: yanna kāye na cānyatra na miśraṃ na pṛthak kvacit /
children.translated_text: That which is not in the body, nor elsewhere, neither mixed [with the body] nor separate from it anywhere —

children.text: tanna kiṃcidataḥ sattvāḥ prakṛtyā parinirvṛtāḥ // SBca_9.104 //
children.translated_text: that is nothing at all; therefore beings are by nature in <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (complete cessation). (SBca 9.104)
If cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) exists prior to the knowable object, what does it apprehend in order to arise?

children.text: jñeyena saha cejjñānaṃ kimālambyāsya saṃbhavaḥ // SBca_9.105 //
children.translated_text: If cognition arises together with the knowable object, [again] what does it apprehend in order to arise? (SBca 9.105)

children.text: atha jñeyādbhavet paścāt tadā jñānaṃ kuto bhavet /
children.translated_text: And if [cognition] arises after the knowable object, then from what would cognition arise?
In this way, the origination of all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be established. (SBca 9.106)
If this is so, then conventional reality (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) does not exist — so from where do the two truths come?

children.text: atha sāpyanyasaṃvṛtyā syātsattvo nirvṛtaḥ kutaḥ // SBca_9.107 //
children.translated_text: Or if [conventional reality] exists through another's convention, how could a being attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>? (SBca 9.107)
That [conventional reality] is a conceptual construction of another's mind; by one's own convention, it does not exist.

children.text: sa paścānniyataḥ so 'sti na cennāstyeva saṃvṛtiḥ // SBca_9.108 //
children.translated_text: If it is subsequently established, then it exists; if not, then convention itself does not exist. (SBca 9.108)
The conceptualizer and the conceptualized — these two are mutually dependent;
all analysis is expressed in dependence upon what is commonly accepted. (SBca 9.109)
But when the analysis itself is analyzed by [further] analysis,
then there is an infinite regress, because that analysis too [would need to be] analyzed. (SBca 9.110)
When the object of analysis has been analyzed, the analysis has no further basis;
because it is without basis, it does not arise — and that is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. (SBca 9.111)
But for one who holds this duality to be real, that person is in an extremely difficult position.

children.text: yadi jñeyavaśādartho jñānāstitve tu kā gatiḥ // SBca_9.112 //
children.translated_text: If the object [of knowledge] depends on the knowable, then what happens when knowledge exists? (9.112)

children.text: atha jñeyavaśājjñānaṃ jñeyāstitve tu kā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, knowledge depends on the knowable, then what happens when the knowable exists?
If both exist by mutual dependence, then neither of the two would exist. (9.113)

children.text: pitā cenna vinā putrātkutaḥ putrasya saṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: If there is no father without a son, then whence does the son arise?

children.text: putrābhāve pitā nāsti tathāsattvaṃ tayordvayoḥ // SBca_9.114 //
children.translated_text: In the absence of a son there is no father; likewise, neither of the two truly exists. (9.114)
A sprout is born from a seed, and the seed is indicated by that very [sprout];

children.text: jñeyājjñānena jātena tatsattā kiṃ na gamyate // SBca_9.115 //
children.translated_text: From knowledge born of the knowable, why is the existence of that [knowable] not ascertained? (9.115)
By a knowledge other than the sprout, it is ascertained that a seed exists;

children.text: jñānāstitvaṃ kuto jñātaṃ jñeyaṃ yattena gamyate // SBca_9.116 //
children.translated_text: From what is the existence of knowledge known, by which the knowable is ascertained? (9.116)
The world, through direct perception, observes that everything has a cause,
For the variety of lotus stalks and such arises from the variety of causes. (9.117)
By what is the variety of causes produced? By the variety of prior causes.
Why does a cause give its effect? Through the power of prior causes. (9.118)
<s>Īśvara</s> (God) is the cause of the world — tell me, who then is this <s>Īśvara</s>?

children.text: bhūtāni cedbhavatvevaṃ nāmamātre 'pi kiṃ śramaḥ // SBca_9.119 //
children.translated_text: If you say the elements, then let it be so — why toil over a mere name? (9.119)

children.text: api tvaneke 'nityāśca niśceṣṭā na ca devatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the elements are many, impermanent, inert, not divine,

children.text: laṅghyāścāśucayaścaiva kṣmādayo na sa īśvaraḥ // SBca_9.120 //
children.translated_text: Transgressed upon, and impure — earth and the rest are not that <s>Īśvara</s>. (9.120)
Space is not the Lord, being inert; nor the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), since that was refuted earlier;
And if the creatorship of the inconceivable is itself inconceivable, what can be said? (9.121)

children.text: tena kiṃ sraṣṭumiṣṭaṃ ca ātmā cet nanvasau dhruvaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is it that He wishes to create? If the <s>Ātman</s>, is not that eternal?

children.text: kṣmādisvabhāva īśaśca jñānaṃ jñeyādanādi ca // SBca_9.122 //
children.translated_text: The nature of earth and the rest is [their own]; <s>Īśvara</s> too [is eternal]; and knowledge is beginningless because of the knowable. (9.122)

children.text: karmaṇaḥ sukhaduḥkhe ca vada kiṃ tena nirmitam /
children.translated_text: Pleasure and pain arise from <s>karma</s> (action) — tell me, what was created by Him?

children.text: hetorādirna cedasti phalasyādiḥ kuto bhavet // SBca_9.123 //
children.translated_text: If the cause has no beginning, how could the effect have a beginning? (9.123)

children.text: kasmātsadā na kurute na hi so 'nyamapekṣate /
children.translated_text: Why does He not create always? For He does not depend on anything else.
Nothing else exists that is not created by Him; so on what could He depend? (9.124)
If He depends on an assemblage [of conditions], He is no longer the Lord, but merely a cause;
He cannot refrain from creating when the assemblage is present, nor create in its absence. (9.125)
If <s>Īśvara</s> creates without willing, it follows that He is subject to another;

children.text: icchannapīcchāyattaḥ syāt kurvataḥ kuta īśatā // SBca_9.126 //
children.translated_text: Even if willing, He is subject to desire — where then is the lordship of the creator? (9.126)
Those who hold atoms to be eternal and minute — they too have been refuted earlier.

children.text: sāṃkhyāḥ pradhānamicchanti nityaṃ lokasya kāraṇam // SBca_9.127 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> hold <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) to be the eternal cause of the world. (9.127)
<s>Sattva</s> (goodness), <s>Rajas</s> (passion), and <s>Tamas</s> (darkness) — these <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), when in equilibrium,
Are called <s>Pradhāna</s>; when in disequilibrium, the world is said [to arise]. (9.128)
That a single entity should have a triple nature is illogical; therefore it does not exist.

children.text: evaṃ guṇā na vidyante pratyekaṃ te 'pi hi tridhā // SBca_9.129 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>guṇas</s> do not exist, for each of them too is threefold. (9.129)
In the absence of the <s>guṇas</s>, the existence of sound and the rest is extremely remote;
And in unconscious things such as cloth, pleasure and the like are impossible. (9.130)
If things have the nature of causes [of pleasure, etc.], have not those things already been examined?

children.text: sukhādyeva ca te hetuḥ na ca tasmātpaṭādayaḥ // SBca_9.131 //
children.translated_text: Your cause is pleasure and the rest themselves, but cloth and the like do not arise from them. (9.131)
If pleasure and the rest arise from cloth and such, in their absence pleasure and the rest would be non-existent;
And the permanence of pleasure and the rest is never observed. (9.132)

children.text: satyāmeva sukhavyaktau saṃvittiḥ kiṃ na gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: If the manifestation of pleasure truly exists, why is the experience not apprehended?

children.text: tadeva sūkṣmatāṃ yāti sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca tatkatham // SBca_9.133 //
children.translated_text: If it becomes subtle — how can the same thing be both gross and subtle? (9.133)
Having abandoned grossness, it becomes subtle; the grossness and subtlety are impermanent.
Why then is the impermanence of all things not accepted in the same way? (9.134)
If grossness is not different from pleasure, the impermanence of pleasure is evident.
If you hold that what is absolutely non-existent cannot arise, because of its non-existence — (9.135)
Then the arising of the manifest from the non-existent is established even against your will.

children.text: annādo 'medhyabhakṣaḥ syāt phalaṃ hetau yadi sthitam // SBca_9.136 //
children.translated_text: If the effect resides in the cause, one who eats food would be eating excrement. (9.136)
Let one buy cotton seeds for the price of cloth and wear them!

children.text: mohāccennekṣate lokaḥ tattvajñasyāpi sā sthitiḥ // SBca_9.137 //
children.translated_text: If the world does not see this due to delusion, that condition applies to the knower of truth as well. (9.137)
Even the world has this knowledge — why then does it not see [the effect in the cause]?
If the world has no authority, then even the perception of the manifest is invalid. (9.138)
If the means of knowledge is itself not a [valid] means, then surely what is known by it is false.
Therefore, the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of things is not properly established [by your reasoning]. (9.139)
Without apprehending an imagined entity, its non-existence cannot be grasped.

children.text: tasmādbhāvo mṛṣā yo hi tasyābhāvaḥ sphuṭaṃ mṛṣā // SBca_9.140 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever entity is false, its non-existence too is clearly false. (9.140)

children.text: tasmātsvapne sute naṣṭe sa nāstīti vikalpanā /
children.translated_text: Thus, in a dream, when a son has died, the thought 'he does not exist'

children.text: tadbhāvakalpanotpādaṃ vibadhnāti mṛṣā ca sā // SBca_9.141 //
children.translated_text: Obstructs the arising of the thought of his existence — yet that [negation] too is false. (9.141)
Therefore, through such analysis, nothing exists without a cause,

children.text: na ca vyastasamasteṣu pratyayeṣu vyavasthitam // SBca_9.142 //
children.translated_text: Nor does anything abide in its conditions, whether taken singly or collectively. (9.142)

children.text: anyato nāpi cāyātaṃ na tiṣṭhati na gacchati /
children.translated_text: It has not come from elsewhere, nor does it remain, nor does it go.

children.text: māyātaḥ ko viśeṣo 'sya yanmūḍhaiḥ satyataḥ kṛtam // SBca_9.143 //
children.translated_text: What difference is there between this [reality] and an illusion, which the deluded take to be real? (9.143)
That which is produced by illusion and that which is produced by causes —

children.text: āyāti tatkutaḥ kutra yāti ceti nirūpyatām // SBca_9.144 //
children.translated_text: Let it be examined: whence does it come, and whither does it go? (9.144)
That which is seen through the proximity of another, and not in its absence —

children.text: pratibimbasame tasmin kṛtrime satyatā katham // SBca_9.145 //
children.translated_text: In that which is artificial, like a reflection, how can there be reality? (9.145)
For a thing that already exists, what need is there of a cause?
And if it does not exist, what need is there of a cause? (9.146)
Non-existence undergoes no transformation, even by hundreds of millions of causes.

children.text: tadavastha kathaṃ bhāvaḥ ko vānyo bhāvatāṃ gataḥ // SBca_9.147 //
children.translated_text: In that state, how could it become an entity? Or what else has attained the state of being? (9.147)
If there is no entity at the time of non-existence, when will the entity come into being?
For non-existence will not depart unless the entity has arisen. (9.148)
And while non-existence has not departed, there is no occasion for the entity.
Nor does the entity pass into non-existence, for that would entail a dual nature. (9.149)

children.text: evaṃ na ca nirodho 'sti na ca bhāvo 'sti sarvadā /
children.translated_text: Thus there is neither cessation nor existence at any time;
Therefore this entire world is unborn and unceased. (9.150)
The courses of existence are dream-like; upon analysis they are like the plantain tree.

children.text: nirvṛtānirvṛtānāṃ ca viśeṣo nāsti vastutaḥ // SBca_9.151 //
children.translated_text: Between those who have reached <s>nirvṛti</s> (peace) and those who have not, there is no real difference. (9.151)

children.text: evaṃ śūnyeṣu dharmeṣu kiṃ labdhaṃ kiṃ hṛtaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: When all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are thus empty, what can be gained and what can be lost?

children.text: satkṛtaḥ paribhūto vā kena kaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati // SBca_9.152 //
children.translated_text: By whom can anyone be honored or humiliated? (9.152)

children.text: kutaḥ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā kiṃ priyaṃ vā kimapriyam /
children.translated_text: Whence comes pleasure or pain? What is pleasant and what is unpleasant?

children.text: kā tṛṣṇā kutra sā tṛṣṇā mṛgyamāṇā svabhāvataḥ // SBca_9.153 //
children.translated_text: What is <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), and where is that craving when sought in its own nature? (9.153)

children.text: vicāre jīvalokaḥ kaḥ ko nāmātra mariṣyati /
children.translated_text: Upon examination, what is this world of the living? Who truly will die here?

children.text: ko bhaviṣyati ko bhūtaḥ ko bandhuḥ kasya kaḥ suhṛt // SBca_9.154 //
children.translated_text: Who will come into being? Who has been? Who is a relative, and who is whose friend? (9.154)
May those like me comprehend that everything is like space!
They become angry and delighted by causes of quarrel and celebration; (9.155)
Through grief, fatigue, despair, and mutual cutting and breaking,
Those who desire their own happiness live with great difficulty through sinful deeds. (9.156)
Having died, they fall into evil realms of long and intense suffering,

children.text: āgatyāgatya sugatiṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā sukhocitāḥ // SBca_9.157 //
children.translated_text: Coming again and again to fortunate states, becoming accustomed to pleasure again and again. (9.157)
In existence there are many precipices, and therein such absence of truth;
There is mutual conflict therein — such reality cannot exist. (9.158)
There are incomparable, intense, and infinite oceans of suffering;
There too, strength is meager; there too, the span of life is short. (9.159)
There too, in the activities of living and health, in hunger, weariness, and exhaustion,
In sleep, in calamities, and in fruitless association with the foolish — (9.160)
Life passes swiftly and in vain; discernment is hard to find therein.
There too, how could one find the means to ward off habitual distraction? (9.161)
There too, <s>Māra</s> (the Evil One) strives to cast beings into the great abyss;
There, because of the abundance of false paths, doubt is hard to overcome. (9.162)
Moreover, the momentary opportunity is rare to obtain; the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is exceedingly rare;
The flood of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) is hard to restrain — alas, what a chain of suffering! (9.163)
Alas, most pitiable indeed are these beings caught in the flood of suffering,
Who do not see their own miserable state, even though they are so badly off! (9.164)
Just as someone who bathes again and again might enter fire repeatedly,
They consider themselves to be well-off, even though they are so badly off! (9.165)
Of those who live as if free from old age and death,
Terrible calamities will come, with death at the fore. (9.166)
When shall I bring peace to those tormented by the fire of suffering,
With my own means of happiness, born from clouds of merit? (9.167)
When shall I teach <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) to those who hold the view of apprehension [of inherent existence],
Through the convention of non-apprehension, with devotion to the accumulation of merit? (9.168)
Thus ends the ninth chapter, on the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>), in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.
Chapter 10: The Dedication of Merit (<s>Pariṇāmanā</s>)
Whatever merit has arisen from my contemplation of the <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> —

children.text: tena sarve janāḥ santu bodhicaryāvibhūṣaṇāḥ // SBca_10.1 //
children.translated_text: By that, may all beings become adorned with the conduct of awakening! (10.1)
In all directions, as many as there are beings afflicted with suffering of body and mind,
May they attain, through my merits, oceans of happiness and joy! (10.2)
Throughout <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence), may the loss of their happiness never occur;
May the world attain the unceasing happiness of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>! (10.3)
In whatever hells exist in the world-realms,
May the beings therein rejoice with the joys and delights of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Pure Land)! (10.4)
May those afflicted by cold find warmth; may those afflicted by heat be cooled
By oceans of water born from the great clouds of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! (10.5)
May the Sword-Leaf Forest become for them radiant as the <s>Nandana</s> grove;
May the <s>kūṭaśālmali</s> (thorny silk-cotton) trees become wish-fulfilling trees! (10.6)
With lakes lovely and charming with the clamor of <s>kādamba</s> geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, and swans,
Fragrant with abundant lotuses in full bloom, may the regions of hell become delightful! (10.7)

children.text: so 'ṅgārarāśirmaṇirāśirastu taptā ca bhūḥ sphāṭikakuṭṭimaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: May that heap of embers become a heap of jewels; may the burning ground become a crystal pavement;
May the crushing mountains become celestial palaces of worship, filled with <s>Sugatas</s> (Buddhas)! (10.8)
May the rain of burning coals, hot stones, and weapons henceforth become a rain of flowers;

children.text: tacchastrayuddhaṃ ca paraspareṇa krīḍārthamadyāstu ca puṣpayuddham // SBca_10.9 //
children.translated_text: And may the mutual fighting with weapons henceforth become a playful battle with flowers! (10.9)
Those whose flesh has completely fallen away, whose bodies are white-boned skeletons, plunged in the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> river whose waters are like blazing fire —

children.text: mama kuśalabalena prāptadivyātmabhāvāḥ saha suravanitābhiḥ santu mandākinīsthāḥ // SBca_10.10 //
children.translated_text: By the power of my merit, may they attain divine bodies and dwell at the <s>Mandākinī</s> (heavenly Gaṅgā) in the company of celestial maidens! (10.10)

children.text: trastāḥ paśyantvakasmādiha yamapuruṣāḥ kākagṛdhrāśca ghorā dhvāntaṃ
children.translated_text: May the servants of <s>Yama</s> and the terrible crows and vultures suddenly look up in alarm, [thinking:] 'The darkness
Is dispelled on all sides — whose gentle radiance is this, generating happiness and delight?'
And looking upward, seeing blazing <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> stationed in the sky,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā prāmodyavegādvyapagataduritā yāntu tenaiva sārdham // SBca_10.11 //
children.translated_text: May they, with the rush of joy, depart free from evil, going with him! (10.11)
A rain of lotuses falls, mixed with fragrant water, and is seen extinguishing the fire of hell.

children.text: kimidamiti sukhenāhlāditānāmakasmād bhavatu kamalapāṇerdarśanaṃ nārakāṇām // SBca_10.12 //
children.translated_text: 'What is this?' — suddenly gladdened with joy, may the hell-beings behold <s>Kamalapāṇi</s> (Lotus-Handed, i.e., <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>)! (10.12)

children.text: āyātāyāta śīghraṃ bhayamapanayata bhrātaro jīvitāḥ smaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Come, come quickly! Cast off fear! Brothers, we are alive!
He has arrived among us — some radiant, fear-dispelling youth, the crowned one (<s>Cīrīkumāra</s>);
By whose power all misfortune has departed and streams of joy have arisen —'

children.text: jātaṃ saṃbodhicittaṃ sakalajanaparitrāṇamātā dayā ca // SBca_10.13 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) has been born, and compassion, the mother who protects all beings! // SBca_10.13 //
May they behold him — his lotus-feet worshipped by the diadems of hundreds of gods,
his gaze moist with compassion, upon his head a shower of abundant flower-rains,
in delightful mansions resounding with the hymns of thousands of celestial women singing his praises —

children.text: rdṛṣṭvāgre mañjughoṣaṃ bhavatu kalakalaḥ sāṃprataṃ nārakāṇām // SBca_10.14 //
children.translated_text: and upon seeing <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> before them, let there now arise a joyful clamor among the hell-beings! // SBca_10.14 //
Thus, through my merits, may those hell-beings rejoice upon beholding the clouds of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> led by <s>Samantabhadra</s>,
with rains of pleasant, cool, fragrant breezes! // SBca_10.15 //
May the intense sufferings of hell-beings be pacified, and their fears as well!
May all who dwell in the lower realms be freed from those lower realms! // SBca_10.16 //
May the fear of being devoured by one another among the animals cease!

children.text: bhavantu sukhinaḥ pretā yathottarakurau narāḥ // SBca_10.17 //
children.translated_text: May the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) become happy, like humans in <s>Uttarakuru</s> (the northern continent)! // SBca_10.17 //

children.text: saṃtarpyantāṃ pretāḥ snāpyantāṃ śītalā bhavantu sadā /
children.translated_text: May the <s>pretas</s> be satisfied, bathed, and always cooled
by the streams of milk flowing from the hand of noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! // SBca_10.18 //

children.text: andhāḥ paśyantu rūpāṇi śṛṇvantu badhirāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: May the blind see forms, and may the deaf always hear!
And may pregnant women give birth without pain, like <s>Māyādevī</s>! // SBca_10.19 //
Clothing, food, drink, garlands, sandalwood, and ornaments —
may all obtain everything their hearts desire, along with what is beneficial! // SBca_10.20 //
May the frightened become fearless, may the grief-stricken gain joy,

children.text: udvignāśca nirudvegā dhṛtimanto bhavantu ca // SBca_10.21 //
children.translated_text: may the anxious become free from anxiety, and may they become steadfast! // SBca_10.21 //
May the sick attain health, may all be freed from every bondage!

children.text: durbalā balinaḥ santu snigdhacittāḥ parasparam // SBca_10.22 //
children.translated_text: May the weak become strong, and may their hearts be affectionate toward one another! // SBca_10.22 //

children.text: sarvā diśaḥ śivāḥ santu sarveṣāṃ pathivartinām /
children.translated_text: May all directions be auspicious for all who travel the roads!

children.text: yena kāryeṇa gacchanti tadupāyena sidhyatu // SBca_10.23 //
children.translated_text: Whatever purpose they travel for, may it be accomplished by that very means! // SBca_10.23 //
May those who have embarked on voyages by boat or ship have their wishes fulfilled!

children.text: kṣemeṇa kūlamāsādya ramantāṃ saha bandhubhiḥ // SBca_10.24 //
children.translated_text: Having safely reached the shore, may they rejoice together with their kinsmen! // SBca_10.24 //
May those who have lost their way in desolate wilderness find the company of fellow travelers!
And may they travel without fatigue, free from fear of robbers, tigers, and the like! // SBca_10.25 //
For those who are asleep, intoxicated, or heedless, in the perils of illness, the forest, and so forth,
for the helpless, the young, and the old — may the deities provide protection! // SBca_10.26 //
May all be freed from every unfavorable condition, endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion,
possessed of good form and conduct, and may they always remember their former births! // SBca_10.27 //
May their treasuries be inexhaustible, like a storehouse in the sky!
Free from conflict, free from distress, may they be self-reliant in their livelihood! // SBca_10.28 //
May beings of little vigor become endowed with great vigor!
May those wretched ones who are deformed become endowed with beautiful forms! // SBca_10.29 //

children.text: yāḥ kāścana striyo loke puruṣatvaṃ vrajantu tāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever women there are in the world, may they attain manhood!

children.text: prāpnuvantūccatāṃ nīcā hatamānā bhavantu ca // SBca_10.30 //
children.translated_text: May the lowly attain high status, and may the proud be humbled! // SBca_10.30 //
By this merit of mine, may all beings without exception,

children.text: viramya sarvapāpebhyaḥ kurvantu kuśalaṃ sadā // SBca_10.31 //
children.translated_text: having renounced all evil deeds, always practice what is wholesome! // SBca_10.31 //
May they never be separated from <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), devoted to the practice of awakening,
embraced by the <s>Buddhas</s>, and free from the works of <s>Māra</s> (the Evil One)! // SBca_10.32 //
And may all those beings have immeasurable lifespans!

children.text: nityaṃ jīvantu sukhitā mṛtyuśabdo 'pi naśyatu // SBca_10.33 //
children.translated_text: May they live forever in happiness, and may even the word 'death' perish! // SBca_10.33 //
May all directions be delightful with gardens of wish-fulfilling trees,
filled with <s>Buddhas</s> and sons of <s>Buddhas</s>, enchanting with the sounds of the <s>Dharma</s>! // SBca_10.34 //
Free from pebbles and the like, even, smooth as the palm of a hand,

children.text: mṛdvī ca vaiḍūryamayī bhūmiḥ sarvatra tiṣṭhatu // SBca_10.35 //
children.translated_text: soft and made of lapis lazuli — may the earth stand thus everywhere! // SBca_10.35 //
May the great assemblies of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> sit in circles on all sides,
and by their own splendor adorn the surface of the earth! // SBca_10.36 //
From birds, from all trees, from rays of light, and from the sky itself,
may the sound of the <s>Dharma</s> be heard unceasingly by all embodied beings! // SBca_10.37 //
May they always encounter <s>Buddhas</s> and sons of <s>Buddhas</s>!
With boundless clouds of worship, may they worship the Teacher of the World! // SBca_10.38 //
May the rain-god send rain in due season, and may the harvest be abundant!

children.text: sphīto bhavatu lokaśca rājā bhavatu dhārmikaḥ // SBca_10.39 //
children.translated_text: May the world be prosperous, and may the king be righteous! // SBca_10.39 //

children.text: śaktā bhavantu cauṣadhyo mantrāḥ sidhyantu jāpinām /
children.translated_text: May medicines be potent, and may <s>mantras</s> (sacred incantations) succeed for those who recite them!
May <s>ḍākinīs</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), and others be filled with compassion! // SBca_10.40 //

children.text: mā kaścidduḥkhitaḥ sattvo mā pāpī mā ca rogitaḥ /
children.translated_text: May no being be unhappy, may none be sinful, may none be sick!

children.text: mā hīnaḥ paribhūto vā mā bhūtkaścicca durmanāḥ // SBca_10.41 //
children.translated_text: May none be despised or humbled, and may no one be despondent! // SBca_10.41 //
May the monasteries stand firm, filled with recitation and study!

children.text: nityaṃ syātsaṃghasāmagrī saṃghakāryaṃ ca sidhyatu // SBca_10.42 //
children.translated_text: May the <s>Saṃgha</s> (community) always be harmonious, and may the work of the <s>Saṃgha</s> prosper! // SBca_10.42 //
May monks attain solitude and be desirous of training!
May they meditate with focused minds, free from all distraction! // SBca_10.43 //
May nuns receive alms, free from quarrels and hardships!
And may all who have gone forth maintain unbroken moral conduct! // SBca_10.44 //
May those of poor conduct be distressed [by their faults] and always devoted to the destruction of sin!
May they attain [rebirth] in the presence of the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One), and there may their vows remain unbroken! // SBca_10.45 //
May the learned be honored, may those who beg for alms receive sustenance!
May their mindstreams be pure, and may their fame be celebrated in every direction! // SBca_10.46 //
Without enduring the sufferings of the lower realms, and without arduous practices,
may the world attain <s>Buddhahood</s> (awakening) with a single divine body! // SBca_10.47 //
May all the fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s> be worshipped by all beings in manifold ways!
May they be exceedingly happy with the inconceivable bliss of the <s>Buddha</s>! // SBca_10.48 //
May the wishes of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> for the welfare of the world be fulfilled!
Whatever those protectors intend, may that be accomplished for all beings! // SBca_10.49 //
May the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) and the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) also be happy,
always worshipped with reverence by gods, <s>asuras</s> (titans), and humans! // SBca_10.50 //
May I always attain the memory of former births and the going-forth into homelessness,
up to the <s>Pramuditā bhūmi</s> (the Joyful Stage), through the grace of <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! // SBca_10.51 //
May I sustain life with whatever seat or posture, endowed with strength!
May I attain the fullness of dwelling in solitude in all my births! // SBca_10.52 //

children.text: yadā ca draṣṭukāmaḥ syāṃ praṣṭukāmaśca kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: And whenever I wish to see or ask anything,
may I behold that very protector, Lord <s>Mañjunātha</s> (<s>Mañjuśrī</s>), without obstruction! // SBca_10.53 //
In order to accomplish the welfare of all beings throughout the ten directions to the ends of space,

children.text: yathā carati mañjuśrīḥ saiva caryā bhavenmama // SBca_10.54 //
children.translated_text: may my conduct be just as <s>Mañjuśrī</s> himself conducts [his]! // SBca_10.54 //
As long as space endures, and as long as the world endures,
so long may I endure, destroying the sufferings of the world! // SBca_10.55 //
Whatever suffering there is in the world, may all of it ripen upon me!
And through all the virtues of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, may the world be happy! // SBca_10.56 //
The sole medicine for the world's suffering, the source of all prosperity and happiness —
may the Teaching endure long, accompanied by gain and honor! // SBca_10.57 //
I bow to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, through whose grace my mind turns toward virtue!
I venerate the spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), through whose grace [that virtue] grows! // SBca_10.58 //
|| Thus ends the tenth chapter, on Dedication (<s>Pariṇāmanā</s>), in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s>. ||
|| Thus is completed the <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s>, the work of the teacher <s>Śāntideva</s>. ||
